523828|2026-03.headline: Menon Bearings FY26 consolidated PAT rose 53.41% to INR 38.25 crore; Q4 PAT up 108.55% YoY, with management guiding 20-22% EBITDA margin.
523828|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total income above INR 300 crore (up 23.16% YoY), PAT of INR 38.25 crore (up 53.41%), and EPS rising from INR 4.45 to INR 6.83. Q4 consolidated PAT grew 108.55% YoY, and the company cited Q4 EBITDA of about 25%. Management guided to 25% annual volume growth, 20-22% EBITDA margin for the next two years, and INR 500 crore revenue by FY28. Alkop (aluminium) growth was flagged as a key swing factor after a slow prior two years.

financial_highlights.value: About 1.5x; Bearings about 2x, Alkop about 1.5x, Brakes about 1x
About 25% (per analyst recap, confirmed as correct by management)

segments.name: Bi-Metal bearings
segments.commentary: Utilisation reached about 85%; new business pipeline above INR 50 crore across 28-30 customers over the current and next two years. Growth guided at about 23-25% per year. Tractors about 35% of revenue, HCV/LCV 25%, brakes-use 25%, transmission 15%, other industrial about 10%.

segments.name: Aluminium (Alkop)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up about 25% QoQ; utilisation rose from 45% to 60% and is expected to reach 90% by year-end. Installed capacity 1,450 tpa with a spare holding furnace. Management guided 29% growth for the next two years and more than INR 120 crore revenue in two years. Pipeline of about INR 30 crore from 51 new parts.

segments.name: Brakes
segments.commentary: Capacity added by about 1 lakh pieces per month. Railway registration done, but no railway revenue yet; dynamometer delivery expected by August 2026. Brakes CapEx of INR 3 crore; pipeline of about INR 10 crore over two years.

segments.name: Exports and channel mix
segments.commentary: Exports about 35% of revenue; about 80% of export orders are ex-works. US exports rose about 50% YoY. Consolidated mix: auto 75%, other 25%. Order book about 60% export and 40% domestic.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance: management said it expects to exceed INR 350 crore and estimates more than INR 360 crore.
Revenue target of INR 500 crore by FY28 at about 25% annual growth, described as optimistic and dependent on geopolitical conditions.
EBITDA margin to be sustained at 20-22% over the next two years on a conservative basis; Q4 level of about 25% was linked to export and high-volume mix.
Asset turnover to reach about 2x on a consolidated basis by FY28.
Planned CapEx of about INR 25 crore over two years for Bi-Metal, INR 7 crore for Alkop, and INR 3 crore for Brakes, mostly funded by internal accruals.
Raw material cost pass-through is quarterly and index-linked; one or two customers still to be moved to full pass-through in Q1 FY27.
capex_capacity: Bi-Metal CapEx INR 25 crore over two years; Alkop INR 7 crore; Brakes INR 3 crore; mostly internal accruals.
Alkop installed capacity 1,450 tpa, running at about 1,500 tpa output and 65% utilisation; a spare holding furnace can double capacity when needed, with another furnace expected next year.
Brakes dynamometer, a key railway qualification item, is expected by August 2026 after earlier delays from two other vendors.
Railway business expected to start from around August/end of 2026 at 5-10% of revenue initially.
demand_pricing: Order book reported at more than INR 32 crore; management expects to target about INR 190 crore in the next six months (as stated on the call).

Raw material costs (aluminium and copper) rose sharply; aluminium grade cost moved from INR 240/kg to INR 280/kg, copper about INR 1,275/kg, vs about INR 900 a year earlier. Pass-through is quarterly, index-linked.
Alkop average realisation about INR 700-750/kg against INR 200-250 value-add for competitors, per management. Alkop EBITDA margin about 20% vs 6-8% at large competitors, per management.
Export interest: European RFQs rising over the last six months; a PTFE bush opportunity for seven parts, with one sample approved, targeting about 6 lakh pieces per month.
Africa exports via Dubai halted for three months (about INR 2 crore lost), offset by about INR 6 crore of annual orders via a merchant exporter with advance payment.

qa_highlights.question: Why is interest expense high, and how will it be controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Export debtor days exceed 180, raising working capital. Management is shifting to PCFC limits (INR 6 crore drawn at about 4.7% vs about 8% earlier; INR 25 crore total limit planned) with a 2.75% export interest subvention, targeting about 4% savings on working capital limit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory from operating leverage and export mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export pipeline (over 50% of new business) carries better margins, and it expects margin improvement above 15 bps in FY27. Q4 uplift was attributed to higher capacity utilisation: Bi-Metal at 85%, Alkop up from 45% to 60%, Brakes up by 1 lakh pieces per month.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Alkop lagged, and what drives its growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed export delays and customer slowdowns from the war, tariffs and raw material inflation, with samples delayed from January to March. It expects about 29% annual growth for Alkop over the next two years and says Alkop could match Bearings' revenue contribution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin guidance and quarterly volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that EBITDA margin would likely range between 20% and 22% for the full year on a conservative basis, and that quarterly margins could move between 22% and 25% depending on export and high-volume mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance of INR 350 crore maintained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to exceed INR 350 crore and estimates more than INR 360 crore; it noted that FY26 had beaten the earlier INR 275 crore target and been revised to INR 290 crore.

risks_watch: Raw material pass-through lag: pass-through is quarterly and one or two customers are still not on full index-linked pricing, so margin can dip in the interim.
Export working capital: debtor days above 180 and about 80% of export orders still on DDP terms; Q1 FY27 receivables and interest cost need monitoring.
Alkop growth depends on order placement timing from John Deere, Taco Prestolite, Eaton, Honeywell and others. Management said orders are not yet firm.
Railway and brakes OEM entry depends on dynamometer commissioning by August 2026 and vendor registration.
Geopolitical risk: Middle East logistics congestion, Africa export halt, and possible export rerouting or customer pricing pressure.
523828|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth and margin outlook; several answers were loosely quantified and some figures were restated on the call (for example, the revenue target, the Alkop tonnage and the CapEx split). Management was evasive on order book segment split and on the reason for the dynamometer delay.
key_quotes: I again assure you that considering the present situation going forward, we will be able to maintain EBITDA more than 20% and it should be about between 20 % to 22% during next two years.
So, we are not after volumes, we are balancing both the games, you see, volumes to the certain extent, which can fetch us margins which are sustainable.
Our management, everything working together, we have exceeded the number by INR 25 crore.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin of 20-22% for FY27-FY28 on a conservative basis versus about 22% FY26 and about 25% Q4, with margin improvement above 15 bps in FY27 flagged from export mix and utilisation gains; quarterly margins could range 22-25%, and one or two customers still need full index-linked pass-through.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q4 FY27 to Q1 FY28 for Alkop second furnace; railway/brakes
rows.why: Bi-Metal utilisation at about 85% with a INR 50 crore+ pipeline, Alkop utilisation rising from 45% to 60% toward 90% by year-end with a spare furnace that can double capacity, and another Alkop furnace expected next year; INR 35 crore capex planned over two years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets 25% annual revenue growth and Alkop 29% growth, backed by a INR 32 crore order book targeting INR 190 crore in six months and Bi-Metal utilisation of 85%, though Alkop orders from John Deere, Taco Prestolite and others are not yet firm.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Bi-Metal utilisation at 85% with INR 25 crore Bi-Metal capex already stated, plus Alkop INR 7 crore and Brakes INR 3 crore, so further capex is likely as the INR 500 crore FY28 target needs capacity; the call gave no firm new board approval or date.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided above INR 350 crore and estimated above INR 360 crore, versus FY26 that beat the INR 275 crore target and was revised to INR 290 crore, suggesting a conservative base, though management calls the INR 500 crore FY28 target optimistic.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Export debtor days above 180, about 80% of export orders ex-works/DDP, Alkop orders not firm, and INR 2 crore lost from the Africa halt; the dynamometer slipped from earlier vendor delays and railway revenue depends on it by August 2026.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Railway/brakes OEM entry at 5-10% of revenue depends on dynamometer by August 2026; a PTFE bush opportunity for seven parts with one sample approved targets about 6 lakh pieces per month; Alkop pipeline of INR 30 crore from 51 new parts.

rows.label: Railway/brakes OEM entry
rows.why: Railway registration done but no revenue yet; dynamometer expected by August 2026, with railway starting at 5-10% of revenue, and brakes pipeline about INR 10 crore over two years.

rows.label: Order book ramp to INR 190 crore
rows.why: Order book above INR 32 crore with a target of about INR 190 crore in six months, but management was evasive on segment split and Alkop orders are not firm.

rows.label: PCFC shift to cut interest cost
rows.why: Shifting INR 6 crore drawn at about 4.7% from about 8% under PCFC with a INR 25 crore total limit planned and 2.75% export interest subvention, targeting about 4% savings on working capital limit, while debtor days exceed 180.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 25% growth, 20-22% margin and INR 360 crore FY27 outlook and Alkop's 90% utilisation ramp, but was evasive on order book segment split and the dynamometer delay; analysts pushed on export debtor days above 180 and interest cost.

523828|2026-06.headline: Menon Bearings Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 36.57% to INR91.79 crores and PAT 67.35%, with management reiterating INR360 crore FY27 revenue as conservative.
523828|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly sales, EBITDA, PBT and PAT for Q1 FY27, with consolidated sales of INR91.79 crores (up 36.57%) and PBT of INR18.51 crores (up 67.36%). Standalone bi-metal sales rose to INR67.06 crores (up ~40%). Growth was attributed to export and new customer wins following a June 2026 US and Canada marketing trip, plus a shift in product mix toward brakes, where EBITDA margin reached about 25%. Management said the FY27 revenue guidance of INR360 crores is conservative, and described a domestic RFQ pipeline of over INR75 crores. Several new-business timelines (Alkop US customers, railway brake approval) run into FY28 and beyond.

segments.name: Bi-metal (Menon Bearings)
segments.commentary: Q1 standalone sales INR67.06 crores; EBITDA margin around 21%+ per management. Utilisation about 80% on machinery basis; Rs 9-10 crore capex this year expected to add 25-30% capacity.

segments.name: Aluminium (Menon Alkop)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin around 21%. Utilisation 65-70%. Management targets Alkop revenue of INR100 crores this year and INR125 crores next year; quarterly run rate cited by an analyst at about INR21 crores.

segments.name: Brakes (Menon Brakes)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin about 25% in Q1, up from about 12-14% previously, attributed mainly to product mix and lower Dubai/Africa export volumes. Utilisation 65-70%. Railway dynamometer expected by end-August 2026, with testing rig running by September-end.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR360 crores, which management called conservative; mid-20% growth possible, with internal target of INR500 crores reached sooner than 2030.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to sustain around 20-21% over time; management said brake margin of 25% may fall next quarter.
Additional business of INR65-75 crores for current and next FY, subject to good monsoon and no worsening geopolitics.
Domestic RFQ list above INR75 crores; at 75-80% conversion, management expects more than INR60 crores of additional business within this year and next.
Export share of revenue expected to rise to about 37% next year; FY27 export share was described as around 24-30% historically.
capex_capacity: Bi-metal: Rs 9-10 crores capex this FY to add roughly 25-30% capacity; expected to yield revenue above INR25 crores. Peak bi-metal revenue on current capacity cited above INR400 crores.
Alkop: about INR4 crores capex this year; 65,000 sq ft new building with 25,000-30,000 sq ft still available for machines already ordered.

Brakes: dynamometer under construction, expected by end-August 2026; railway approval, then testing for about one year. Railway business INR5-6 crores in year one, scaling to INR25-30 crores within two years.

Management says current infrastructure supports up to about INR500 crores revenue; about seven acres of empty land at the aluminium plant. New land for bi-metal being evaluated for the next two years.
Future capex asset turn about 2.5x; capex to be funded through internal accruals, no fresh loans for bi-metal and Alkop.
demand_pricing: Alkop: RFQs, NDAs and vendor profiling from Magna, Allison Transmission, Linamar-type US customers after June 2026 US and Canada trip; management cites INR50-60 crores potential, realisation expected in 9-12 months (targeting 6-7 months). Samples by 2027.
Bi-metal engine bearing: began receiving RFQs and orders from US customers; supply expected from Q3-Q4 FY27.

Africa: bearings, bushes, washers estimated at about INR9 crores; brake linings INR6-7 crores; existing Dubai distributor business INR7-8 crores per year. Merchant export orders were stalled for three months due to Strait of Hormuz disruption; new orders require 100% advance for the initial six months.
Aluminium realisation above INR900 per unit now, up from about INR700 when aluminium was about INR250-300/kg; aluminium rates now INR340-370.
Competition: China pressure in Dubai and Africa for brake linings; company keeps minimum margins on these exports.
EV share in Alkop about 4-5% now, targeting about 8% within two years; Tata EV parts moved to a 1,600-ton press.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue expected from brakes in FY27 and railway timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Dynamometer by end-August; RDSO vendor code registered; railway audit then approval; INR5-6 crores in year one, INR25-30 crores within two years. Management declined to give precise OEM numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Africa revenue potential and payment terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Bearings, bushes, washers about INR9 crores; brake linings INR6-7 crores; Dubai distributor INR7-8 crores a year. Aluminium excluded; new merchant exporters require 100% advance for initial six months.

qa_highlights.question: Alkop business visibility and FY28 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets INR100 crores this year and INR125 crores next year. US RFQs and NDAs received; new business takes 9-12 months to realise. Europe visit planned for September.

qa_highlights.question: Bi-metal capacity beyond current utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation about 85-87% by one measure, about 80% by management's machinery-based count. Capex of INR9-10 crores adds 25-30% capacity; third shift available.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 INR360 crore guidance conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called INR360 crores conservative, declined to raise the number, and said Q4 would be better.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of margins with raw-material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated margin 20-21% expected over time; brake margin of 25% driven by product mix and may fall next quarter.

risks_watch: Brake margin of 25% is product-mix driven and may fall; management expects consolidated margins of 20-21%.
Monsoon and geopolitical conditions (Strait of Hormuz, war) cited as conditions for the INR65-75 crore additional business.
Railway brake approval timeline is uncertain: testing could run about one year after registration, and orders are unknown.
Raw-material and consumables cost volatility: aluminium up sharply; carbide tools up about 300% per management.
Dependence on export: about 60% of order book is export; US concentration; tariff impact noted earlier.
523828|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth and pipeline, with repeated optimism about FY27 and beyond. Evasive on hard numbers for brakes, Alkop realisation timing and exact guidance changes, which were left as "conservative" without a revised figure.
key_quotes: we have recorded highest-ever sales, highest -ever EBITDA, highest -ever profit before tax and PAT in the history of the company for this quarter.

The total potential of additional business for the current and next financial year is expected to be around INR65 crores to INR75 crores, subject to good monsoon and geopolitical situation doesn't worsen further.
we are 100% sure that we will get additional business from them and maybe there will be substantial and significant increase in the volumes of Menon Brakes in the next year.
So, INR360 crores, I would say is a conservative figure and we will stick to that.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 20-21% sustained, but brake margin jumped to about 25% (from 12-14%) on mix and management says it may fall next quarter, so no clear expansion beyond current levels.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bi-metal Rs 9-10 crore capex under way to add 25-30% capacity (about 27.5% midpoint), Alkop 65,000 sq ft building under construction with INR4 crore capex, and railway dynamometer due end-August 2026 with rig by September-end.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone bi-metal sales rose 40.41% to INR67.06 crores and FY27 guidance of INR360 crores (about 28% implied growth) is called conservative, backed by INR75 crore+ domestic RFQs at 75-80% conversion (more than INR60 crore) and Alkop INR100 crore target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Bi-metal utilisation is about 80% on management's machinery count (85-87% by another measure) and the Rs 9-10 crore add is the only plan; management is evaluating new land for bi-metal over the next two years, so a further capex announcement is probable.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called INR360 crore FY27 revenue conservative and said Q4 would be better, but declined to raise the figure; Q1 sales grew 36.57% to INR91.79 crores.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Brake margin of 25% may fall, Strait of Hormuz disruption stalled merchant export orders for three months, and the INR65-75 crore additional business depends on a good monsoon and no worsening geopolitics.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bi-metal engine bearings for US customers supply expected from Q3-Q4 FY27, railway brake dynamometer by end-August 2026 and testing rig by September-end, and Alkop US samples by 2027.

rows.label: Alkop US customers (Magna, Allison, Linamar-type)
rows.why: RFQs, NDAs and vendor profiling after June 2026 US/Canada trip with INR50-60 crore potential, but realisation runs into FY28.

rows.label: Railway brake business (Menon Brakes)
rows.when: approval after audit; revenue INR5-6 crore year one, INR25-3
rows.why: RDSO vendor code registered and dynamometer due end-August, but testing could take about one year and orders are unknown.

rows.label: Domestic RFQ pipeline
rows.why: RFQ list above INR75 crore at 75-80% conversion implies more than INR60 crore of additional business.

tone.note: Management was confident on the INR360 crore guidance, the INR75 crore+ domestic RFQ pipeline and Alkop INR100 crore target, but evasive on brake OEM numbers, Alkop realisation timing and any revised guidance; analysts pushed on utilisation, margin sustainability and raw-material inflation.

523828|2026-09.headline: Menon Bearings guides 30%+ growth for FY27 and FY28 after H1 FY27 income from operations of INR 194.9 crore (+47% YoY).
523828|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly sales, EBITDA, PBT and PAT on a consolidated basis for Q2 FY27, with total income up 58.6% YoY, EBITDA up 103.8%, PBT up 123% and PAT up 117%. H1 EBITDA rose 77%, PBT 92% and PAT 89.55%, with cash and bank balances including mutual funds of INR 25.69 crore. Management said it expects over 30% growth in FY27 and FY28, citing additional business of INR 30 crore in FY27, INR 131 crore in FY28 and INR 157 crore in FY29, plus a Europe pipeline of over INR 35 crore. Management attributed margin resilience to productivity gains (stated at 25%), material-usage reductions and automation, while noting raw material inflation (tin up 72%, copper up 50%, steel up 12%).

financial_highlights.metric: Total income growth (consolidated, Q2 FY27 YoY)
H1 FY27 PBT and PAT growth
Cash and bank balance incl. mutual funds
Operating cash flow H1 FY27 (analyst figure, not confirmed by management)
financial_highlights.value: ~INR 20 crore vs INR 23 crore for full FY26

segments.name: Bearings (engine/bimetal)
segments.commentary: Management cited an EBITDA margin of about 23% for the bearing segment. OEM business grew about 50% YoY in Q2 per management.

segments.name: Menon Alkop (aluminium/EV and non-auto)
segments.commentary: Alkop margin stated at 18-19%. Export value and volume growing; EV business growing about 20%; about 54 new parts developed in last two years. Auto is only about 18-20% of Alkop revenue.

segments.name: Brakes
segments.commentary: Brake segment margins stated at 30-35%, depending on product mix; management expects brakes to lead replacement-market growth.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export growth above 75% YoY in Q2 per management; exports at about 34-35% of revenue, about 80% of which goes to the USA.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth of more than 30% in revenue, with FY28 also expected above 30% if conditions hold.

Additional business estimated at INR 30 crore (FY27), INR 131 crore (FY28) and INR 157 crore (FY29), excluding a Europe opportunity of INR 35 crore to INR 40 crore expected to convert over a longer time.
Management indicated revenue could reach INR 500 crore 'next year or maybe year after', versus INR 300 crore in FY26; H2 expected to be stronger than H1.
EBITDA margin expected to range 20-22% in normal course, with a target of about 23% for next year.
Roughly 20% of the 30%+ growth expected from volume, with the balance from price revisions.
capex_capacity: Automation and robotic cells planned: about INR 5 crore in Alkop and about INR 4.5 crore in Bearings over the next 12-15 months, with ROI stated at 2.5-3.5 years.
Bearing lines: about 16 bimetal lines (from around 90 semi-automatic machines) moving to single-piece flow, expected to save about 3 people per line, roughly 50 employees in bearings.
AI-based automated visual inspection systems: some implemented, others under development; expected in place within 9-12 months. About 10 lakh engine bearing parts inspected monthly.
Capex funded from internal accruals; no term loan availed for more than six months.
Infrastructure stated as in place, with capacity added by adding machines as needed.
demand_pricing: Raw material inflation: tin up 72%, copper up 50%, steel up 12%, with average price increases near 50% YoY per management; pass-through to customers via pre-agreed formula, with a one-quarter lag absorbed.
Aluminium prices fell about 15% from May-June peak, benefiting Alkop, and vendor prices also reduced.
Headcount up about 5% YoY against about 30% revenue growth; sales and distribution costs rose on US/Europe freight.
Replacement market growing strongly, with management citing HCV, LCV and passenger vehicles growing 14-15% and EV around 20% over last six months.
Tractor schedules at all-time high despite drought-like conditions in Maharashtra; management says tractor share has fallen from 54% to 34% of the business over 10 years.
Working capital: US customers hold about 3 months of inventory in their warehouses; air freight used where Strait of Hormuz disruption extends shipping times.

qa_highlights.question: Did the decline in aluminium prices help Alkop margins in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, lower aluminium prices benefit Alkop; vendor pricing was also reduced in the quarter, adding to profit. No quantification given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did sales promotion and other expenses rise (from about INR 4.7 crore to INR 8.15 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher replacement market activity and substantially higher export freight to the USA and Europe, which raised sales and distribution costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin expand despite a 7-percentage-point gross margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower raw material consumption through process improvements, 25% productivity gains and better overhead absorption; price revisions to customers are a routine pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Is EV share of Alkop on track for 8-10% in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said it will be at or above that range, but the EV share of total will stay roughly flat as domestic and other exports also grow.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EBITDA margin expectations and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin will range 20-22% and it targets about 23% next year; competitors cited at 7-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Where does the company stand in the auto cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tractor schedules are rising despite drought in Maharashtra, HCV/LCV/PV growing 14-15%, and EV growing 20%; de-risking through non-auto applications is ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the working capital and inventory improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory build for US customers (about 3 months stock) is complete; future inventory will rise modestly with volumes, and borrowing costs have stayed flat despite turnover growth.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (tin, copper, steel) and the one-quarter lag before price pass-through may compress margins.
Concentration in USA exports (about 80% of exports) and trade policy volatility; Europe pipeline (INR 35-40 crore) not yet converted and expected to take 9-12 months from RFQ to sales.
Shipping disruptions (Strait of Hormuz) increasing working capital and air freight costs.
Management's FY27 and FY28 growth targets rely on the stated INR 30 crore/131 crore additional business pipeline; delivery against these will be the key check.
Tractor exposure (about 34% of engine bearing business per management) amid drought in Maharashtra.
Other income and intercompany eliminations mean Q1 and Q2 figures do not sum to H1; standalone and consolidated figures differ.
523828|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and promotional, with strong emphasis on record results and forward growth. Management was specific on historical numbers and margins but gave looser, qualitative answers on five-year aspirations, Europe timing and the origin of the margin gains, and repeatedly qualified targets as forward-looking.
key_quotes: There will be more than 30% growth for this year, FY27, and similarly in '27-'28 also we expect, if all the things are in place, it will be more than 30% again
So we are not looking at top line to increase significantly. We want our EBITDA margins, our PAT margins to grow at what numbers we have now.
So in the next 9 to 12 months, a lot of automation and visual systems are getting in place where we save on manpower, we save on time that leads in productivity, and quality is more focused.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets EBITDA margin of 20-22% in normal course and about 23% next year, but raw material inflation (tin up 72%, copper up 50%, steel up 12%) passes through with a one-quarter lag, and Q2 gross margin fell 7 points even as EBITDA margin expanded.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or facility addition is named; the bearing lines move from ~90 semi-automatic machines to single-piece flow and capacity is added by adding machines as needed, with capex of about INR 5 crore (Alkop) and INR 4.5 crore (Bearings) being automation rather than capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides more than 30% revenue growth in FY27 and FY28 with roughly 20% from volume and the balance from price, backed by INR 30 crore additional business in FY27 and INR 131 crore in FY28, and H2 expected stronger than H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Automation capex of about INR 9.5 crore is planned over 12-15 months funded from internal accruals, but utilisation was not disclosed, so a larger capacity capex call cannot be made from this brief.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 total income up 58.6%, EBITDA up 103.8% and H1 income up 47%, with management guiding more than 30% for FY27 and FY28 and revenue potentially reaching INR 500 crore 'next year or maybe year after' versus INR 300 crore in FY26.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Tin, copper and steel inflation (average near 50% YoY per management), the Europe INR 35-40 crore pipeline taking 9-12 months to convert, and Hormuz shipping disruption could pressure margins and delay the INR 131 crore FY28 additional business.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new product or model launch was named; management cited about 54 new parts developed in Alkop over two years but gave no launch timing.

rows.label: Europe pipeline conversion INR 35-40 crore
rows.why: The Europe opportunity of INR 35-40 crore is not yet converted and management says it takes 9-12 months from RFQ to sales, so it is a longer-dated upside outside the stated FY27-FY28 figures.

rows.label: US customer inventory build complete
rows.why: US customers hold about 3 months of inventory and management says the build is complete, with future inventory rising only modestly with volume, though air freight costs rise where Hormuz disruption extends shipping.

rows.label: Automation and productivity gains

524091|2026-03.headline: Carysil Q4 FY26 consolidated total income rose 16% to INR237 crores and PAT (after MI) jumped 42% to INR27 crores, with EBITDA margin at 20.3%.
524091|2026-03.overview: Carysil reported Q4 FY26 consolidated total income of INR237 crores (up 16% YoY), EBITDA of INR48 crores (up 33%, margin 20.3%, up 277 bps) and PAT after MI of INR27 crores (up 42%). For FY26, total income rose 14% to INR932 crores, EBITDA grew 30% to INR185 crores (margin 19.9% vs 17.3%) and PAT after MI rose 53% to INR98 crores. Management framed FY27 as a year of capacity expansion and execution, with a 250,000-unit quartz sink line due in Q4 FY27 and 70,000 units of stainless steel capacity commissioned on the call date. The company guided to 15-20% revenue growth and 18-20% EBITDA margin, while flagging freight, gas and MMA cost pressures.

524091|2026-09.headline: Carysil Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14.6% YoY to INR275.7 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 19.4% on freight and raw material costs.

EBITDA rose 9.3% to INR54.1 crore, but margin contracted to 19.4% from 20.3% a year earlier and 21.2% in Q1, which management attributed to higher raw material cost and sea freight. H1 FY27 revenue was INR537.9 crore (up 15%) and PAT INR61.1 crore (up 21.3%). Management maintained FY27 guidance of 15% revenue growth and 18-20% EBITDA margin, and announced a 5% price increase from October; the CFO is also departing.

Ibuprofen and major products run at 90-100% capacity utilisation over the last 3-4 quarters. Paracetamol capacity is about 10,800 MT, with a plan to optimise to 100% first. A paracetamol facility of 18,000 MT was mentioned in a question.
Ethyl Acetate capacity raised from 1 lakh to 1.2 lakh tonnes through debottlenecking, not a new plant.
demand_pricing: Ibuprofen prices have been stable for the last 2-3 quarters. Management expects them to hold at similar levels for the next 1-2 quarters and declined to forecast 2-3 year prices.

Order book: big customers typically 4-6 months, average order book 4-6 quarters; cost pass-through clauses are included given volatile raw material prices. Products covered are mainly ibuprofen, paracetamol and metformin.
API customer onboarding takes about 6-8 months to start commercial orders.
CDMO: development is under way with 2-3 customers, mainly European, with existing customers; validation takes about a year including customer approval.
Management could not give a volume/price split of growth, saying the increase reflects price, better utilisation and procurement.
Paracetamol prices were broadly flat QoQ despite higher acetic acid prices (management said acetic acid is not used directly for paracetamol).
Imported raw materials are about 62-63% of total raw material consumption; 60-70% in chemicals (e.g., acetic acid) and 20-22% in API.

qa_highlights.question: Ibuprofen realisation trends and whether the company will benefit in Q3/Q4.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices have been stable for several quarters and are expected to stay flat for 1-2 quarters; the price benefit is already in the P&L, and the new capacity is a strategic move rather than a response to current pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Will incremental ibuprofen capacity go to merchant or formulation customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the split is roughly 50:50 between new customers and internal CDMO consumption.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and borrowing needs for the rest of FY27.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR200 crore working capital line as of 30 September 2026 is the peak requirement, that no further borrowing is planned, and that cash flow and cash on hand are sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Does FY27 25% growth imply lower H2 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said 25%+ is for the full year on value basis, with H2 expected to perform at a similar level to H1.

qa_highlights.question: What asset turn and margins are expected in CDMO and the overall business?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset turn is about 1:3 for chemicals, 1:1 for API and 1:1 to 1:1.25 for CDMO, around 1:1.75 blended. CDMO margins are expected to exceed API margins, but management said it was too early to quantify them.

qa_highlights.question: What is the specialty chemicals toll-manufacturing arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: A renowned global chemical company customer under a cost-plus, long-term tolling arrangement with a dedicated plant; the product is confidential and is not sold in the open market.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise to about 14.5% of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to higher power and fuel costs in the summer quarter and higher freight cost, and expects these to decline in Q3 and Q4.

risks_watch: Ibuprofen supply additions from peers and China could weigh on realisations once the 18,000 MTPA expansion is commissioned in FY28.
CDMO and specialty chemical ramp-ups depend on customer validation and approvals (about one year for European approval); commercialisation timing has shifted from Q3 FY27 to FY28.
Raw material price volatility and acetic acid spikes; pass-through clauses in contracts are not fully in place. Management could not quantify the ibuprofen price trend beyond 1-2 quarters.
Other expenses rose to about 14.5% of sales (vs 13.7-14% historically); watch whether freight and power costs ease in Q3 and Q4.
Management declined to disclose product-level profitability, volume/price split and API per-kg price changes, which limits analysis.
Triacetin export commercial orders have not yet started despite REACH registration.
524164|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on H1 performance and FY27 guidance, which was revised up. Cautious and evasive on ibuprofen pricing beyond 1-2 quarters, product-level margins, volume/price split and CDMO margins, citing confidentiality or market dynamism.
key_quotes: We have maintained the positive momentum during the second quarter of FY27, delivering healthy growth across our businesses, accompanied by a meaningful improvement in profitability.
So, around 15% to 17% is a sustainable number, and we should target that.
We received certificate of suitability from EDQM for Fenofibrate-Process II, taking our total CEP approvals to 22.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin at 14-15% (H1 at 14.5%), targets 15-17% sustainable for FY29, and expects power, fuel and freight costs to ease in Q3-Q4 from the elevated 14.5% other-expense ratio.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Specialty chemicals toll plant is in trials with first batches expected Nov 2026, Ethyl Acetate debottlenecked to 1.2 lakh tonnes is done, and the 12,000 to 18,000 MTPA ibuprofen and CDMO projects are approved for FY28, though the brief notes CDMO commercialisation timing has already slipped.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Ibuprofen and major products run at 90-95% utilisation and H2 is guided similar to H1 (~INR1,550 crore per half), with the FY27 25%+ growth figure given on a value basis and no volume/price split disclosed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Three projects worth about INR500 crore were announced in Q2 and FY27 capex of INR250 crore is planned with about half spent in H1, so no new announcement is needed in the window and any further one would be a follow-on at 90%+ utilisation.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance was just raised to 25%+ from 15-20% after H1 growth of about 39%, but management said H2 will be similar to H1, so a further raise depends on ibuprofen prices holding beyond the 1-2 quarters they guided.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Ibuprofen prices are guided flat only for 1-2 quarters and the peer and China supply additions are a named risk, while raw material exposure (62-63% imported) and pass-through clauses are not fully in place.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Specialty chemicals toll batches are expected in November 2026 and CDMO tablets (1,500 million per year, Europe-focused) are due for FY28 commercialisation, though CDMO needs about a year of customer validation.

rows.label: API customer onboarding and CDMO ramp
rows.why: API customer onboarding takes 6-8 months to start commercial orders and CDMO works with 2-3 mainly European customers, with validation about a year, so new revenue lands mostly after the window.

rows.label: No further borrowing; working capital peak INR200 crore
rows.why: Management said no further borrowing is planned and cash flow plus cash on hand are sufficient, with INR250 crore FY27 capex about half spent in H1.

rows.label: Ibuprofen prices flat for 1-2 quarters
rows.why: Prices have been stable for 2-3 quarters and are expected to hold for 1-2 more, but management would not forecast beyond that and peer supply is a watch item.

tone.note: Management was confident on H1 performance, the raised FY27 guidance and the 15-17% FY29 margin target, but cautious and evasive on ibuprofen pricing beyond 1-2 quarters, CDMO margins and the volume/price split, while analysts pushed on those same points.

524200|2026-03.headline: Vinati Organics FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 17% to INR741 crores and PAT 18% to INR488 crores, with the company still debt-free.
524200|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone net income including other income rose 17% QoQ to INR631 crores, EBITDA grew 20% QoQ to INR203 crores and PAT rose 27% QoQ to INR137 crores. For FY26, standalone net income was flat at INR2,281 crores while EBITDA and PAT grew 17% and 18%. Demand softened from October 2025 and management says it has since recovered. IBB volumes fell about 20% versus FY25 because of raw material unavailability linked to the Iran war, which management says is now resolved. Management guides about 15% company-level volume growth in FY27 and FY27 capex of INR200-250 crores.

segments.name: ATBS
segments.commentary: Roughly one-third of FY26 revenue; management expects about 15% volume growth YoY for at least the next three years. Plant running at about 80% utilisation (about 75% post-expansion). Phase 2 of the expansion comes into effect by October 2026, with fuller utilisation in FY28.

segments.name: Antioxidants (AO)
segments.commentary: Roughly 15-20% of FY26 revenue; revenue grew 15% in FY26. Management said FY26 AO volume was roughly flat-to-5% up, and the anti-dumping duty (ADD) application was rejected and reapplied, with a decision 6-9 months away.

segments.name: IB and HP-MTBE
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-12% of FY26 revenue; stable in FY26, with management expecting double-digit growth in FY27.

segments.name: IBB
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-12% of FY26 revenue; volume fell about 20% versus FY25 due to raw material unavailability linked to the Iran war, now reported as resolved.

segments.name: Butyl phenols
segments.commentary: Capacity about 50,000 tonnes running at roughly 70-75% utilisation; management expects moderate growth in FY27 with no room for further expansion, so incremental demand goes first to captive use.

segments.name: Customised and others
segments.commentary: Grew 10% YoY in FY26 on higher customer demand. Remainder of revenue mix.

segments.name: VOPL (100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales were only about INR10 crores. Process reengineering of about 6 months to finish by September 2026, with production from October and revenue of about INR100-120 crores expected in FY27, from Q2/Q3.

guidance_outlook: FY27 company-level volume growth guided at about 15%.
ATBS volume growth of about 15% YoY expected for at least the next three years.
FY27 capex earmarked at INR200-250 crores (about INR200 crores at Vinati Organics and INR40-50 crores at VOPL); management says about INR250-300 crores a year for 3-5 years.
AO and butyl phenol revenue targeted at INR800-900 crores in the next two years.
Long-term EBITDA margin of 26-27% considered achievable, given expansions, new products and raw material swings.
Gross block addition of about INR500 crores assumed at 1:1 asset turn.
Two to three new downstream products expected in H2 FY27, with revenue mainly from FY28.
Company will continue to fund expansion from internal accruals and remain debt-free.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR270 crores, including VOPL capacity expansion, new product development and operational scalability. The ATBS capacity expansion was completed during FY26.

ATBS: a Phase 1 of 10,000 tonnes is commissioned. Total ATBS capacity is about 50,000 tonnes for lower molecular weight grades and about 40,000 tonnes for higher purity grades. Phase 2 (another 10,000 tonnes) expected by October 2026. Two-phase cost about INR250-300 crores.
CWIP was about INR210 crores at year-end, of which about INR60-70 crores is yet to be capitalised at VOPL. About INR120-125 crores of VOPL CWIP is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

Pipeline products are downstream derivatives of MEHQ, butyl phenols and antioxidants, plus TAA, PTAP and 4-MAP at VOPL. Isoamylene derivatives were dropped. Monomers and polymers are under consideration but not confirmed.
Butyl phenol capacity of about 50,000 tonnes is at 70-75% utilisation with no space to expand.
demand_pricing: Demand softened from October 2025. Management says demand has since recovered, and ATBS is still growing at double-digit rates industry-wide.
ATBS pricing is stable and follows a formula-based mechanism. Management says it passes raw material and logistics price moves through to customers and holds margins.

AO faces undercutting and aggressive selling by Chinese producers. Management says ADD was not granted and has been reapplied, and it notes that 80-90% of ADD applications were rejected in the sector.
Raw material and logistics availability normalised after early disruption from the Iran war in Feb 2026. Logistics is described as stable.
ATBS end-use spans polymers for enhanced oil recovery, superabsorbents, personal care, detergents, mining and water treatment. Vinati sells to polymer makers, not directly to oilfield operators.

qa_highlights.question: What new products are in the pipeline, and when will they come online?
qa_highlights.answer: Most are downstream niche chemicals for fragrance, personal care, food-additive and plastics users. Two or three products are due in H2 FY27, with revenue mainly from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 revenue mix by product?
qa_highlights.answer: ATBS is about one-third and AO is 15-20%. IB is 10-12%, IBB is 10-12%, and customised and other products make up the rest, with overall ATBS and AO together around 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VOPL revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: VOPL sales were about INR10 crores in FY26. Management expects about INR100-120 crores in FY27 once reengineering finishes, with revenue from Q2/Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is planned in VOPL and how much CWIP is there?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR40-50 crores of the FY27 capex goes to VOPL and about INR200 crores to the parent. VOPL CWIP of about INR120-125 crores is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ATBS capacity and cost of the two expansion phases?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is about 50,000 tonnes (about 40,000 tonnes for higher-purity grades) with 10,000 tonnes per phase. The two phases cost about INR250-300 crores in total.

qa_highlights.question: Will AO and butyl phenol revenue reach the targeted INR700-800 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan is on track, with AO and butyl phenol revenue in the INR800-900 crore range within the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 26-27% EBITDA margin is a reasonable long-term level given expansions, new products and raw material swings.

qa_highlights.question: Why has AO growth lagged, and what is the status of the ADD?
qa_highlights.answer: AO growth was about 5% in FY26 because of aggressive Chinese undercutting. ADD was not granted, has been reapplied, and a decision could take 6-9 months.

risks_watch: AO margins and volumes depend on the anti-dumping duty decision, which could take another 6-9 months after reapplication, while Chinese players undercut prices.
VOPL revenue of INR100-120 crores in FY27 depends on finishing process reengineering by September 2026. The plant had teething troubles with its new process.
ATBS Phase 2 utilisation is expected to build mainly in FY28, and the plant is running at about 75-80% utilisation.
Butyl phenol capacity is at 70-75% utilisation with no room to expand, so growth may cut merchant sales.
Sector cyclicality has shortened, with sharp swings in raw material prices, logistics and customer destocking.
Management guidance rests on about 15% volume growth, a recovery from the October 2025 slowdown and IBB volumes resuming after the Iran war disruption.

key_quotes: I think I've maintained an EBITDA margin of 26% to 27% because given expansions, new products, raw material fluctuations, I think that's a reasonably achievable EBITDA margin on a long-term basis.
So first of all, we did not hear back for the ADD on antioxidants, which means it was rejected. We have reapplied again for it because we have a strong case.
Basically, we went for a new process. And we faced some teething troubles there, and then we went to the main consultant and realizing some reengineering is required.

524200|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the balance sheet, ATBS demand, margins and the debt-free funding model, and openly acknowledges the slowdown from October 2025. Cautious and somewhat evasive on AO growth and the anti-dumping duty outcome, and on the VOPL timeline, which management said had hit teething troubles and was being re-engineered.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Phase 2 by October 2026 (Q3 FY27); VOPL production from Octo
rows.why: ATBS Phase 1 of 10,000 tonnes is commissioned, Phase 2 of another 10,000 tonnes is due by October 2026, and about INR120-125 crores of VOPL CWIP is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets about 15% company-level volume growth in FY27 and about 15% ATBS volume growth for at least three years, though ATBS utilisation is about 80% (75% post-expansion), IBB is down about 20% and AO grew only about 5%.

rows.why: Utilisation is about 80% in ATBS and butyl phenols are at 70-75% with no room to expand, and management has already guided INR200-250 crores for FY27 and INR250-300 crores a year for 3-5 years, so further capex plans are likely to be firmed up.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 20% QoQ and PAT 27% QoQ, and the Iran-war raw material disruption is resolved, but the FY27 guide of about 15% volume growth rests on recovery that is not yet proven.

rows.label: VOPL revenue ramp to INR100-120 crores in FY27
rows.why: VOPL sales were about INR10 crores in FY26; process reengineering of about 6 months must finish by September 2026 and the plant had teething troubles, so the ramp depends on that timeline.

rows.label: AO anti-dumping duty decision
rows.why: ADD was rejected and reapplied, with 80-90% of sector applications rejected historically, and AO revenue grew only about 15% in FY26 with volume roughly flat to 5% up under Chinese undercutting.

rows.label: IBB volume recovery after Iran-war disruption
rows.why: IBB volume fell about 20% versus FY25 on raw material unavailability, which management now says is resolved, but no recovery figures were given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the debt-free model, ATBS demand, formula-based pricing and margins, and openly acknowledged the October 2025 slowdown; it was cautious and somewhat evasive on AO growth, the anti-dumping duty outcome and the VOPL timeline after teething troubles.

524200|2026-09.headline: Vinati Organics Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA fell 27% YoY to INR142 crores on a 21% margin, while net income rose 21% to INR707 crores.
524200|2026-09.overview: Standalone net income including other income rose 21% YoY to INR707 crores in Q2 FY27, but EBITDA fell 27% to INR142 crores and PAT fell 33% to INR87 crores. Management attributed the margin squeeze to Middle East war-driven increases in energy and logistics costs that were not fully passed on, and to an ATBS volume shift from Q2 into Q3 and Q4 due to customer destocking. Management guided to a 20-25% top-line increase for FY27 and an EBITDA margin of about 24-25%, and announced two INR500 crore specialty chemical capex plans funded from internal accruals. VOPL (MEHQ/BHA chain) commercial sales are now delayed to April, and its FY27 revenue is guided at only INR75-100 crores.

segments.name: ATBS
segments.commentary: Approximately 27-28% of H1 FY27 revenue. Demand did not pick up as expected due to customer destocking, and volume shifted from Q2 into Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: IBB
segments.commentary: Approximately 12-15% of H1 revenue. Management said H1 was strong on both volume and price, and expects similar in H2.

segments.name: Butyl Phenol
segments.commentary: Approximately 16-20% of H1 revenue per the sales-mix answer, later clarified as 15-17% (or 17-18% at the start of the call). Performance described as stable, with better H2 expected.

segments.name: Antioxidants (AO)
segments.commentary: Approximately 15-17% of H1 revenue. Strong H1 performance despite a challenging market; management expects momentum to continue in H2 on market expansion.

segments.name: IB (isobutylene)
segments.commentary: Reported strong H1 performance, with the same trend expected in H2. No figures given.

segments.name: VOPL (Veeral Organics, MEHQ/BHA chain)
segments.commentary: MEHQ is self-consumed to make BHA at low volume. Commercial sales are expected from April. FY27 revenue guided at INR75-100 crores, below the earlier INR100 crore expectation. Ramp-up to optimum utilisation expected in about one year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line expected to grow 20-25% YoY on volume and pricing improvement.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 24-25%, down from the earlier 25-30% range.
FY28 EBITDA margin guided at 25-26%; management said the worst is behind us.
Logistics rates have started cooling in Q3 and are expected to fall further in Q4, supporting Q3 and Q4 profitability.
VOPL revenue for FY27 guided at INR75-100 crores, with streamlined operations expected by April or May 2027.
New products revenue is expected to start from December 2026 or January 2027 (per management, Q&A).
capex_capacity: INR500 crore capex announced for new specialty chemicals for fragrances, personal care, water treatment, oilfields and resins. Commercialisation in two years, funded from internal accruals.
Expected asset turnover of about 1:1 to 1.5x and ROI of 15-20% on the new capex.

A second INR500 crore capex is under consideration; land acquisition is in progress, and management expects clarity in about six months (noted as a couple of months in the prepared remarks). It may not proceed. Also funded from internal accruals.
Of the new products, 65-70% of volume is expected to be exported. Management said some products would be the only Indian producer and others the second or third.
VOPL: MEHQ expansion and debottlenecking are taking longer than expected. Commercial sales expected from April 2027. Customer evaluations are under way.

Management expects the process re-engineering at VOPL to take until April or May 2027, then about one year to reach optimum utilisation. Another source said it would take four months to reach optimum capacity.
demand_pricing: ATBS destocking delayed the H1 volume target. Management says Q3 is already showing an uptick in ATBS demand, and H2 recovery is expected.
Raw material cost increases were largely passed on to customers. Energy and logistics cost increases were not fully passed through, compressing margins.
New specialty products: average realisation around USD 3/kg, with a range of USD 2 to USD 4.5/kg. Management expects EBITDA margins similar to the current 25% range.
MEHQ demand is still considered strong because it is used as a polymer inhibitor. Management called the current situation a temporary downturn and said it is still high gross margin.
Management did not give a specific reason why oil and gas price strength has not lifted ATBS demand this time. It repeatedly deferred to H2.

qa_highlights.question: What chemistries and pilot testing sit behind the INR500 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Products are adjacent to existing ones (backward, forward or horizontal integration). They have been tested over the last year in pilot work, and management is confident about commercialisation.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue scale-up and margin profile are expected from the new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset turnover of about 1:1 to 1.5x and ROI of 15-20%, with similar economics for the second INR500 crore project.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q2 margin the lowest in company history?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about the full drop to ATBS volume shifting from Q2 into Q3 and Q4. It also cited energy and logistics costs not being fully passed on. It said the worst is now behind.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 MEHQ/VOPL revenue outlook, given the earlier expectation of about INR100 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 VOPL revenue guided at INR75-100 crores, not expected to cross INR100 crores. The delay was attributed to an internal process re-engineering that will be streamlined by April 2027. Five products are in the VOPL range, including MEHQ, guaiacol, anisole and PTAP.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to 25-26% EBITDA margin for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How are the new products' competitive landscape and export mix?
qa_highlights.answer: For some products Vinati would be the only Indian producer, and for one segment the second or third. Exports are 65-70% of the expected mix, with average realisation around USD 3/kg.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the Q3 and Q4 volume shift from ATBS and on logistics and energy cost relief.
VOPL/MEHQ: revenue guided lower than before, and commercial sales have slipped to April 2027. Watch for the ramp-up and any further delays.
Execution risk on the INR500 crore capex, given the company's past project execution issues (acknowledged by management) and a 15-20% ROI target.
Chinese capacity additions in the MEHQ/BHA chain could pressure prices and volumes.
The second INR500 crore project is not confirmed and may not proceed.
Inconsistent product-mix percentages for butyl phenol and AO were given during the call and need clarification.

Management was also candid about past execution problems at VOPL.

524208|2026-03.headline: Aarti Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 2,422 crore and EBITDA 29% to INR 342 crore, with FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crore.
524208|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 2,422 crore (up 9% YoY), EBITDA INR 342 crore (up 29%) and PAT INR 137 crore (up 43%), helped by volume growth and higher utilisation. West Asia disruption raised benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene and methanol prices by over 60%, lifted freight costs and cut Middle East shipments, which are about 9-10% of revenue. Zone IV projects are delayed 3-4 months on contract labour shortages, with the bulk now expected in FY27. Management guided FY27 capex to INR 700-800 crore and aims to reduce net debt in FY27 despite working-capital pressure.

segments.name: Dyes, pigments and paints

qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory impact was not significant; FX gain was about INR 10 crore in the quarter, and raw material costs also rose in March.

qa_highlights.answer: About 9-10% of revenue on an annual average basis, mostly energy; product is being redirected elsewhere, with the full impact visible in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY27 capex fall and what is the breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was INR 1,125 crore as guided, not reduced; FY27 guided at INR 700-800 crore mainly for Zone IV, the new long-term contract and about INR 150 crore maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt high despite about INR 600 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash was a late-March term loan disbursement; net debt is about INR 4,300 crore, with bulk of cash used to repay debt in early April. Working capital rose INR 250-300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 freight and other-expense jump and inventory build?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight rates rose from mid-February, exports were 57% of revenue, and US mix lengthened voyages; INR 409 crore stock build reflects goods in transit not yet recognised as revenue.

524208|2026-06.headline: Aarti Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to Rs 2,627 crore and EBITDA 79% to Rs 385 crore, with management refusing to guarantee the run rate.
524208|2026-06.overview: Revenue of Rs 2,627 crore (+41% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 385 crore (+79% YoY) were lifted by raw-material price pass-through, product mix, and inventory and FX gains, which management sized at roughly Rs 50-60 crore. Volumes fell sequentially (energy -17% QoQ, non-energy -7%, overall about -12%) amid West Asia disruption and high raw-material prices. Zone IV commissioning is delayed by 3-6 months due to labour shortages, and management declined to commit to a forward EBITDA run rate. The Augene JV is near commissioning, and FY27 capex remains on track at Rs 700-800 crore.

segments.name: Energy (Fuel Additives)
segments.commentary: Fuel additives capacity expanded to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA; West Asia share fell to about 2% from about 15%, and volumes were redirected to US, Africa, Europe and India. Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged about $15-18/bbl, and management expects the capacity to reach high utilisation in Q1 itself.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Polymers
segments.commentary: Demand was soft in Q1 on weak downstream US and China demand, and low shipments followed heavy Q4 FY26 bulk shipments to the US. Management expects recovery in Q2 and full-year growth.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Dyes & Pigments
segments.commentary: Demand remained subdued amid high raw-material prices and seasonality. Price increases in dyes and pigments and pharma were partly linked to China's VAT removal on the NCB chain.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Pharma and Agro
segments.commentary: Pharma demand was stable. Agrochemical volumes were marginally lower as customers resisted elevated raw-material-linked prices; recovery is expected in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY28 EBITDA target of Rs 1,800 crore retained; the Augene JV is included in this guidance, but management said Zone IV ramp-up may be slower than originally assumed.
Management declined to guide to a sustainable quarterly EBITDA run rate, citing plus/minus 15-20% monthly price volatility; it expects volume growth to offset lost inventory gains.

qa_highlights.question: What were the FX and inventory gains in Q1, and what is the impact on the EBITDA base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a Rs 50-60 crore impact but said it is hard to quantify because of intra-quarter volatility; the CFO said FX gains came from squaring off import positions as the rupee moved in a Rs 92-97 range, and management advised treating this as operating profit with no forward commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gross margin lower sequentially despite the inventory and FX benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly gross margin is not a reliable steady-state indicator, citing timing of raw-material purchases and product placement, freight, lower volumes raising operating costs, and the chemical business running on absolute rupee deltas rather than percentage margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Zone IV delay affect FY28 EBITDA visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MPP and calcium chloride unit are on track, but the five chemistry blocks face slower ramp-up than originally planned, and it will share ramp-up details once the blocks commission.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Augene JV affect reported EBITDA, and is it in the Rs 1,800 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that the Rs 1,800 crore FY28 guidance includes Augene EBITDA, while the Re Aarti JV is not expected to contribute meaningfully before FY28; reporting treatment for JVs is yet to be finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is the energy business's volume, capacity and market share sustainable once West Asia normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business remains in a market-development phase; the portfolio is diversified across US, Africa, Europe, Middle East and India (Southeast Asia not yet penetrated), and it expects utilisation gains rather than volume shifts when West Asia reopens.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company stop disclosing absolute sales volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it removed absolute sales numbers from slides because they were being used in an unfavourable way, and now gives energy/non-energy volume growth plus value-chain utilisation ranges.

risks_watch: Zone IV: five chemistry blocks face a 3-6 month delay and slower ramp-up; the MPP first product is expected in August 2026, and the FY28 Rs 1,800 crore EBITDA guidance (which includes Augene) depends on this ramp-up.

Earnings quality: management said FX and inventory gains (Rs 50-60 crore, roughly Rs 47 crore per an analyst's figure) helped Q1, and it declined to commit to a forward quarterly EBITDA run rate given plus/minus 15-20% monthly price swings.

Energy seasonality and West Asia: management expects winter weakness from late October to December, and West Asia volumes (share down to about 2% from about 15%) are not yet restored; utilisation of the 360 KTPA fuel additives capacity is the key test over the next 12 months.
Working capital and leverage: management said working capital expanded and debt and finance costs rose in Q1; watch debt levels as imported-raw-material inventory (1-1.5 months) carries price risk.

Augene JV commissioning in Q2 FY27 and the Re Aarti JV reporting treatment, which management has yet to finalise; watch the Rs 300-400 crore steady-state revenue assumption and PAT-level consolidation.

I would again hesitate to hazard a guess.
So we did not see the EBITDA run rate can be maintained.

524208|2026-09.headline: Aarti Industries Q2 FY27 revenue rose 73% YoY to Rs 3,887 crore and EBITDA hit a record Rs 418 crore (+44% YoY), helped by raw-material pass-through.
524208|2026-09.overview: Aarti Industries reported record quarterly revenue and EBITDA for Q2 FY27, with H1 EBITDA above Rs 802 crore against Rs 507 crore a year earlier. Growth was driven by volumes and by passing through higher raw-material costs, with Energy-linked products the main contributor. Net debt rose above Rs 4,650 crore on working capital and finance costs, prompting a Rs 1,000 crore fund-raise enabling resolution approved by shareholders on 31 October 2026. Zone IV Phase I was commissioned on 7 September 2026, with most of the Rs 1,800-1,900 crore CWIP expected to be capitalised by 31 March 2027.

524332|2026-03.headline: BCL Industries FY26 revenue INR2,913 crore, EBITDA INR251 crore (+18%), margin 8.6%; 150 KLPD Bathinda unit nearing commercial output.

Q4 PAT was INR126 crore, up 23% YoY at a 4.3% margin. Ethanol allocation from OMCs was lower than expected, so the company diverted output to ENA and SBF, which kept utilisation near full but pressured realisations. The packaged edible oil business was exited, while the refinery and trading businesses continued. The 150 KLPD Bathinda grain-based distillery is in testing, taking total installed capacity to 900 KLPD.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 revenue and EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about INR300 crore from the 150 KLPD unit at full utilisation and similar or slightly better EBITDA margins as overheads stay flat.

qa_highlights.question: Can the new 150 KLPD unit run at 100% in year one?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects at least 75% utilisation from Q2 FY27, with rated capacity by early July after a 15-day trial production.

qa_highlights.question: Can distillery EBITDA hold at 11.8% in Q4 given peers guide 12-15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should hold, citing the paddy straw boiler and consolidation of vegetable oil operations. Pure ethanol could reach 15% at full OMC allocation, but ENA/SBF are raw-material linked and not fixed-margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3-5 year strategy and real estate exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Real estate projects date from 2005-2010 and are winding down with no new projects. Focus is biofuel: Fatehabad ethanol, later CBG and sustainable aviation fuel, and a debt-free balance sheet within 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt and cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR300-335 crore including fund and non-fund based; INR120 crore on interest subvention at about 4.25%; average cost below 7%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the OCF improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital release is not one-off: no capex currently, ENA/SBF cash-and-carry sales, OMC receivables cut to 21 days, and edible oil inventory liquidation adds to it.

qa_highlights.question: Why exit packaged edible oil and sell land?
qa_highlights.answer: City unit had to move due to red-category restrictions. Machines were shifted or sold, and about 18 acres of city land is being sold for about INR30 crore. Proceeds go to cash and expansion.

524332|2026-06.headline: BCL Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore (10.5% margin) despite revenue falling to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore.
524332|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue fell to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore, mainly due to closure of the edible oil unit and exit from packaged oil. EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore, with margin up 370 bps to 10.5%, and PAT rose 6% to INR 36 crore (5.7% margin). Distillery EBITDA margin improved to 12.41%, while ENA realisations fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. A fire at a 200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol tank on 19 June 2026 shut that plant temporarily; management said insurance recovery is virtually certain and no net loss was booked. Management also completed the acquisition of the remaining 25% of Svaksha Distillery and reduced working capital borrowings, but deferred the Fatehabad 250 KLPD project and the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 820 crore in Q1 FY26 (decline)
from 11.8% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Distillery
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 12.41% in Q1 FY27 versus 11.8% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in Q1 FY26. ENA volume rose to 19,376 KL from 7,960 KL YoY, but ENA realisation fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. The 115 TPH paddy straw boiler meets 100% of steam and power needs.

segments.name: Country liquor (PML)
segments.commentary: Sold 6,37,993 boxes, up 42% QoQ and 46% YoY. Punjab Raspberry launched in Q4 FY26 and Jamun Vodka in July 2026. Management targets 30 lakh cases this year out of a market of about 1.25 crore cases per annum in Punjab.

segments.commentary: Exit completed, including closure of the Bathinda oil and vanaspati unit. Soft oil refinery and trading continue as legacy operations. Revenue decline was mainly from this exit.

Order book described as full for about the next three months, supported by OMC allocation of about 4.5 crore litres from a Supreme Court order covering until November.

200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol plant shut after the 19 June 2026 fire; the tank was holding about 90,000 litres at the time and is under repair.
Fatehabad 250 KLPD grain-based plant: orders and advances are on hold after social media backlash; machinery orders are reportedly finalised and management is waiting before starting construction.
Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project is on hold because biodiesel prices are not remunerative. Goyal Distillery 250 KLPD project is on hold pending industry clarity.
Malt plant is at conceptualisation stage with no timeline. IMFL entry targeted for next year, with the company still working on it.

Management said maize-based ethanol to OMCs is profitable, while FCI-rice-based ethanol is near cost. ENA and private ethanol margins are about the same. Blended average EBITDA is about 12%, roughly INR 9-10/litre on maize and ENA.
Maize procurement cost was about INR 22-23/kg last quarter. Current maize price is about INR 25/kg, and management said ENA prices have been revised upwards.
DDGS prices have eased INR 1-2/kg over 2-3 months to about INR 24-25/kg for both maize and rice based.
Management expects ethanol demand to improve only slightly next year, as sugarcane-based ethanol is unlikely to be allowed. Flex fuel demand is a long-term driver, with few FFV models on sale so far.
Management said E20 is in place for about 18 months with no major vehicle damage seen, but blending expansion beyond E20 may be delayed. Isobutanol and SAF are cited as future demand sources.

qa_highlights.question: At what price is ethanol sold to private players, and is it FCI rice or maize based?
qa_highlights.answer: Private ethanol buyers are mainly Reliance at an average ex-factory price of about INR 58/litre. Private buyers use damaged grain, while the company's own FCI-rice ethanol is tied to 40% of OMC allocation. Maize procurement cost was about INR 22-23/kg last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Cause of the Bathinda fire and safeguards for other plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the likely cause was static charge, possibly from clothing of a nearby worker. The company has added facilities to prevent such incidents and called it rare.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for grain ethanol after E20 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is expected to improve only slightly next year because sugarcane ethanol is unlikely to be allowed. Flex fuel is a long-term driver, with isobutanol and SAF as additional sources, and cooking fuel use was also cited.

qa_highlights.question: Unit economics across FCI-rice, OMC maize and ENA/private ethanol?
qa_highlights.answer: FCI-rice ethanol to OMCs is near cost. Maize-based ethanol to OMCs is quite profitable. ENA and private ethanol margins are about the same, with blended EBITDA margin near 12%, or roughly INR 9-10/litre on maize and ENA on average.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Goyal bio-CNG, biodiesel and the 250 KLPD Goyal Distillery project?
qa_highlights.answer: Bio-CNG is under active evaluation after a favourable new policy, though paddy straw is tricky, mainly due to by-product sale. The company is not making biodiesel. The 250 KLPD Goyal project is on hold pending industry clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project on hold, and does maize oil locally sourced change this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said biodiesel prices are not remunerative and biodiesel feedstock is largely imported, so government has focused less on it. Isobutanol is being tested to promote indigenous feedstock. Management said the government's view could not be commented on.

qa_highlights.question: Malt plant and IMFL entry timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Malt plant is still at conceptualisation with no timeline. IMFL entry is being worked on and is hoped for next year. Management views country liquor as more profitable than competitive IMFL.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the 250 KLPD Fatehabad project after the July statement about construction by August?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders and advances are on hold after social media backlash against the ethanol policy. Machinery orders are finalised and the company is waiting before starting construction.

qa_highlights.question: Land sale timing, debt repayment and release of pledged shares?
qa_highlights.answer: No update on the land sale, as Bathinda real estate is slow and there is no rush. Working capital utilisation is low, some small loans were repaid, and banks released pledged shares. Working capital limit to be cut by INR 50 crore in August.

qa_highlights.question: Trend in DDGS realisations and Punjab country liquor market share?
qa_highlights.answer: DDGS prices eased INR 1-2/kg over 2-3 months to about INR 24-25/kg for maize and rice based. Punjab country liquor market is about 1.25 crore cases a year, with a 30 lakh case target for this year.

qa_highlights.question: Volume outlook, total debt level and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes should stay about flat until the 200 KLPD unit restarts in about 15 days. Working capital utilisation is about INR 60 crore, with total debt around INR 360 crore including working capital. Debt rises only with a new capex project, and working capital is to be run towards zero over about 1.5 years. No buyback is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Ethanol mixing in diesel, E20 damage, and government mandates beyond E20?
qa_highlights.answer: Management distinguished ethanol-in-diesel, which faces a flash point issue, from isobutanol, which it said is still under trial and not shelved. It said E20 has run 18 months without major vehicle damage, but further blending could be delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Insurance cover and stock lost in the 200 KL tank, and expected restart?
qa_highlights.answer: The tank held about 90,000 litres at the time. The plant is being repaired and is expected to restart in about 15 days. Management said both stock loss and profit loss are covered by insurance, and the P&L impact is still being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Share of the Supreme Court-allowed OMC volume and the order book outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is among the biggest gainers, with about 4.5 crore litres from both units under the Supreme Court order, covering until November. The order book is more than full for the next 3 months. Flex fuel demand will take time.

qa_highlights.question: Current maize price, margin outlook and state subsidy for CBG?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize is about INR 25/kg now. ENA prices have been revised upwards, but raw material and fuel costs are rising. Management guided margins at about 10-12% with variation. Haryana has a CBG policy and the central policy is also favourable.
