524774|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 57% YoY to ₹149.23 crore and EBITDA margin hit 14.35%, but margins were marginally lower QoQ on cost pressures.
524774|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was ₹149.23 crore, up 57% YoY and 17% QoQ, driven by higher volumes and better capacity utilisation. EBITDA rose to ₹21.41 crore (14.35% margin, up 769 bps YoY) and PAT to ₹13.49 crore from ₹0.54 crore. Management said margins were slightly lower sequentially because fixed-price contracts blocked immediate pass-through of higher freight and raw material costs, and because of forex and investment mark-to-market provisions. FY26 revenue was ₹500.95 crore (+36%), EBITDA ₹72.69 crore (14.51% margin) and PAT ₹48.13 crore (+128%). Phase II commissioning slipped to early Q2 FY27 due to gas and labour shortages, with commercial production still guided for H2 FY27.

segments.name: Animal API
segments.commentary: Core business, contributing 95% of Q4 FY26 revenue. Top 10 customers were 29% of sales and top 10 products 66%. Company now offers about 45 APIs versus about 20 three years ago.

segments.name: Regulated markets (Europe/US)
segments.commentary: Europe sales expected to start in FY27 and US in FY28, with significant revenue from FY28. Europe has three CEPs approved, three under review and two being prepared; US VMS filings are five done with six planned this year.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin target of 15% to 18%; management said the company is close to this band, with Q1 FY27 possibly 1-2% lower as price increases only started flowing mid-quarter and margins expected from Q2 onwards.
Partial price pass-through achieved in Q1 FY27; management declined to quantify the overall price increase.
Phase II (Tarapur greenfield) commissioning moved to early Q2 FY27 from Q1 FY27; commercial production still targeted for H2 FY27.
Expected total Phase II capex of ₹210 crore, of which ₹182.75 crore was spent up to Q4 FY26; ongoing capex after completion estimated at ₹15-20 crore.
New expansion revenue potential of up to ₹350 crore turnover, to be reached over three to four years; the company declined to combine it with existing-plant revenue.
Regulated market margins expected to be 3-5 percentage points higher than the 15-18% band, but management declined to give regulated revenue figures.
capex_capacity: Phase I of the expansion is contributing meaningfully and is operating at about 70-80% utilisation, with Q4 volumes absorbed within it.
Phase II includes five clean rooms and is expected to be commissioned in early Q2 FY27, with commercial production from H2 FY27.

Phase II capex rose from ₹160 crore to ₹210 crore: about ₹20 crore for automation and digitisation and about ₹50 crore from higher metal costs; management said the increase will not add sales capacity.
Brownfield expansion of existing facilities is planned for FY27 to add ROW capacity.
Peak utilisation of the new plant is expected to take three to four years.
Company outsources about 20% of its intermediate requirements.
demand_pricing: Volume growth reported across geographies, with Latin America a successful new market and customer count up 47 QoQ on new country registrations.
Competition from Chinese and Indian players continues; price erosion on fluralaner has largely settled, and Chinese producers have begun raising prices from April/May 2026.
Oversupply in 2024 and 2025 drove price erosion; management does not expect return to prior 20-21% margins for at least two to three years.
Management plans to add 9-10 new products per year, and five new APIs were added in Q4.
Fixed-price contracts delayed pass-through of freight and raw material cost increases linked to geopolitical developments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue run rate from Phase I without Phase II, and how is outsourcing contributing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed a run rate of about ₹150 crore per quarter from Phase I plus outsourcing, with 10-15% growth on top; Phase II's five clean rooms commission next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the USFDA inspection and the Phase II utilisation until then?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the audit timing depends on the regulator and could fall in 2026 or 2027; until then Phase II will serve ROW and Europe, with European business expected in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How many CEPs and DMFs are approved, and when will the rest come through?
qa_highlights.answer: Three CEPs are registered and three are under review, with a ~18-month review period; management expects six CEPs and nine DMFs by year-end 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise ₹10-11 crore QoQ, and how much was forex loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to mark-to-market provisioning on forex and investments; it did not have the exact forex figure on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company likely to hit a higher margin band?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is 15-18% EBITDA margin and it is close; it said partial pass-through is done and China has started raising prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation and dividend plan given the debt and cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth capex is funded internally without new borrowing, and it has not yet set a dividend strategy for three years out.

risks_watch: USFDA audit timing is entirely at the regulator's discretion, and US regulated revenue could slip beyond FY28.
Phase II commissioning already slipped one quarter due to gas and labour shortages.
Fixed-price contracts and the lag in pass-through leave margins exposed to crude-linked freight and raw material inflation; Q1 FY27 margins may be 1-2% lower.
Forex and investment mark-to-market provisions weighed on Q4 margins and other expenses; the amount was not disclosed.
Chinese supply and capacity could keep pressure on prices and limit recovery to the earlier 20%+ margin range.

524804|2026-03.headline: Aurobindo Q4 FY26 revenue ₹8,853 crore (flat-to-up YoY, Revlimid-hit base), EBITDA ₹1,801 crore at 20.3%; FY27 EBITDA margin guided north of 21%.
524804|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 and FY26 both set record revenue and EBITDA, with FY26 revenue at ₹33,653 crore (+6% YoY, +9.5% ex-gRevlimid) and EBITDA at ₹6,856 crore (20.4% margin). Q4 ex-gRevlimid revenue grew 15.3% YoY (7% in USD), while US formulations fell 18% YoY in constant currency on the high Q4 FY25 gRevlimid base. Europe was the standout, up 30% YoY to ₹2,795 crore, and the company crossed €1 billion of annual European revenue. Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin to sustain and progressively improve to north of 21%, and called out biosimilars, the TheraNym CMO and Pen-G backward integration as medium-term drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating costs ex-R&D rise 11% QoQ and 17% YoY, and will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly power and fuel for the Pen-G plant, which ramped in Q4. Costs will stay at this level, but captive 6-APA lowers raw material cost and lifts gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA loss came from new projects in FY26, and will they break even in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Pen-G and 6-APA lost about ₹200 crore+ in FY26 but turned EBITDA-positive in Q4 on operating leverage and better yields. China plant incurred a loss and is expected to be profitable in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline to the $2 billion US revenue mark, and Lannett closing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit to a date, saying it could take 1-2 years, faster if acquisitions materialise. Lannett expected to close early Q2 FY27 after FTC delays from a 76-day government shutdown.

qa_highlights.question: Europe growth outlook after crossing €1 billion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least double-digit growth in constant currency, supported by more than 10 China-sourced products already launched and tech-transfer products.

qa_highlights.question: Biologics CMO revenue timing and TheraNym strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit-1 commissioning by end-2026 with steady revenue from 2028; Unit-2 revenue from 2031. Long-term goal is a multi-customer CDMO by 2032, with MSD as anchor for about 10 years.

qa_highlights.question: Biosimilar margins and price erosion assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin of 65-75% at portfolio level; US erosion capped at about 60%, Europe 75-85%. Yields of 4-6 g/L and 2,500-5,000 L bioreactors seen as the cost-competitiveness basis.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 21% FY27 EBITDA margin guidance include the rupee tailwind?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said it nets out cost pressures (solvents, freight, raw materials) and said the outcome is a combined effect, without confirming the exact split.

qa_highlights.question: Pen-G capacity and yields?
qa_highlights.answer: March output ~11,300 t and April ~10,800 t, with the company running 17 fermenters and balancing yield and inventory build.

524804|2026-06.headline: Aurobindo Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to Rs 9,150 crore; operating EBITDA Rs 1,924 crore (21% margin) after a Rs 43 crore one-time charge; FY27 guidance reiterated.
524804|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16% YoY to Rs 9,150 crore, with formulations at Rs 8,101 crore (89% of sales) growing 17%. Operating EBITDA was Rs 1,924 crore at a 21% margin, after a Rs 43 crore one-time loss on derecognition of leased residuals, and PAT was Rs 1,032 crore. The Lannett acquisition closed after FTC approval, and management reiterated FY27 guidance of double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin above 21% and absolute EBITDA above Rs 8,000 crore. Management was largely forthcoming on biosimilars, CDMO economics and Lannett, but declined to give specifics on Lannett's product pipeline and the Europe upfront payment.

526227|2026-06.headline: Filatex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.3% QoQ to INR1,145 crore and PAT to INR49.1 crore, driven by pass-through raw material prices.
526227|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose 16.3% QoQ to INR1,145 crore on higher realisations, while volumes were flat QoQ at 89,872 MT. PBT rose to INR65.87 crore and PAT to INR49.1 crore, helped by inventory gains of about INR15-17 crore expected in the quarter. Production fell to 84,075 MT from 94,996 MT a year earlier as the company cut run-rates in April to avoid carrying high-cost inventory. Management focused on the Ecosis textile-to-textile chemical recycling project, which is still under installation with commercial operations guided for end-October/early-November 2026.

526247|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR89.2 crores with net profit up 78%, but FY26 revenue fell 7% to INR388.3 crores; FY27 guided at INR600-700 crores.
526247|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 20% YoY to INR89.2 crores, with EBIT up 35% to INR9.6 crores (10.8% margin) and PAT up 78% to INR6.6 crores. For full FY26, revenue fell 7% to INR388.3 crores as FY25's high-value chaffs and flares emergency orders were not repeated, while EBIT rose 42% to INR69.3 crores (17.8% margin) and PAT rose 61% to INR45.8 crores, helped by one-off other income. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR600-700 crores and EBIT margin to 15-20%, with the order book at a record INR1,569 crores. Execution remains the central concern: raw material shortages (MIL, DRDO alternate materials), the Katepally plant accident, and pending free-issue material from BDL and DRDO all delayed deliveries.

FY27 EBIT margin expected at 15-20%, versus 17.8% in FY26.
FY27 export revenue expected at about INR200 crores, with domestic about INR500 crores; management said quarterly phasing will vary.

Katepally large rocket motor facility: commissioning targeted by September 2026, with production from November 2026. Broader Katepally RDX/HMX expansion may slip to Q3 FY27, with qualification taking 1-2 months more.
Andhra Pradesh 400-acre defense facility: land price still under negotiation; management expects commissioning 1-1.5 years after the price is finalised.
FY27 capex total of about INR32 crores (INR60 crores less INR28 crores spent in FY26), per management's reconfirmation of earlier guidance.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR28 crores. The FY26-27 plan was INR60 crores in total, comprising Katepally expansion and PDK, which the analyst read as INR45 crores and INR15 crores. Management said the PDK flare plant was already productionised in FY25, with mixers, storage and magazines still under construction.
Katepally: the RDX and HMX expansion is ongoing and not complete. A large planetary mixer and balancing equipment are in progress, and some items are expected to be capitalised by end-Q1 FY27.

Katepally rocket motor facility (large motors for ISRO and DRDO strategic systems) was hit by an accident. Equipment is in fabrication and the building is under construction, with commissioning targeted for September 2026.
Peddakandukur flares plant: rebuilt after an accident about 1.5 years ago, recommissioned, and now producing in-house. Import dependence for flare components has reduced.

Odisha: the first land parcel was rejected and the state government is proposing new parcels. Management is in a video conference with Odisha officials. The three-phase plan has its second and third phases 4-5 years out.

Output is about 50 motors per month across LRSAM, MRSAM and Astra (per management's answer on domestic deliveries). About 40 motors were delivered to domestic customers in the current status described.
demand_pricing: Exports are about 54% of the order book and domestic about 46%. Management said export licences are held for most export orders, and that the INR400 crores of export orders still pending are development orders where invoicing follows milestones.
Newly won INR350.23 crore export order (April 2026) for defence products. Management expects an export licence decision in about 3 months.

A INR18.9 crore order received in February 2026 was cancelled in April because an export licence was not granted. Management said licence rejection risk depends on government policy and the destination country.
Domestic BDL and DRDO orders depend on free-issue materials (FIMs) from those agencies; management said these cannot be executed without them.

Management said alternate raw materials for land mines, loitering munitions and medium-calibre ammunition are in DRDO trials. MIL, the high-explosive supplier, could not meet requirements. Management expects approval within 1-2 months.

Pipeline: QRSAM is not included in the estimates. Some chaffs and flares orders are at negotiation stage and some RFPs are pending. Management expects the order book to stay at about INR1,000 crores-plus after current execution.
Other income: management said the Q4 and FY26 increase came from supplier discounts on delayed deliveries, paid in two parts, and that it is non-recurring.

qa_highlights.question: What growth and margin is targeted for FY27 given fewer emergency orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue target INR600-700 crores and EBIT margin 15-20%. Drivers are land mines, drone and loitering munition payloads, and medium-calibre ammunition, where alternate raw materials have been accepted.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR500 crore guidance from February missed (about INR390 crores delivered)?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material shortages: MIL could not supply inputs for mines, loitering munitions and flares. Alternate materials are in DRDO trials, with production expected once approved in 1-2 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Katepally capex on track, and when does it finish?
qa_highlights.answer: Some items to be capitalised by end-Q1 FY27. Full completion may slip to Q3 FY27 because plant and product qualification takes another 1-2 months after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export/domestic split of the order book, and how much export licence risk exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 54% and domestic about 46%. Management said licence approval depends on government policy and the country; the INR18.9 crore cancelled order shows the risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pending order book is stuck, and why?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic orders depend on free-issue materials from BDL and DRDO; about 40 motors delivered recently. Development-stage export orders are being executed against milestones.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the INR430 crore October 2025 order will be executed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution has just started. About two-thirds is expected by end-FY27, with one-third in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Jagdalpur O&M contract lost, and is ISRO renewal possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagdalpur was lost in bidding because costs had risen. ISRO contract has about 2.5 years left, and renewal will be bid when the RFP is issued.

526247|2026-06.headline: Premier Explosives Q1 FY27 revenue fell 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore, EBIT margin 4.7%, order book INR1,393 crore (94% defence).
526247|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore as dispatches and project execution slipped, mainly on export deliveries held up by maritime disruption and imported countermeasure components. EBIT fell 80% YoY to INR4.8 crore (4.7% margin) and PAT fell 80% to INR3 crore (3% margin), with raw material costs squeezing margins. Management said the export licence backlog is largely cleared and expects the delayed execution to complete in Q2 and Q3. Order book stands at INR1,393 crore, and FY27 revenue target is retained at about INR600 crore. Apollo Micro Systems' acquisition of promoter stake was discussed, with synergy details deferred to next quarter.

segments.name: Defence and Space
segments.commentary: Revenue declined about 35% YoY per analyst question; management attributed delays to export licences and component imports, not customer acceptance. Defence is 94% of the order book.

segments.name: Industrial explosives / bulk
segments.commentary: About 6% of order book. Singareni execution of about INR25-30 crore remains for FY27; margins described as very thin, with some contracts negative. Coal India work withdrawn.

segments.name: Services (O&M)
segments.commentary: INR42 crore of order book (3%), no separate commentary on quarterly performance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target retained at about INR600 crore (analyst-reported INR600-700 crore earlier); management said Q1 revenue of about INR103 crore leaves 9 months to deliver INR500-600 crore.
EBITDA margin target of 15-20% for the year, reiterated; management said the gap in Q1 would be made up in coming quarters.
FY27 order inflow expected at INR200-300 crore; management said run rate of INR1,000 crore-plus per year over the next two years.
Export execution targeted at INR150-200 crore in Q2 FY27, with prior-quarter export backlogs expected to clear in the quarter.
Order of INR430 crore (Oct 2025) to be fully executed in FY27 per management, versus earlier guidance of about two-thirds; Q1 execution was about INR21 crore.
Other expenses run-rate of INR9-10 crore per quarter cited as sustainable.
Katepally RDX/HMX water trials expected in September 2026 (about one month); mixing plant dummy trials expected by end September after imported mixer components are airlifted.

Katepally mixing plant: 2.5 tonne planetary mixer installed; imported components delayed by shipping, now being airlifted; dummy trials targeted end-September 2026.
Andhra Pradesh expansion: land pricing unresolved; company has asked the state government to revise price. Management said Apollo would continue the expansion, with a decision after presentation.
Flares produced in own plant; production has started on the July 2023 flares order, with backlog of about INR75 crore to complete in 4-5 months. Chaff payload depends on imports, now executed.
Drones: company builds payloads and partners with drone makers as a partner, not a standalone supplier.

RDX/HMX: international demand good, but licences difficult; management said war-driven demand has lifted prices for now.

Naval opportunity linked to Apollo association; potential to be clearer by December 2026.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said earlier quarters had expected credit loss provisions and forex losses that did not recur; a sustainable run rate of about INR9-10 crore per quarter was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin improve from the 35% level, and what is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will improve as the product mix and dispatches improve; it reiterated the 15-20% EBITDA target and did not quantify a gross margin.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 execution was about INR21 crore, the order will be fully executed in FY27 (not two-thirds), and capacity is available with chaff imports already executed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Defence revenue fall 35%, and was it procurement or acceptance delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to export licence and component import delays, and said customer procurement and acceptance were not a cause; completion expected in Q2 and Q3.

526263|2026-03.headline: Mold-Tek Q4 FY26 PAT turned to INR 2.28 crore from a loss, but FY26 PAT fell 17% to INR 10 crore on a INR 4 crore FX MTM hit.
526263|2026-03.overview: Management reported a Q4 FY26 profit of INR 2.28 crore versus a loss of about INR 1.6 crore a year earlier, despite a roughly INR 4 crore MTM loss from rupee depreciation on forward contracts. Full-year PAT was about INR 10 crore against INR 12.16 crore in FY25, with management citing EBITDA of about INR 20 crore standalone (INR 19.64 crore consolidated) against INR 23 crore a year earlier. Beryl, acquired in November 2025, contributed five months of revenue, and the MES automobile (BIW) team was cut from about 160 to 60 people by end-March. Management reiterated plans to move into structural design and targets of INR 250 crore revenue and 15% EBITDA margin for FY27. Analyst questions were pointed on EBITDA definition, the cancelled preferential issue, receivables and hedging, and several figures were disputed or left for follow-up with the CFO.

segments.name: Civil / Structural (steel detailing and design, India-based, US clients)
segments.commentary: Work on hand grew from about $4 million at start of FY26 to about $5 million at end-March 2026, which management described as growth of about 60-70% versus $2.84 million in June 2024. Structural design is about 10% of civil revenue, versus nearly 0% three to four years ago. Management targets 30-40% of revenue from design in three to four years.

segments.name: MES (Mechanical Engineering Services) - BIW automobile
segments.commentary: Team cut from about 160 to 60 people by end-March; the team was closed from April 1. The segment lost about INR 7-8 crore a year and about INR 1.7-1.9 crore in Q4 FY26. Work on hand fell from about $0.5 million in Q1 to about $0.25 million.

segments.name: MES - Poles, towers and substation (US)
segments.commentary: Team grew from 45-50 to about 80 people. FY26 revenue was about $0.8 million; management expects FY27 to cross $1.5-2 million. Around 80-90% of this work comes from the USA.

segments.name: Beryl (US residential structural design, inspection and permitting; acquired Nov 2025)
segments.commentary: Revenue mix about 80% permitting/inspection and 20% design. Team of about 40 in Tampa with no resignations in five months. Management guided Beryl margin at 8-10% for FY27 and said it can grow to about $5-7 million with India design support.

segments.name: PEMB (Pre-Engineering Metal Buildings)
segments.commentary: Now about 5% of revenue, down from being the core business before 2010.

segments.name: New MSA with Danieli Corus (Delhi, MES manpower)
segments.commentary: Mandate for 20 people; 3 fulfilled so far. Contract period 1-3 years, potential about $0.5 million per annum within a year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR 250 crore, with management saying INR 240 crore is 'easily feasible' from the Q4 run-rate of INR 59 crore (times four).
EBITDA margin to move from about 11% to at least 15%.
Standalone engineering business (MES plus civil from India) expected to grow at least 15-20%, with EBITDA margin in the 15-16% region.
MES cost cut expected to add about INR 7-8 crore back to profitability; productivity target improvement of at least 20% in FY27 (10-15% gain claimed in April).
Nashik office move expected to save about INR 2-2.5 crore per year from FY28; building targeted to be ready by end of FY27.
Hedging policy to be limited to 25-50% of turnover (previously up to 100%); operational EBITDA to be reported separately from MTM gains and losses from FY27.
Salary hike of 8.5-9% provided in Q4 for Indian teams; Beryl not yet covered.
capex_capacity: Team of 40-45 structural designers in India plus 2-3 in the USA; a 6-member Indian team was created for Beryl, with a plan for a 15-20 person India team, targeted by Q4 FY27.
Nashik owned building site acquired a couple of years ago; municipal approvals expected by end of May, ground work in June, completion by end FY27.
Management is in talks for an acquisition of a high-rise steel structural design company; one target is near the Atlanta office. No deal concluded.
Two PEs (professional engineers) certified in more than 20 US states; PE support needed for full member design.
demand_pricing: Civil work on hand up to about $5 million at end-March 2026, against about $4 million at start of the year (per Q4 opening remarks); Q&A figure of $2.5 million at start of year.
Pricing: projects quoted on a fixed-price basis at about $30/hour in India, with 2-3% negotiation; structural design rates about $70-80 per hour versus $25-30 for detailing.
Trade uncertainty between the US and India has stalled Interarch and Mold-Tek building orders in the US; no revenue progress from Interarch or Affordable Robotic Partnership.
BIW automobile demand fell as EV adoption and new model launches slowed; European work was over 50% of MES, while poles and towers are 80-90% US.
Beryl order book estimated at $0.2-0.3 million at any time, maximum about $0.5 million (per management; to be checked).

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 INR 250 crore revenue and 15% EBITDA margin realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 240 crore is easily feasible from Q4 revenue of INR 59 crore annualised, and that margin should rise from 11% to at least 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 2.9 lakh preferential issue at INR 164 cancelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the investor did not transfer funds because the share price had fallen to about INR 130, so the issue lapsed on 30 April against a 31 May deadline. The issue was independent of the Beryl stake purchase. About 30% of acquisition money is held as a three-year retention guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation hit P&L when costs are mainly wages, and what is the hedging policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Forwards booked at INR 85-92 led to about INR 4.9 crore MTM loss in Q4 as rupee moved to about INR 95. Management is cutting hedge cover to 25-50% of turnover and will show MTM separately from operational EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables doubled and revenue rose only about 40%; is the standalone business weakening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 turnover rose 81% YoY, that the rise in debtors reflects this growth, and that acquisitions are strategic rather than a response to weakness. It cited zero debt and INR 25-30 crore of deposits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MES loss and when does it end?
qa_highlights.answer: The MES loss was about INR 1.7-1.9 crore in Q4 and about INR 7-8 crore a year; management said the team was closed from 1 April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What were Beryl's revenue and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Beryl did INR 22.9 crore in the five months since acquisition, including INR 11 crore in Q4 with a loss of about INR 70 lakh. Management said Beryl's seasonal Q4 is typically weak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Danieli Corus MSA and its revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: A manpower MSA in MES with a mandate for 20 people (3 deployed so far), a contract period of 1-3 years, and potential of about $0.5 million per year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY26 Florida SB 4-D inspection tailwind at Beryl ending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first inspection phase is complete and payments received; the second design phase was delayed by a government shutdown and is now restarting, so the tailwind is mid-cycle.

qa_highlights.question: What is the threat from AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI has a limited role in design and detailing, may cut headcount by 5-10% through checking tasks, and that back charges are zero.

526263|2026-09.headline: Mold-Tek H1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose to INR 18.62 crore, about 4.7x the prior-year H1, with standalone Q2 PAT of INR 10.16 crore.

Consolidated H1 PAT was INR 18.62 crore against INR 10 crore for full FY26. Management attributed the gains to product mix, operational efficiency, and higher-value engineering services in poles and towers and structural steel detailing. The BIW segment has been cut sharply, and the Beryl acquisition is still loss-making (about USD 25,000 loss in Q2) with breakeven targeted for Q3.

segments.commentary: Revenue from MES automobile services has fallen to about USD 100,000 in the quarter. BIW headcount was cut from 150-160 to about 50, with a further 5-10 possible reduction and 20-25 people being retrained.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated top-line growth of at least 18-20% and standalone growth of about 20-25% over the next 12-18 months, subject to dollar movements.

Management said US outsourcing of core civil and mechanical engineering will keep growing given local engineer shortages.

The rupee was stabilising around USD 95 per dollar, which management expects to yield forex gains in Q3 if it holds.

526299|2026-03.headline: Mphasis Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7.1% YoY in constant currency to $463 Mn, with record FY26 net new TCV of $2.1 Bn (up 68%).
526299|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was $463 Mn, up 2.5% QoQ and 7.1% YoY in constant currency, with full-year constant-currency growth of 6.7%. Direct revenue was $456 Mn (98.6% of total), growing 9.2% YoY in constant currency. EBIT margin rose 20 bps QoQ to 15.4% in Q4 and was stable at 15.3% for the year, within the 14.75%-15.75% band. Operating cash flow was $21 Mn, or about $38 Mn excluding roughly $17 Mn of delayed customer remittances collected in early April. Management guided FY27 to high single-digit to low double-digit growth and an approximately 80% OCF-to-net-income conversion.

segments.commentary: Direct revenue grew 7.3% QoQ and 46.5% YoY in constant currency, led by AI-driven underwriting, claims and risk use cases.

qa_highlights.answer: Management is fairly confident BFS and Insurance can keep driving growth given pipeline build-up, but did not commit to matching FY26 rates. Logistics is expected to recover gradually through FY27, with one or two large wins able to swing the vertical.

526299|2026-06.headline: Mphasis Q1 FY27 revenue $471M, up 8.3% YoY constant currency; net new TCV $461M; FY27 guidance maintained at high-single to low-double-digit growth.

rows.label: One 91 Thaltej sale value

rows.label: Borrowings rising and debt expected in FY27

526367|2026-06.headline: Ganesh Housing Q1 FY27 revenue rose 86% YoY to Rs 280 crore on One 91 Thaltej land sale, but PAT fell to Rs 42 crore on one-time tax; FY27 guided at Rs 1,000-1,200 crore revenue.
526367|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 280 crore, up 130% QoQ and 86% YoY, driven largely by the One 91 Thaltej land sale plus some completed old-project inventory. EBITDA was Rs 110 crore and PBT about Rs 105 crore, while PAT was Rs 42 crore because the land carried a higher tax cost from a 2020 amalgamation. Management guided FY27 revenue of Rs 1,000-1,200 crore and PAT of Rs 300-325 crore, with Million Minds lease rentals starting in Q4 FY27. Management said the Thaltej sale was a capital-allocation choice rather than a liquidity need, but did not disclose buyer, consideration or margin details.

financial_highlights.change: Lower QoQ and YoY due to one-time tax on Thaltej land sale
Management said up about 10% or roughly flat

segments.name: One 91 Thaltej (land monetisation)
segments.commentary: Land sold during Q1 rather than developed; management called it a project sale and said the transaction is complete. Consideration and buyer (a listed entity) were not disclosed; management indicated the Rs 500-600 crore land component of FY27 revenue includes Thaltej and Godhavi.

segments.name: Malabar Retreat (residential)
segments.commentary: Construction about 83% complete; 73 units booked, about 45% of units and Rs 183 crore, about 45% of sale value. Sale value above Rs 450 crore; no revenue recognised yet in Q1 as project is incomplete.

segments.name: Million Minds (commercial leasing)
segments.commentary: Phase-I inaugurated; fit-out in final stages. LOIs executed for about 43% (2.64 lakh sq ft) of leasable area, with a further 15-20% under negotiation; lease rentals to start in Q4 FY27. Management said FY28 rentals could exceed Rs 75 crore.

segments.name: Godhavi land (411 acres)
segments.commentary: Planned as a township mixing development, plotted development and land sales; possible monetisation towards later part of FY27, with details not yet worked out.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at Rs 1,000-1,200 crore and PAT at Rs 300-325 crore; management said PAT could rise about 10% or be flat given the Q1 one-time tax.
Million Minds lease rentals to start in Q4 FY27; full-year rentals expected in FY28.
Million Minds Phase-II launch expected in Q3 FY27; Million Minds residential Phase-I launch expected in Q4 FY27.
Management expects most FY27 revenue to be realised in cash within the year, with cash flows of about Rs 700-1,000 crore cited; GDV and cash-flow disclosure may be added going forward.
FY28 guidance not given; management indicated it may update in Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 510 acres fully paid, including 411 acres at Godhavi and 65 acres at Million Minds.
Million Minds long-term development potential of about 15 million sq ft (stated as 15 billion sq ft in the call; likely a transcription error).
Million Minds Phase-I built entirely from internal accruals; management said Thaltej monetisation adds cash for land purchases and Million Minds.
Million Minds Phase-II and residential Phase-I launches are scheduled for Q3 and Q4 FY27 respectively.
Several new land acquisitions are under discussion and not in the current land bank.
demand_pricing: Million Minds demand is coming from GCCs, technology companies and managed co-working operators; only SEZ portions remain to be leased, with full leasing expected in two to three months.
Malabar Retreat booking pace is about 45% of units and value, indicating healthy premium residential demand in Ahmedabad.

Margin compression on Thaltej was attributed to a higher land cost base from the 2020 amalgamation rather than to pricing; management said quarterly margins should be viewed in the context of project life cycle and IndAS 115 revenue recognition.
Management said the Thaltej land sale was worth more on a present-value basis than developing a commercial building over about five years (three years construction plus two years sales).

qa_highlights.question: Has the Thaltej land sale been completed, and is the full payment realised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the sale is complete and Q1 numbers include it, but declined to disclose consideration, rate or payment status until the listed buyer is ready to disclose.

qa_highlights.question: How much of FY27 revenue of Rs 1,000-1,200 crore is land sale versus project revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would classify most revenue as project sales. Excluding those, it cited about Rs 550-600 crore from land and about Rs 470 crore from projects, including the Rs 700 crore of project sales from Malabar Retreat and completed projects.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Thaltej land sold and why did margins fall to about 39%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the sale was a present-versus-future value decision rather than a liquidity need. Margins were lower because the land cost from the amalgamation was higher, and the one-time tax was elevated by the same cost basis.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose GDV and cash flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will reflect cash flows and GDV going forward, with cash flows being the more important metric; an offline discussion was offered for the FY27 numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for Godhavi and Smile City?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said monetisation could come towards the later part of FY27, but details are not worked out given fluid developments in the area.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the cash generated from the sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash will fund land purchases in Ahmedabad and Million Minds development, which is being funded from internal accruals.

risks_watch: Thaltej sale consideration, buyer and margin remain undisclosed; a later disclosure is expected.
Million Minds rentals depend on closing the remaining 15-20% of leasable area under negotiation and on starting rentals in Q4 FY27.
FY27 PAT guidance (Rs 300-325 crore) relies on a large Q2-Q4 contribution after a Rs 42 crore Q1 PAT.
Revenue recognition for Malabar Retreat depends on construction completion, and the project is about 83% complete.
Godhavi monetisation timing and plans are still open.
526367|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and Million Minds leasing, but guarded on specifics: management repeatedly declined to disclose Thaltej sale value and buyer details and deferred FY28 guidance. Tone was defensive on the margin and tax questions, attributing them to a one-time amalgamation tax effect.
key_quotes: We got a compelling offer to sell this land rather than developing it and taking the risk of both construction and sale of this multi-storied building over the next five years.

Monetization land under favorable market conditions enables us to accelerate cash generation, strengthen liquidity, and redeploy capital into opportunities that can deliver superior long-term returns.
Approvals and all were not the issue. Project by itself was not the issue, it was purely the present versus future possibilities that led to deciding that we should sell.
Yes, we are hopeful that Godhavi land and also developments therein should be there towards the later part of this year.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Land bank of 510 acres is fully paid and several new land acquisitions are under discussion, funded by Thaltej sale cash, but no specific capex amount or project has been announced and utilisation is not a metric disclosed for this developer.

rows.why: Million Minds Phase-II launch is guided for Q3 FY27 and Million Minds residential Phase-I for Q4 FY27, both with a plan behind them.

rows.why: Monetisation could come towards the later part of FY27, but management said details are not worked out given fluid developments in the area.

526367|2026-09.headline: Ganesh Housing Q2 FY27 PAT rose to INR67 crores on INR121 crores land-sale revenue; FY27 guidance of INR1,000-1,200 crores revenue reaffirmed.
526367|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR121 crores, all from project land sales, with EBITDA of INR98 crores (80.7% margin) and PAT of INR67 crores (EPS INR8.02), up 59% QoQ but slightly lower YoY against a high base of INR174 crores revenue and INR108 crores PAT. Management attributed the QoQ margin swing to Q1 carrying a high-cost inherited land basis and a one-time tax charge on the One 91 Thaltej land sale. H1 revenue was about INR402 crores, EBITDA INR208 crores and PAT about INR109 crores, and management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of INR1,000-1,200 crores revenue and INR300-325 crores PAT, which depends on H2 completions and land sales. Million Minds Tower 1 leasing reached 68.4% of leasable carpet area, and Malabar Retreat is 87% complete with possession targeted for 15 January 2027.

financial_highlights.change: Lower YoY vs INR174 crores in Q2 FY26
Margin up from 39.3% in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: INR67 crores, 55.1% PAT margin, EPS INR8.02
financial_highlights.change: Up 59% QoQ from INR42 crores; down YoY from INR108 crores

financial_highlights.metric: Contracted rent roll, Million Minds Tower 1

financial_highlights.value: INR132 crores; expected receivables booked and unbooked INR305 crores

segments.name: Land sales / project sales
segments.commentary: Entire Q2 FY27 revenue of INR121 crores came from project land sales; company says reported quarterly revenue depends on project completion under Ind AS 115.

segments.name: Million Minds Tower 1 (leasing)
segments.commentary: 68.4% of leasable carpet area let across 15 deals; 4.21 lakh sq ft let of 6.16 lakh sq ft. Average rent INR110.20/sq ft per month; latest deals at about INR122.4. Lease rentals expected from Q4 FY27; fully let rent potential about INR84 crores a year.

segments.name: Malabar Retreat (residential)
segments.commentary: 87% complete; about 50% of units booked (76 units; 53% by carpet area). Priced at top of micro market with no discounting; possession intimation 15 January 2027, BU expected mid-February 2027.

segments.name: Million Minds Phase 2 (Tower 2)
segments.commentary: Plan of 6.6 lakh sq ft leasable carpet on about 14.5 lakh sq ft construction submitted for approval; target rent about INR118/sq ft, implying about INR94 crores annual rent at full occupancy. Bhumi Pujan targeted 24 November 2026.

segments.name: Million Minds residential Phase 1
segments.commentary: About 9 lakh sq ft, around 334 units (3 BHK), two towers; expected GDV INR500 crores; launch planned Q4 FY27, timeline 2 to 2.5 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,000-1,200 crores and PAT of INR300-325 crores reaffirmed; H2 expected to be much stronger, with Malabar Retreat completion and other project and land sales in Q3-Q4.
Management expects Malabar Retreat to sell about 75% (possibly nearly all) of unsold units by March 2027.
Tower 1 rentals to begin from Q4 FY27; expects about 90% of Tower 1 let by March 2027.
FY28 year-on-year guidance to be given in Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
Godhavi monetization plan (mix of plotted development, land sales and project development) to be updated later in FY27; company now expects about 6 more months for concrete plans.
RERA timeline for Malabar Retreat runs to September 2027; company aims to complete about 6 months early.
capex_capacity: Million Minds Tower 1: final-stage fit-outs and landscaping; lease rentals from Q4 FY27.

Million Minds Tower 2: 18-24 month build, fit-out-ready window May-November 2028, pre-leasing from late 2027; company also cited 24-28 months in call. Construction approval pending; contractor appointed for civil work.
Malabar Retreat: about 87% complete, with about 13% remaining; soft possession 15 January 2027, BU mid-February 2027.

Fully paid land reserve of 513 acres (about 405 acres at Godhavi, about 65 acres at Million Minds, balance around Ahmedabad); new large parcels under negotiation/acquisition with partial payments made, not included in 513 acres.

Planned Million Minds SEZ: 64 acres, about 18 million sq ft across 7 office phases plus residential, retail (mall about 4.5 lakh sq ft), hotel/convention (about 5 lakh sq ft) and service apartments; about 63,000 jobs at maturity.
demand_pricing: Malabar Retreat: about 76 units booked (50% by units, 53% by carpet area); about 30-40 units sold in last 4 months per management; priced at top of micro market with no discounts.
Tower 1 rents rose from about INR90/sq ft (2025 leases) to about INR115 (2026) to above INR122 (Q2 deals); building average INR110.20/sq ft.
Co-working concentration fell: three operators held 28.7% of space let, versus about 36% a quarter earlier; all three new Q2 deals are direct corporate tenants.
Q2 Tower 1 leases: LOIs/leases with Airtel, Conga Software, Flagler Health and iBase-t; new deals about 84,000 sq ft; contracted leases 9 to 10 years with 5-year lock-in for most.
Ahmedabad housing: 14,300 units sold in 9 months to September 2026 (up 2%); weighted average price INR4,837/sq ft (up 3.7%); unsold inventory about 38,700 units.

qa_highlights.question: Where will H2 revenue of INR600-800 crores come from, given Malabar Retreat's unsold inventory and minimal rent in FY27? Also what are lock-in, rent-free and deposit terms for new tenants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the H2 gap would be filled by Malabar Retreat completion plus pipeline project and land sales expected in Q3, or by Q4 at latest. Leases are mostly 9-10 years with 5-year-plus lock-ins; rent-free and deposit terms were not detailed in the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned split of the 405-acre Godhavi land between plotted development, land sales and project development, and when will monetization be announced?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix not yet finalized and depends on infrastructure around Godhavi; management now expects about 6 more months before concrete monetization plans are announced.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Malabar Retreat sales velocity low despite no discounting, and what is the plan for the unsold half?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the market has been in a lull for 3-4 quarters with premium units selling most; bookings picked up with 30-40 units in the last 4 months; rainy-season slowdown was also cited. Target is to sell nearly all, or at least 75%, by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Size, pricing, GDV, approval status and funding timing for Million Minds residential Phase 1?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9 lakh sq ft, around 334 3 BHK units across 2 towers, GDV about INR500 crores, timeline 2-2.5 years, launch Q4 FY27. Approval status and SEZ versus non-SEZ split were not clearly answered.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund the projects and what peak debt is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will take some leverage but not at historical ratios; existing borrowings are against discounted lease rentals, and residential projects are funded by bookings and already-paid land, with land monetization and lease rentals as further cash sources. No peak-debt figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Tower 2 approvals, Tower 1 original versus actual schedule, and why Tower 2 target rent (INR118) is below Tower 1 (INR122)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called INR118 conservative and said it could reach INR130-140/sq ft. Bhumi Pujan on 24 November needs no approval; construction start depends on approvals in process. Schedule was not compared to Tower 1's original timeline in detail.

qa_highlights.question: Malabar Retreat progress: how can the remaining 13% be completed by 15 January possession and mid-February BU?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said external facade is about 90% done, MEP about 60-70%, and painting has started on one tower; remaining work is shorter than the initial construction phase. Soft possession 15 January and BU mid-February are on track; RERA deadline is September 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Tower 1 leasing went from 43% to about 68%; how does this reconcile with only 84,000 sq ft added this quarter, and will LOIs and signed leases be reported separately?
qa_highlights.answer: 43% earlier plus 17% under discussion became signed deals, so the 68% figure reflects completed signings only. Remaining space is for large negotiations. Separate reporting of LOIs versus leases was not committed.

risks_watch: H2 revenue gap: guidance of INR1,000-1,200 crores needs H2 revenue of roughly INR600-800 crores; management relies on Malabar Retreat completion (BU mid-February 2027) plus land and project sales in Q3 or by Q4, with no named transactions.
Malabar Retreat sales velocity: about 50% sold by units, with 30-40 units booked in the last 4 months; target of 75% or nearly all unsold units by March 2027 needs to be tracked against bookings.
Million Minds Tower 1: 68.4% let versus 90% target by March 2027; remaining about 1.95 lakh sq ft held for one or two large tenants, and rentals start Q4 FY27.
Tower 2 timing: construction approval still pending while Bhumi Pujan is set for 24 November 2026; the 18-24 month build and May-November 2028 fit-out window depend on approvals.
Rising rate environment: RBI repo hike to 5.5% on 7 October 2026 and a tightening stance; management plans some leverage for Tower 2 and residential projects, with no peak-debt figure given.
Godhavi monetization plan delayed about 6 months to an update later in FY27; FY28 guidance due in Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
key_quotes: We expect a much different and better performance during H2 and hence, our guidance which we have given in Q1 this year for FY27 of INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores revenue and INR300 crores to INR325 crores PAT is reaffirmed.
Our balance sheet, on the other hand, is almost debt free. So a rate cycle that squeezes others gives us room to be selective.
We should be honest that in a market with such kind of a supply, pre -leased Grade A space is what wins.
The leverage, we have always said that we have been a near zero debt company for a long period of time.
526367|2026-09.management_tone: Management was confident on the project pipeline, Tower 1 leasing and Malabar Retreat timelines, but cautious and vague on H2 revenue sources, Godhavi timing and debt levels. Several answers were non-specific on land sale names, peak debt and LOI reporting.

526371|2026-03.headline: NMDC guides FY27 production to 60 million tonnes and FY27 capex to about INR6,000 crore, with Q1 FY27 output up about 15% YoY.
526371|2026-03.overview: NMDC reported FY26 production above 50 million tonnes and an 11% PAT rise despite sluggish prices, with management citing a record capex of about INR3,300 crore. Management guided FY27 production to 60 million tonnes, with the first two months of Q1 FY27 about 15% higher YoY at roughly 10 million tonnes. New iron ore (Deposit 4, Deposit 13) and coal (Tokisud, Rohne) assets are being commissioned, and a INR3,000 crore blending yard at Vizag is sanctioned. The EBITDA margin was 33% group-level, down from 42%, due to a one-time HR coil trading arrangement with NMDC Steel; standalone iron ore EBITDA was stated at 42%.

segments.name: Iron ore (NMDC standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone EBITDA margin at 42%, with FY27 guided at 42-43%. Kirandul FY26 about 21 million tonnes (to ~30 million by decade-end); Bacheli about 18-19 million tonnes (to ~35 million).

segments.name: NMDC Steel (NSL)
segments.commentary: NSL has turned profitable; the HR coil trading in the last quarter was a one-time cash-flow support and is not expected in Q1 FY27. NSL dues are being recovered at about INR100 crore per month, with full liquidation in 16-18 months (pre-demerger dues about INR2,500 crore, now about INR1,800 crore).

segments.name: Coal
segments.commentary: Tokisud (2.3 million tonnes peak, thermal, opened) targets 0.75-1 million tonnes in FY27 from Q2; Rohne (8 million tonnes peak coking coal) opens around end-Q3 FY27 with no FY27 production. Management expects INR500-600 crore revenue per 1 million tonnes at G10 grade, at 30-40% EBITDA (approximate).

segments.name: Pellets (KIOCL)
segments.commentary: KIOCL 3 million tonne job-work plant: FY26 about 2.4 million tonnes; FY27 target 3-3.3 million tonnes. Pellet grade achieved 66.5% Fe; targeting 67% DR-grade with a $20-30/t premium.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at 60 million tonnes including NSL, built from Deposit 14 (+1 mt), NMZ (+1 mt), Kumaraswamy (+~3.3 mt), Deposit 5 (+2 mt to 12 mt), plus Deposit 4 (~1 mt) and Deposit 13 (~0.5 mt).
Deposit 4 expected to start commercial mining in Q2 FY27: about 1 mt in FY27, 2 mt in FY28, and 7 mt peak rated capacity after 1.5-2 more years.
Deposit 13 start targeted around Q2 FY27 after pending clearances: under 0.5 mt in FY27, about 2 mt next year, 10 mt initial peak rising to 20-21 mt in 4-5 years.
Capex guidance: about INR6,000 crore in FY27 (range INR6,000-7,000 crore); INR7,000-10,000 crore per year over the next 2-3 years; INR40,000-50,000 crore over 3 years to reach 100 mt.
Overseas critical mineral and mineral asset acquisitions: INR2,000-3,000 crore expected in FY27; a couple of overseas assets targeted this year.
Management reiterated a 100 million tonne target by end of decade and said the 60 mt FY27 guidance is achievable without the railway doubling, but 100 mt requires it.
No immediate plans to leverage the balance sheet; internal accruals expected to fund capex and acquisitions, with debt possible late FY27 only for large global acquisitions.
Iron ore prices expected to stay range-bound in FY27; monthly price calls to be taken.
capex_capacity: Railway: 131 km doubling; two sections remaining, one by end of June 2026 and the Bhansi-Bacheli section by December 2026; evacuation capacity to rise from 28-30 mt to ~40 mt, with 60 mt+ after doubling beyond Jagdalpur.
Slurry pipeline (15 mt, Bacheli to Nagarnar), Nagarnar pellet plant and Bacheli grinding mill in pre-commissioning; commissioning expected by end-June or mid-July 2026.
EC capacity 64.8 mt vs CTO ~55.4 mt; CTO enhancement sought in three places to ~58.8 mt. All mines reached EC capacity as of 1 April 2026 (Deposit 5 the exception in FY26).
Deposit 5 downhill conveyor and bottleneck fix due June-July 2026, enabling 12 mt. New infrastructure at Deposit 14, NMZ, 11 and 11C takes about 1.5 years, adding 5-6 mt.
INR3,000 crore blending yard at Vizag (board sanctioned, ~2-2.5 year build); Vizag land parcel ~1,100 acres; pellet plant at Vizag on drawing board, pending slurry pipeline route decision.
Expansion works (~INR15,000-20,000 crore worth of major tenders) expected to be awarded by end-June or July 2026.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is not a constraint even at 100 mt, citing JSW, AMNS (10 mt plant near Vizag, 17 mt total), JSPL and NSL expansions; NMDC's phosphorus content of 0.05% is a claimed differentiator.

Iron ore prices expected range-bound in Q1 FY27 after steel prices peaked Dec-Feb and stabilised in March-April; the company sets prices monthly, citing international prices, competitor prices and logistics, not a direct steel-price link.
RINL consumes 7-8 mt per year; bills discounted at ~10% premium with a 45-day payment lag; no recourse to NMDC in FY25 or FY26.
Blended/branded iron ore (Vizag) planned as a premium product; exports unattractive given 30% export duty, so pellets are preferred for export.
Iron ore realisation slightly down ~2% per an analyst question; no quantified FY27 realisation guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Mine-wise bridge to 60 mt FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit 14 +1 mt, NMZ +1 mt, Kumaraswamy +~3.3 mt (MPAP relief from 8.6 mt), Deposit 5 +2 mt (to 12 mt), totalling ~5.3 mt; plus Deposit 4 (~1 mt) and Deposit 13 (~0.5 mt) gives ~60 mt including NSL.

qa_highlights.question: Coal mine economics and grade?

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is about 85% (main sectors 90-95%) and capacity additions are planned in Mumbai, South, East and North, though none are quantified and the Gurugram facility is already commissioned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY26 tonnage grew about 7.1% to about 1,439,000 tons but Q4 slowed to about 4.6% YoY at 359,913 tons, management declined to give FY27 volume colour, and surface volume growth was slower than FY25.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 85% and automation (sorters, MHE) plus planned capacity additions are flagged, but management gave no new capex figure and said no new line-of-business expansion is planned; recurring aircraft maintenance capex is INR 100-150 crore a year.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal FY27 volume or margin guidance was given, management declined forward-looking colour, and Q4 PBT fell about 17%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

526612|2026-06.headline: Blue Dart Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR1,658 crore (from INR1,442 crore) and PAT reached INR87 crore, driven mainly by yield and fuel surcharge rather than volume.
526612|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR1,658 crore against INR1,442 crore a year earlier, with PAT of INR87 crore. Management attributed growth mainly to pricing: GPI-led increases, targeted repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery after diesel and Brent prices rose from around March–May. Tonnage grew about 7% to 364,430 tons and shipments about 2% to 96.15 million, with air volume up about 2.6% and surface up about 9%. Management declined to quantify yield growth or give forward volume and margin guidance, citing seasonality and H2 resourcing challenges.

segments.name: Air
segments.commentary: About 60% of revenue but about 25% of kilos (1:3 air:surface by weight). Volume growth about 2.6%; growth is mainly yield-led. Freighter pallet utilisation 85–90%.

segments.name: Surface / Ground
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue and about 75% of kilos. Volume up about 9%; B2B revenue up about 14%. Management says surface is the faster-growing segment and is approaching air in size.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Revenue up more than 10% YoY. Management says about 50-plus million of the 96.15 million shipments are e-commerce, and Blue Dart holds about 12–13% of outsourced/3PL e-commerce.

segments.name: B2B vs B2C
segments.commentary: Revenue mix about 70% B2B and 30% B2C (plus or minus 2%).

segments.name: BFSI (documents and cards)
segments.commentary: BFSI alone is about 10–15% of total revenue; documents plus cards together, including small parcels, about 25–30%. Management says BFSI is no longer a growing segment.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance. Management said it will not forecast volumes, citing seasonality, but expects Q2 to reflect the full fuel-surcharge increase from May onward.
Typical GPI realisation is about 4–5%, with extra customer-specific corrections on top.

Standalone annualised capex guided at INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Aviation capex is driven by maintenance and engine cycles, with roughly 20–25% of depreciation as ongoing capex.
H2 is expected to bring higher volumes, but resourcing flex will determine margins; management aims for stable, consistent margin improvement.
No major expansion plans; growth is expected to be organic. Possible consolidation and expansion of southern hubs (Bangalore, Chennai) and Mumbai, a few quarters away.
capex_capacity: Two major hubs added in North and a couple of medium-sized hubs in East in the prior period.
Freighter pallet utilisation at 85–90%; aircraft flown mainly at night and scheduled against available load.
Belly cargo is 30–40% of overall load in a typical month, and can reach 70–80% on lower-volume weekends. Blue Dart flies to 8 stations and carries belly cargo at 25–50 other locations.
The two aircraft acquired earlier are back to pre-acquisition pallet utilisation (as of 2024) and are integrated into the network.
demand_pricing: Growth came mainly from pricing: GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge pass-through. Management said yield was 'directionally' the main driver of revenue growth.
Fuel surcharge on surface is revised monthly based on local diesel prices, which rose in mid-May after about 5–6 years. Air fuel surcharge rose from April as Brent climbed from around mid-March.
Auto is a niche express vertical; management estimates it grows at about high-teens, in line with surface B2B. Market share is hard to quantify.
Management says e-commerce pricing remains competitive, with capacity still available in the market; Blue Dart positions itself as a premium player.
Management says it gained a very small but roughly stable market share in SME clients versus last year (informal assessment).

qa_highlights.question: Is the revenue growth mainly from pricing, given volume growth was only about 7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed directionally. Pricing came from GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery (fuel surcharge offset fuel cost rises, which also lifted yield).

qa_highlights.question: Why is e-commerce growth lower than the industry, and is it a focus area?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce is a growth driver but not a mass-volume focus. It is prioritising premium, time-critical traffic that fits its capacity, and it is not targeting the largest e-commerce share.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and new hubs?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone annualised capex is INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Two major northern hubs and some medium eastern hubs were added, and southern and Mumbai hub consolidation is being considered a few quarters away.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins, and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 brings volume opportunity but also resourcing challenges. It aims to keep or improve margins through efficiency and better realisation, without quantifying either.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2 recently acquired aircraft stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said pallet utilisation was restored to pre-acquisition levels by 2024. The aircraft are part of the wider network, and capacity is not a constraint; yield is the main lever.

risks_watch: Growth quality: about 7% tonnage growth against about 15% revenue growth implies most of the increase came from pricing and surcharges, which may not persist.
Fuel: diesel and Brent rises were passed through with a lag; Q2 is expected to show the full surcharge effect, but any fall in fuel prices would reverse it.
Air volume growth of about 2.6% versus surface about 9% suggests air is stagnating in volume.
H2 resourcing: management flagged that peak-season flex will decide margins.
Competition in e-commerce pricing remains intense, with spare capacity in the market.
BFSI (documents and cards) is no longer growing, and the 25–30% documents-plus-parcels exposure needs monitoring.
Management declined to provide e-commerce split by air and surface, D2C share, or yield premium figures, limiting visibility.
526612|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's numbers and direction, but guarded on forward-looking detail: it declined to quantify yield, the e-commerce premium, and market share, and repeatedly deferred to seasonality rather than guiding.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1,442 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +15%)

key_quotes: This seems to be a good quarter where what we have kind of put ourselves for seems to be bringing positive indications in terms of numbers moving in the right direction.

Blue Dart has been, I would say, focused on not playing on the volumes, but ensuring what we get as a piece from e-commerce works well to synergize with our capacities and adds profitability to the bottom line.

Iin short, from a capacity utilization, that has never been a challenge. It's a question of what kind of product that goes in, how critical or important it is for the customer to be able to pay the premium that ensures the profitability of the overall network.
So the effort will be to maintain or improve further. But we seem to be on the right path is what I would say.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Tonnage grew about 7% and shipments about 2%, with air volume only about 2.6% and surface about 9%; management expects higher H2 volumes but will not forecast them.

rows.why: Freighter pallet utilisation is 85-90%, which is high, but the call guides only INR100-150 crore annualised capex and a possible southern/Mumbai hub consolidation a few quarters away, with no new plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no formal guidance and declined to forecast volumes or margins, citing seasonality and H2 resourcing challenges.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Growth is mainly price and fuel-surcharge led (about 15% revenue vs about 7% tonnage), which may not persist if fuel falls, and e-commerce pricing is competitive with spare market capacity.

rows.why: No new products, brands or service launches were discussed.

rows.label: Fuel surcharge full-quarter effect in Q2
rows.why: Management expects Q2 to reflect the full fuel-surcharge increase from May onward, after diesel rose in mid-May and Brent climbed from mid-March.

rows.why: Typical GPI realisation is about 4-5%, with extra customer-specific corrections and repricing of loss-making lanes on top, which drove most of the 15% revenue growth against 7% tonnage.

rows.why: E-commerce revenue grew more than 10% and Blue Dart holds about 12-13% of outsourced/3PL e-commerce, but pricing is competitive with spare market capacity and no split was disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on the quarter's numbers and pricing-led growth but cautious on forward detail, declining to quantify yield, e-commerce premium, market share, volumes or margins and deferring to seasonality and H2 resourcing.

526668|2026-03.headline: Kamat Hotels Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 19% YoY to INR 110 crore, with EBITDA margin at 29%, and FY26 revenue INR 386 crore (+8%).
526668|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of about INR 110 crore (+19% YoY), EBITDA of INR 32 crore (29% margin, +213 bps) and PAT of INR 18 crore (+59% YoY, 16% margin). For FY26, revenue was INR 386 crore (+8%), EBITDA INR 97 crore (25.1% margin) and PAT INR 39 crore (10.1% margin). Brand-level ARR and occupancy fell YoY because new hotels are still ramping up, and IRA Mumbai (a leased property, about INR 50 crore revenue) has been vacated from 31 March 2026. Management guided to a cautious outlook, did not give FY27 top-line guidance, and announced Milind Wadekar as incoming CFO.

financial_highlights.change: Management cited ~4% compression FY25 to FY26 when questioned
Includes ~INR 3 crore income tax refund, rent, and INR 5 crore Ilex loan repayment with interest; breakdown promised

segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 50 crore revenue and about INR 20 crore EBITDA; management says EBITDA impact after closure is positive by INR 1-2 crore. Property was vacated after the owner ended the lease from 31 March 2026.

segments.name: Fort Jadhavgadh
segments.commentary: Occupancy and ARR fell sharply YoY (management referenced a 26% dip in the call); management attributed this to leadership change and sales-strategy issues, expects better FY27, and says the property is profitable.

segments.commentary: Ramping up after an initial slow period; management says it is now doing exceedingly well through OTA and web channels.

segments.commentary: Management estimated about INR 10 crore EBITDA drag from pre-opening and ramp-up costs, of which about INR 6 crore should be absorbed through operations; about 250-260 keys were added in FY26. Chandigarh delivered INR 14 crore revenue in FY26 against an INR 20-22 crore target.

guidance_outlook: Management is cautiously optimistic and pragmatic on volumes, with focus on domestic demand; no FY27 top-line growth guidance given (explicitly declined to speculate).

Expects to operationalise at least 150-200 keys in FY27 (based on current pipeline).
IRA by Orchid Bhavnagar expected to open by June 2026; Orchid Dehradun estimated for September 2026 (already delayed).

Labour cost target about 20-23% of revenue for matured hotels.
Management reports no additional payroll burden from absorbing IRA Mumbai staff.

demand_pricing: Wedding and domestic MICE demand described as very good; majority domestic client base limited exposure to foreign travel disruption.

Chandigarh was hit last year by airport closure; management expects improved performance this year.
Orchid Passaros child-free positioning is seeing rising advance enquiries, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ARR and occupancy fall YoY at IRA and Fort Jadhavgadh, and will EBITDA and PAT be lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said brand-level metrics fell because of new hotels with a wider base; Jadhavgadh had a mid-year slump, and a strategy change is under way. Management said the current EBITDA already reflects this, with gains expected next year as hotels mature.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IRA Mumbai contribution, and how will it be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IRA Mumbai contributed about INR 50 crore revenue and about INR 20 crore EBITDA, and that the exit is roughly EBITDA-positive by INR 1-2 crore. Replacement will come from maturing hotels, new openings and tie-ups.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 4% EBITDA compression, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wage code revisions add about INR 4 crore, which is permanent. About INR 2 crore is a one-time IRA closure payout, and newer hotels' payroll costs should be absorbed as they mature.

qa_highlights.question: Why are finance costs around INR 10 crore while borrowings fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not answer on the call and promised a follow-up. Other income of about INR 10 crore includes rent, interest from group companies, a INR 5 crore Ilex loan repayment and about INR 3 crore tax refund; a breakdown was promised.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 top line grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance, but acknowledged the INR 50 crore IRA loss would reduce top line unless offset by other properties.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA drag from new properties and how many keys were added?
qa_highlights.answer: About 250-260 keys were added in FY26. The EBITDA drag is about INR 10 crore, of which about INR 6 crore should be absorbed into the gross operating profit (GOP) in the next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why hold INR 40 crore of cash rather than prepay debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers to hold cash as a contingency buffer rather than prepay the INR 86 crore loan at 9.75%, given the risk of shocks.

risks_watch: Top-line base falls by about INR 50 crore after IRA Mumbai exit; FY27 growth depends on ramp-up of new keys.
Fort Jadhavgadh occupancy and ARR recovery after strategy change; the company did not disclose a target occupancy.
Project delays (Dehradun, Gwalior, Nashik) linked to LPG-driven material shortages and owner-led timelines.
Recurring wage code cost increase and labour cost inflation.
Other income of about INR 10 crore and finance cost of about INR 10 crore queried but not fully explained; breakdown promised.
Transition to new CFO Milind Wadekar.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company take price hikes given flat Orchid ARR?

526668|2026-09.headline: Kamat Hotels Q2 FY27 EBITDA more than doubled to Rs 22 crore, margin up 13 pts to 26% on revenue of Rs 86 crore (+12%).
526668|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs 86 crore and EBITDA rose 131% to Rs 22 crore, with margin at 26%, while PAT turned to Rs 5 crore from a Rs 2 crore loss a year earlier. H1 revenue was Rs 179 crore (+11%), EBITDA above Rs 50 crore (+67%) at 28% margin, and PAT Rs 15 crore. Same-store revenue rose 31% after excluding IRA Mumbai, Orchid Shimla and IRA Bhavnagar. Net debt to EBITDA fell to 0.23x from 0.52x, and Rs 30 crore of Axis Finance debt was repaid after quarter end. Management guided to a stronger H2 and a FY30 expansion plan of 31 properties and 3,000 keys.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of Rs 2 crore in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Portfolio (occupancy and ADR)
segments.commentary: Portfolio occupancy rose from 50% to 58% while ADR was flat at about 3% growth; RevPAR up about 20% per management. Pune Orchid revenue grew 32%.

segments.name: IRA by Orchid
segments.commentary: Weaker ARR and RevPAR, mainly because IRA Mumbai (high occupancy, good rate) left the portfolio after lease ended 31 March 2026. Excluding IRA Mumbai, RevPAR was Rs 2,337 in Q2 FY27 vs Rs 2,477 in Q2 FY26; H1 Rs 2,472 vs Rs 2,423 (wording as stated in call).

segments.commentary: Both show negative EBITDA in H1 but management called the amount insignificant; positive EBITDA expected in the next two quarters. Stabilisation takes about one year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 to be the strongest half, with revenue and EBITDA growth above last year's H2 and continued rate and occupancy gains.
Q2 is typically 60-65% of annual business; management expects FY27 to be robust, citing an encouraging October and a strong second half of November.
Indicative: if H2 EBITDA is 60% of the full year, FY27 EBITDA could cross Rs 130-135 crore (FY26 was about Rs 100 crore). Management said it does not want to give forward-looking numbers.
Net debt to be zero by year-end FY27, per the CFO.

capex_capacity: Pipeline about 620 keys across seven properties; expansion to be within existing states unless financially attractive.
Management model is a flat 6% of top line; lease or revenue-share deals only for properties of roughly 80-100 rooms, management contracts from about 40-45 rooms.

CFO estimates about Rs 750 crore cumulative EBITDA over five years (about Rs 600 crore after tax available for growth) and about Rs 1,000 crore total expansion capacity including debt headroom, on a lower-side basis.
Electric kitchens and an all-EV hotel fleet were capex-heavy decisions that management says helped during LPG/PNG disruption.
demand_pricing: Q2 demand came mainly from corporate for business hotels and leisure for leisure properties; MICE demand described as intact.
Goa (Orchid Passaros) showed strong demand, with a high share of foreign guests.
Wedding season weaker than last year but supportive of weekday and weekend demand.
Management said the focus is on RevPAR over ADR; rates to rise as occupancy picks up, with Pune Orchid ADR expected to jump in Q3 and Q4.
Ayodhya occupancy took a small hit in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 26% EBITDA margin and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: ADR flat at about 3% but occupancy rose 50% to 58%; higher volume with fixed costs drove margin gains, plus Pune (revenue +32%), Bhubaneswar and cost efficiencies. Management said margins are sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 revenue growth driven by occupancy, ARR or new properties?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: H2 is the strongest period; rates and occupancy are both expected to rise, lifting top line and EBITDA. No split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is IRA by Orchid weaker on ARR and RevPAR?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman: new hotels dilute averages and mature markets such as Sambhaji Nagar and Nashik are growing slowly. CFO: the drop is mainly IRA Mumbai leaving the portfolio; ex-Mumbai RevPAR was broadly flat, with a small Ayodhya dip.

qa_highlights.question: When will new properties such as Bhavnagar and Rishikesh stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: about one year to stabilise; H1 EBITDA is slightly negative but not significant; positive EBITDA expected in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expansion pipeline and EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman declined to name specifics, citing negotiations; expansion limited to existing states with internal norms. CFO gave indicative numbers: FY27 EBITDA of about Rs 130-135 crore if H2 is 60%, and about Rs 1,000 crore of expansion capacity over three years.

qa_highlights.question: Which models will expansion use and what are the economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman: management contracts at a flat 6% of top line (GOP-linked fees dropped), above 40-45 rooms; leases only for 80-100+ room hotels because GST at 18% is a cost for smaller hotels; revenue share as an exception.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the royalty payable to Plaza on the Mumbai hotel up from 3% to 5%, and will it be cut, given the interest-free deposit?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: royalty is about Rs 9 crore a year at 6% on Rs 150 crore revenue, compared with about Rs 35 crore finance cost on a Rs 300-350 crore land value; a merger with the promoter entity is being evaluated but is not yet decided. Chairman: the 1994 arrangement is not to be changed, and the board will decide.

qa_highlights.question: How did demand and ARR evolve across segments, and when will rates improve?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: outlook robust; Q2 demand was corporate-led for business hotels and leisure for leisure properties. Rate levels depend on micro-market; RevPAR is the focus, with occupancy pushed in Q2 and rates to follow.
