526797|2026-03.headline: Greenply Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit record INR776.2 crore (+19.6% YoY) with core EBITDA margin of 12%, up 150 bps YoY.
526797|2026-03.overview: Greenply reported its highest-ever quarterly consolidated revenue of INR776.2 crore in Q4 FY26, with core EBITDA of INR93.2 crore at a 12% margin. MDF delivered its record quarter at INR189.4 crore revenue and 17% margin, while plywood volume grew 15.6% YoY. Management flagged a CEO/JMD resignation, a tax search operation, and a INR15.16 crore exceptional impairment linked to the Dubai entity, and guided to a 0.7-0.72 peak debt-to-equity during the MDF capex cycle. Part of Q4 volume growth was attributed to channel stocking in the second half of March, and chemical costs rose sharply, prompting price increases from April.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR588.5 crore, volume +15.6% and value +14.6% YoY, core EBITDA margin 10.4% (+120 bps YoY). FY26 revenue INR2,105.7 crore (+7.5%), volume +8.3%, margin 8.8%. Price hikes of 4-5% effective April 2026; management attributes gross margin dip to product mix.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 record revenue INR189.4 crore on 62,000 CBM (+45.3% volume YoY), margin 17%. FY26 revenue INR635.6 crore (+19.9%), margin 13.4%. Price increases of 5% and 10% effective April 2026 (15% total per analyst confirmation); FY27 volume guidance 25-30%.

segments.name: Furniture & fittings JV
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales INR12.99 crore; FY26 revenue INR44.27 crore with PAT loss INR50.8 crore (Greenply share INR25.4 crore). Management expects breakeven around the middle of next year.

guidance_outlook: Plywood volume growth target of 10% for the rest of FY27, with margins held at recent levels contingent on volume delivery.
MDF volume growth of 25-30% in FY27, using near-full capacity; EBITDA margins to be kept consistent with recent performance (Q4 FY26 MDF margin 17% described as sustainable).
Management expects the March 2026 quarter consolidated margin to be the new norm, with H2 FY27 plywood margin upside from new process technology.
Peak debt-to-equity expected at 0.7-0.72 during FY27 or the year after, reverting to 0.5-0.6 the following year.
Effective tax rate around 22% (standalone 22%, subsidiaries around 17%).

Odisha plywood plant capex about INR130 crore; other plywood technology improvements about INR45-50 crore; MDF capex about INR425 crore, of which about INR300 crore falls in FY27 and INR125 crore in FY28.
capex_capacity: PVC and WPC plant commenced commercial production in April 2026 with installed capacity of 6 million kg for doors and 3 million kg for door frames; peak revenue potential INR75-80 crore.
New MDF facility: civil construction underway and key machinery ordered; management says on track. About INR10 crore paid as advance to main equipment supplier so far.
Plywood greenfield facility (Odisha) under construction at full pace with major orders placed.

Plywood process change (ContiRoll technology): implemented in 2 of 4 existing facilities, remaining 2 to be done in FY27. Management says it lowers cost, manpower and material use and improves quality.
Flooring line in MDF expected to be fully operational in early Q2 FY27, with annual top-line capacity of about INR70-75 crore at peak.
Management says investment per cubic metre on the new Conti capacity is lower, aiming to improve capex turnover and ROCE. Steady-state ROCE aspiration of 18-20% at peak utilisation.
demand_pricing: Chemical prices rose over 50% early in the quarter; chemicals are about 30% of MDF raw material cost. Price increases: MDF 5% and 10% (15% total per analyst question confirmed by management) and plywood 4-5%, effective April 2026. Management says chemical prices have stabilised.

Q4 volume growth partly reflected channel stocking in the second half of March, plus a shift from unorganised to organised players as small MDF and plywood players were disrupted by cash-tight supplier terms.
Industry MDF growth estimated at 15-20% annualised; plywood industry growth 3-4%. Management estimates Greenply MDF market share about 7% currently, peaking at 8-8.5%.
Timber prices stable in Q4 and expected flat for FY27. Imports of MDF largely wiped out due to BIS and dollar/freight conditions.
Receivable days rose by about 3 days from December 2025 (analyst cited 47 to 54 days YoY), attributed to OEM growth and furniture factory business; management says receivables are LC-protected.
Advertising spend in Q4 lower YoY; management says the annual amount is unchanged and it is timing of expense recognition.

qa_highlights.question: Is MDF margin sustainable and is plywood double-digit margin sustainable with quality issues in the lower-end brand fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says MDF margin is sustainable, driven by volume and operating leverage on fixed costs, with cost increases already passed on. Plywood margin is sustainable if volume targets are met; process changes have improved quality.

qa_highlights.question: What is the balance sheet trajectory after capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-equity may peak at 0.7-0.72 in one year, then return to 0.5-0.6 the following year; management does not want substantially higher debt.

qa_highlights.question: Are the one-offs (Dubai/GMEL, forex) behind the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no further challenges, with all potential liability on equity, corporate guarantees and loan advances provided for in the books.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 volume growth inflated by channel inventory, and does Q1 FY27 continue the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management partly agreed, noting some stocking in the second half of March, and attributed growth mainly to a shift from unorganised to organised players; Q1 FY27 has started strongly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and split of growth capex?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR425 crore MDF capex, roughly INR300 crore in FY27 and INR125 crore in FY28; Odisha plywood about INR130 crore; plywood technology upgrades INR45-50 crore. Analyst estimated about INR480 crore for FY27, which management said was almost right.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MDF gross margin volatile and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q2 and Q3 volatility to line extension disruption and trading mix; Q4 FY26 margin is the base to deliver going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the income tax search conducted and is there any liability?
qa_highlights.answer: Search covered Greenply, Greenlam and Greenpanel; management said the reason is not known, no order or demand has been received, and the auditor has noted no liability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the JMD and CEO Manoj Tulsian step down, and is there a change in strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: He stepped down to pursue personal commitments and will continue as an advisor; sales, plant, IT, HR and marketing heads are in place, and a full-time replacement at his level is not planned immediately.

526797|2026-06.headline: Greenply Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.7% YoY to INR724.9 crore, with core EBITDA margin of 10.8%, up 50 bps YoY.
526797|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR724.9 crore (up 20.7% YoY) and core EBITDA was INR78.3 crore at a 10.8% margin. Plywood and MDF both delivered double-digit volume growth, but management said Q1 sales were lost to election-related labour disruption, lower plant utilisation (92-93% vs ~98-99% in Q4) and weak outsourcing. Price increases of 7-9% in MDF and 3-5% in plywood were taken, and the new MDF flooring line started commercial production on 20 July 2026. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 10% plywood volume growth and 25-30% MDF volume growth, and a 10% plywood margin.

Furniture JV: management says BIS enforcement is weak, so cheap Chinese hinges still compete; Greenply prices are close to Hettich MRP but dealer landing is 8-10% better than Hettich.

qa_highlights.question: Why did plywood EBITDA margin fall QoQ even though gross margin improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed low absolute volumes in Q1 versus Q4 (~600+ crore quarterly run-rate), plus election-related labour shortages, lower outsourcing and utilisation of 92-93%. It reiterated the 10% margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable MDF EBITDA margin, and the upside after the second line?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity supports 16-17% margin on a sustainable basis; the second line's operating leverage could add ~1% more, so 18% is possible.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the MDF gross margin decline of ~300 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Sharp timber cost rise from monsoon-season moisture and cutting disruption; management expects timber prices to stay stable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the employee cost increase and what is the normalised run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase reflects a provision for April wage increments plus lower sales. Q1 employee cost was ~INR98.88 crore; management expects ~INR100 crore per quarter for the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR500 crore total: parent ~INR47 crore (incl. SAMET loss funding), GSPL ~INR100 crore, GSPPL ~INR300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and leverage path?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt INR710-730 crore at 31 March 2027 (0.75x D/E), falling below 0.7x six months later and to ~0.65-0.7x by year-end. Term loan cost ~7-7.25%, working capital ~7%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the furniture JV revenue flat because of deliberate choice or weak demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed weak BIS enforcement, continued cheap Chinese imports and the need to cut imported product prices once made in India; it expects losses to reach zero around mid-next year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROCE targets for MDF and the path to them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 17-18% ROCE over a five-to-seven-year cycle. It said this requires selling 100% of capacity profitably and lower capex per cbm on line two.

526797|2026-09.headline: Greenply Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.1% YoY to INR799.7 crores, with core EBITDA margin up 300 bps to 11.2%; MDF volumes missed on production disruptions.
526797|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR799.7 crores (+16.1% YoY) and core EBITDA was INR89.2 crores at an 11.2% margin, up 300 bps YoY. Plywood value grew 15.5% on 6.1% volume growth, helped by premium mix and a realisation of INR264 per sq m. MDF revenue grew 18.4% in value but volume and realisation fell QoQ after price-hike rollbacks and monsoon and maintenance disruptions. Management kept plywood guidance, cut MDF full-year volume guidance to about 20% growth while holding a 15-16% margin, and announced a 15 million sq m Sandila plywood expansion at INR125 crores capex.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR625.7 crores, volume +6.1% YoY, realisation INR264 per sq m, core EBITDA margin 10.05%. Management attributes the margin gain to premium and Green product mix and says plant utilisation exceeded 100%.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR173.9 crores, volume 54,605 CBM, realisation INR31,816 per CBM (down QoQ after price-hike rollback), EBITDA margin 15.2%. Production was about 53,000 CBM against about 54,000 CBM sold, so the volume shortfall was supply-side.

segments.name: SAMET furniture fittings JV
segments.commentary: Q2 sales INR14.08 crores with a JV PAT loss of INR12.6 crores (Greenply share INR6.3 crores). Greenply says it stopped funding losses from Q1 and will dilute its stake to 19% by a January 5 end date.

segments.name: HDF flooring
segments.commentary: Commercial production started in July 2026. Management expects contribution from H2 FY27 and targets INR2-3 crores a month to begin with.

guidance_outlook: Plywood: existing guidance maintained. H2 plywood EBITDA margin expected at 10%+, provided sales cross about INR600 crores a quarter. Management expects more than 10% plywood volume growth annually.

MDF: full-year volume growth cut to about 20% (from earlier guidance), with 63,000 CBM targeted in each of Q3 and Q4. Core EBITDA margin guided at 15-16%; management says it can sustain above INR5,000 per CBM.

Odisha greenfield plywood facility expected in about two quarters; Vadodara MDF expansion expected in Q2 FY28 (the transcript says Plywood in Q4 FY27 and MDF in Q2 FY28, which conflicts with the Odisha and Sandila timing given elsewhere).
SAMET: dilution to 19% targeted by January 5 (head of terms signed). Greenply expects brand-charge income and zero further drag thereafter.
Chipboard: multi-day press line of about INR100 crores capex per line, 250-300 CBM output per line, asset turn about 1:2; first line planned next year or the year after.
capex_capacity: Sandila (Lucknow) plywood: 15 million sq m new capacity, INR125 crores capex, commercial production Q4 FY28; total plywood capacity 81.3 million sq m from Q4 FY28.
MDF Vadodara expansion: management says Q2 FY28 start; the new MDF line is running ahead of schedule per management. Current line produces about 60,000 CBM per quarter.
Odisha greenfield plant: about two quarters to start for Odisha, and about four to five quarters for Sandila, per management's Q&A remarks.
Pre-lam plywood for furniture makers: trials done, full-scale commercial production expected from November 2026.

Agroforestry carbon program: first phase covers over 2,300 hectares across Gujarat and Nagaland; second stage targets 12,000 hectares; 2,56,688 carbon credits allotted. Management says 50-60% of Vadodara timber sourcing and 100% of Nagaland sourcing now come through the program.
demand_pricing: Plywood: management says competition in pricing is very high, and the Q1 price increase of about 15.5% has been almost fully passed back. Raw-material chemical costs are up about 7-8% permanently, while other inputs are stable. Management attributes the margin hold to mix, Pre-lam and plain-board growth, energy-cost savings and operating efficiencies.

MDF: new capacity from Action TESA (south) has started, and Elixir is starting up soon. Management expects unorganised players to exit within 6-12 months and sees the next 12 months as weak. It describes imports as a limited threat because of freight and geopolitics.
Timber prices are stable, and management assumes no further increase. Any decline would be a margin windfall.
Carbon credits: a sample credit sold at USD15; management estimates INR25-30 crores of revenue at that price, with Greenply's share at 10-20%.
Management targets ROCE of about 18%+ over 3-5 years for MDF, and says the short-term return is low.

qa_highlights.question: Why did plywood growth slow to 6% this quarter after 10%+ in prior quarters? Any strategy change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no strategy shift. Plant utilisation was above 100%, so capacity was prioritised for premium products and margin, with the TermiVax campaign helping. Management does not expect this constraint after Odisha starts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MDF volume fall QoQ and what drives the volume and price trends?
qa_highlights.answer: The shortfall was production-driven: monsoon disruption and an OEM annual maintenance that ran four days against one planned. Sales slightly exceeded production (about 54,000 vs 53,000 CBM). Management expects to recover in Q3 and Q4 and still guides 20% full-year volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Can MDF EBITDA per CBM be guided, given the INR4,700 in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it can sustain above INR5,000 per CBM, with margin guided at 15-16%. Value-added mix and flooring and insulation are expected to lift it further.

qa_highlights.question: How is 15% MDF margin held despite raw-material inflation, and what new capacity is coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited better product mix, Pre-lam volume growth, the replacement of plain interior-grade sales, energy-cost savings and operational efficiencies. It sees Action TESA and Elixir as new competitors and says the third and fourth lines are where challenges begin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for reducing the SAMET stake, and is further capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the JV partner plans about INR400 crores of capex and Greenply's balance sheet cannot fund that. The stake will drop to 19%, Greenply will earn brand charges, and the partner's listing could benefit Greenply. No further capex is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sandila plywood revenue assumption (INR220 per sq m implied), and is more Ecotec capacity planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the INR220 blended realisation conservative. It covers PVC, premium, cheap and industrial grades, and future growth is mainly Ecotec. Some capacity is planned to shift from outsourced to in-house manufacturing.

risks_watch: MDF: Q2 volume was below plan and realisations fell QoQ. The 20% full-year volume target now needs about 63,000 CBM per quarter in H2, above the roughly 60,000 CBM run-rate cited by management.
Competitive intensity in MDF is rising with new capacity from Action TESA and Elixir. Management expects margins to stay weak for the next 12 months.
Plywood H2 margin of 10%+ depends on sales crossing about INR600 crores a quarter, and volume growth needs outsourcing.
SAMET JV: the January 5 dilution deadline and the INR105 crores invested. Management says no further provision is needed.
Carbon credit monetisation and the timing of Odisha and Sandila commissioning. Management's timelines for Odisha and Sandila were not consistent across the call.

526807|2026-03.headline: Seamec Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 58% YoY to Rs330 crore and PAT more than doubled to Rs103 crore; FY27 growth guided at about 15%.
526807|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue and profitability, with consolidated revenue of Rs1,000 crore (up 47%) and PAT of Rs253 crore versus Rs88 crore. Q4 consolidated EBITDA reached Rs162 crore versus Rs91 crore a year earlier. Management guided FY27 revenue and profit growth of about 15% and a stable EBITDA margin of 40-42%, while flagging that vessel Seamec Paladin remains stuck in Dubai due to the West Asia conflict, which removes its revenue for April-May. The company added two ONGC O&M contracts with Supreme Hydro and SEAMEC AGASTYA, and is acquiring SEAMEC ANANT (about $70 million capex in FY27).

segments.name: International (Saudi Arabia, Dubai)
segments.commentary: International markets contribute about 10-15% of revenue. Dubai operations have been pruned; one vessel is working for Saudi Aramco and one vessel (Paladin) is stuck in Dubai dry dock.

segments.commentary: Samudra Sevak and Samudra Prabha contracts run to 31 March 2028 with values of Rs348 crore and Rs270 crore; Supreme Hydro holds about 10%. Billing is monthly. Samudra Prabha expected to start work around the first week of June 2026.

qa_highlights.answer: Supreme Hydro holds about 10% and provides technical know-how, manuals and personnel; billing is monthly to ONGC at month end.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 incremental revenue be about Rs500 crore from AGASTYA, SWORDFISH, ANANT and O&M contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the assumption was not right and would not go beyond 15% guidance, citing Paladin being idle and SEAMEC-II contracted only till August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 capex and FY27 plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was about Rs300 crore; FY27 scheduled capex is about $70 million for ANANT.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 margin one-off or should margins be lower?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-off in Q4; Paladin idle for Q4 and April-May; margin guided stable at 40-42%, with 1-2% upside possible depending on utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Diamond's rate far below spot OSV rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ocean and Emerald are larger vessels doing geotech and stimulation work, so comparison is not like-for-like; Diamond is an OSV, an aberration in a DSV-focused fleet.

qa_highlights.question: Is there impairment on UK subsidiary and any progress there?
qa_highlights.answer: Impairment taken on prudence due to geopolitics, not abandonment; no accounting or execution impact; no new contract announced yet.

526807|2026-06.headline: Seamec Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 41% YoY to INR 297 crore, with EBITDA of INR 124 crore (about 42% margin).

Consolidated PAT rose to INR 81 crore from INR 76 crore, while standalone PAT was flat at about INR 81 crore versus INR 80 crore. The call focused on the Seamec ANANT acquisition (USD 70 million, expected by end-August), the 40-42% margin band and the 15-20% growth CAGR target.

526829|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 117% YoY to INR2,408 crore and PAT more than tripled to about INR62.6 crore, driven mainly by LPG volumes.
526829|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue (about INR2,408 crore), EBITDA (about INR147 crore) and PAT (about INR62.6 crore) for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, with basic EPS of INR1.86. Management attributed the top-line jump largely to higher LPG prices during supply disruption from West Asia, while saying volumes also rose sharply (about doubled YoY) and that a portion of the growth came from new bulk and institutional customers on short- to medium-term contracts. Auto LPG volumes slowed temporarily on higher prices and have since recovered per management. Most company-specific numbers (segment revenue split, FY26 capex, LPG import volumes, Type 4 cylinder margins) were deferred to follow-up emails.

qa_highlights.answer: Mumbai, Hyderabad and Indore were named, but none is finalised.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue, EBITDA and PAT will grow QoQ, though revenue will move with LPG prices. It later quantified 10-15% QoQ growth.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said BW, a strategic investor from 2023-24, exited in the secondary market to focus on its shipping business, with no impact on the company.

526861|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 7% to ₹160 crore while PAT fell 55% to ₹3.67 crore; management targets ₹60 crore from Malur in FY27.
526861|2026-03.overview: Management admitted missing its FY26 sales target, blaming delayed commissioning of Malur machinery and a workforce readiness gap. EBITDA margin slipped to 8.7% from 9.1%, and PAT fell 55% YoY to ₹3.67 crore. Management says Malur is now fully operational, the paint shop phase one went live in June 2026, and shipments to the largest customer have started. Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin of 8–11% and a ~20% revenue CAGR over three years. Analysts pressed on plant utilisation, idle capacity, cost structure and the gap between guidance and a 13–14% margin ambition.

segments.commentary: Management targets ~₹60 crore revenue in FY27 (analyst pencilled ₹50-60 crore), rising to ₹100 crore by FY29; ~₹25-30 crore of existing Bangalore business is being shifted there.

segments.commentary: Revenue ~₹36-38 crore in FY26; management targets at least ₹50 crore in FY27 (~80% utilisation), excluding new export trial orders.

segments.commentary: Management sees flat volumes as a major customer's business declined; first small US export orders received recently.

segments.commentary: Largest electrical customer Schneider's offtake fell sharply from Q4 FY25; management sees little benefit from the power sector boom to its current customer mix.

qa_highlights.question: Dhwanil Desai asked what FY27 Malur revenue to expect, whether product approvals are in place, and whether ₹50-60 crore is incremental to ₹160 crore.
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets ₹60 crore from Malur in FY27 and ₹100 crore by FY29, with product approvals in place and shipments started to the largest customer. About ₹25-30 crore of the ₹160 crore base will move from Bommasandra to Malur, so the addition is not simply ₹160 + ₹60.

qa_highlights.question: Dhwanil Desai asked whether the margin path could move from 8-9% toward 13-15% as Malur utilisation ramps.
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave an EBITDA band of 8-11% for FY27 and declined to quantify beyond that. Harshad Patel said gross margin has held for three years and a good part of 20-25% compounded growth should flow to EBITDA, aided by automation.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mehta questioned why the company keeps adding plants while Pune and Vadodara run at low utilisation and whether consolidation is planned.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new Bangalore plant was needed because the old facility lacked space for Caterpillar growth, and no other new plants are planned. Harshad Patel said Pune will reach about 80% utilisation and that idle plants must improve or be closed, while citing skill and certification differences across plants.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mehta asked whether FY27 revenue should be closer to ₹190 crore or ₹210-225 crore, and how raw material price increases are passed through.
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Agrawal said the outlook is conservative given geopolitical and raw material volatility, while agreeing the projections could make the higher number achievable. Pass-through is quarterly when prices move more than ±5%, with a one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Rahul Jain asked about Caterpillar growth and the power sector opportunity.
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Agrawal said Caterpillar talks are very positive, with at least 15-20% growth expected in FY27. Harshad Patel said power sector gains are mainly in transformers and not in the company's switchgear customers, and Schneider offtake fell sharply with no explanation.

On employee cost, he said Karnataka wage rises of up to 30% are a major challenge and the target is employee cost as a % of sales below FY26, with the labour line affected by duplication across old and new plants last year.

qa_highlights.answer: Harshad Patel agreed double-digit EBITDA is needed and said the company must aim for it, calling a failure to do so a failure. On growth beyond ₹300 crore, he said global earthmoving export demand is the focus and tube business is on hold for the next 12 months.

rows.label: Employee cost as % of sales below FY26
rows.why: Management targets a lower employee cost ratio than FY26, but Karnataka minimum wage hikes of up to 30% and last year's duplication across old and new plants make it hard to achieve.

tone.note: Management was candid about the FY26 miss and confident on Malur, Pune and Caterpillar, but was defensive on margins beyond 8-11% and on idle capacity at Pune and Vadodara; analysts pressed on utilisation, the Malur overlap with Bommasandra, cost structure and the gap to a 13-14% margin ambition.

526951|2026-03.headline: Stylam's third laminate plant at Manak Tabra is due to start commercial production by end-June or early July 2026, with INR250-300 crore revenue targeted in FY27.
526951|2026-03.overview: Management said the third greenfield laminate plant at Manak Tabra is in testing and should begin commercial production in late June or early July 2026, delayed from earlier guidance by an environment clearance issue. Total capex to date is INR334 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of roughly 20-25% over FY26 and said Q4 gross margin was about 49% (which an analyst later cited as 39%, a discrepancy unresolved on the call). The call was dominated by the AICA Japan open offer and strategic partnership, the impact of the West Asia war on raw material costs, and management's answers were often vague or hard to hear.

segments.name: Laminates (existing plants)
segments.commentary: Laminate capacity utilisation was 74% in FY26; management said existing orders are being delayed due to capacity constraints. Export is about 75% of revenue.

segments.name: New third laminate plant (Manak Tabra)
segments.commentary: Management guided INR250-300 crore revenue in FY27 and INR600-700 crore in FY28 at about 80% utilisation; peak utilisation could yield INR900-1,000 crore. Operating margin guided at 22-24%.

segments.name: Acrylics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue was about INR15 crore; FY27 target is INR50-70 crore, supported by AICA Japan purchasing acrylic, which management said is at a preliminary stage.

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Management took over domestic handling about three months ago and does not report domestic EBITDA separately; the company reports consolidated EBITDA only.

guidance_outlook: Commercial production at new Manak Tabra plant expected end-June to early-July 2026; testing has started.
New plant revenue INR250-300 crore in FY27 (earlier stated INR300-400 crore in the next three quarters), INR600-700 crore in FY28 at about 80% utilisation.
Overall FY27 revenue growth guided at roughly 20-25% over FY26; management declined to give an exact number.
EBITDA margin for new plant expected at 22-24%; an analyst's suggestion of about 22% company-level EBITDA by FY28 was answered with 'hopefully'.
Management expects EBITDA impact from West Asia-driven cost increases to be limited to about 1-3%, offset by price hikes, higher revenue absorbing fixed costs, and favourable USD/EUR exchange rates.
AICA deal (open offer completion and remaining stake tender of about 40%) expected to finish by mid-June, after which collaboration will be discussed.
capex_capacity: Third greenfield laminate plant at Manak Tabra: construction largely complete; delayed from November, then March, now June due to environment clearance (EC) needed from the Ministry of Environment in Delhi because Haryana had no CER at the time.
Capex incurred to date INR334 crore; management said fixed costs for the new plant are already in the P&L and staffing is about 150 workers with ~70-80% of wage costs already set.
New plant: three of four lines dedicated to export; compact laminates; some sizes to be produced in India for the first time.
Ramp-up: 30-40% utilisation expected from Q2 FY27; 80%+ utilisation targeted within two years.
Management said next quarter it would outline further expansion plans; a planned expansion was mentioned but not detailed.
demand_pricing: Management said new customers for the new plant's sizes are in discussion but gave no quantified PO book; existing orders are being delayed due to capacity constraint.

Raw materials: phenol and paper costs rose due to Middle East supply disruption; management said melamine has 5-6 months stock, phenol was bought 3-4 months ago at old prices, and some chemicals are under forward contracts.
Price hikes: 3-5% taken across customers; domestic in two tranches; export only where feasible, as management said Stylam competes with European players less affected by commodity costs.
Management said demand is not expected to fall with price increases, citing construction demand.
Export shipments are on FOB terms; transit time 45-60 days; no shipping delays reported. US tariff 10%.
Domestic brand visibility: management expects results in two to three quarters after restructuring of domestic sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the new plant delayed and what is the commercial production date?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay was due to an environment clearance issue after a Supreme Court observation; EC was applied to the Ministry of Environment in Delhi, taking 2-3 months plus. Commercial production expected late June to early July; testing started.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue guidance for FY27 and what is the peak potential of the new plant?
qa_highlights.answer: New plant FY27 revenue INR250-300 crore; FY28 INR600-700 crore at 80% utilisation; peak INR900-1,000 crore. Company-level FY27 growth 20-25%.

qa_highlights.question: Will management structure or the AICA stake change after the open offer?
qa_highlights.answer: Manit Gupta said no change in management; AICA is a strategic partner with no operational role. Management said the aim is not to sell stake, though the SHA put option exists.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the West Asia war on costs and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said impact limited to 1-3% of EBITDA, offset by price hikes, revenue scale, and favourable exchange rates (USD near INR96, EUR near INR112). Q4 gross margin cited as 49%, later referenced as 39% by an analyst.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and FY26 export vs domestic mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex to date INR334 crore. FY26 revenue split 75% export and 25% domestic; management expects to keep the same split in FY27 while growing domestic.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AICA Japan opportunity for supply and acrylics?
qa_highlights.answer: AICA Global is not currently buying from India and has its own plant in Rudrapur; deal not yet finished, expected in about a month. Acrylics FY27 target INR50-70 crore.

risks_watch: Commissioning slippage: plant has already been delayed from November, then March, now June; watch for commercial production start by end-June/early July.

Raw material and freight volatility from West Asia conflict (phenol, crude-linked inputs, ocean freight); management said forward contracts and price increases will cover impact but this is unquantified.
Ramp-up risk: 30-40% utilisation from Q2 FY27 and new customer onboarding for new sizes not quantified.
Management clarity: guidance figures varied across the call (FY27 new-plant revenue of INR300-400 crore vs INR250-300 crore), and management was hard to hear at multiple points.
AICA open offer completion and ~40% stake tender by mid-June, plus SHA put option; collaboration terms and any ownership change remain open.
US tariff review on July 1 and transit times of 45-60 days.

Management repeatedly gave ranges or deferred detail ('next quarter we will let you know'), and call audio quality was poor for several speakers.
key_quotes: So we are quite hopeful that we can get INR300 crores, INR400 crores turnover from this plant in the next 3 quarters.
We have at this moment done the capex of INR334 crores.
The tariff right now, US is 10%.
Next quarter, we will let you know what we are actually planning further ahead.

financial_highlights.change: Management said only 12% increase from existing plant without acrylic

financial_highlights.metric: US tariff rate applicable to Stylam

526951|2026-06.headline: Stylam Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin crossed 20%, with management guiding 19-20%+ going forward and the third plant targeted for commercial production by early September.
526951|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 margins beat the company's usual ~20% ceiling, which they attributed to higher utilisation and sales volume rather than inventory gains. The new third laminate plant has slipped from earlier timelines; dry run is under way and management targets commercial production around 15-20 August, with 1 September as the outer limit. Domestic revenue remains flat with restructuring (new team, distributors, warehouses) guided to show results from Q3 FY27. Management said the next major capex announcement is deferred to after the plant starts, around the end of August or early September.

segments.name: Laminates (exports)
segments.commentary: Europe is the strongest export region per management; US and Middle East each estimated at 10-15% of laminate revenue. Laminate capacity has a 5-10% efficiency gap to close.

segments.name: Laminates (domestic)
segments.commentary: Domestic sales stuck around INR300 crore run rate for four years per analyst. Price hikes taken across multiple SKUs, but volumes flat; restructuring to add distributors, warehouses and states.

segments.name: Acrylic
segments.commentary: Acrylic capacity is completely empty per management; ties to the domestic and export revamp. Aica may begin taking acrylic, but management said this is unconfirmed (3-4 months to know).

segments.name: Third plant (new laminate plant)
segments.commentary: Management expects roughly INR250-300 crore revenue this fiscal at 25-30% first-year utilisation, ramping month on month with no annual POs. Commercial production targeted by 15-20 August, latest 1 September.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to stay around 19-20%+ even after the new plant starts.

Domestic volumes flat in Q1; ramp-up slow in Q2, significant from Q3 FY27.
Domestic revenue share expected to rise slowly from about 25%, with margins held steady.

Raw material costs unchanged; price hikes to hold; reversal only if war-driven input costs fall, which may take 6-9 months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin spike above 20% and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no inventory gain; margins came from efficiency and higher utilisation as sales rose. They expect 19-20%+ to hold after the new plant starts.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the plant delayed and is the INR300 crore revenue still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays were due to a family dispute that slowed work and monsoon rain. Management still expects INR250-300 crore revenue from the plant this year, with commercial production by 15-20 August or 1 September at the latest.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Aica partnership and tech transfer scope?
qa_highlights.answer: Aica has joined the Board (first meeting 22 July); no operational role or export discussions yet. Tech transfer could cover any product, possibly over the next 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: How long until domestic revival and what is changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said results should show from Q3 FY27 after restructuring of the team, distributors and warehouses; Q1 volumes flat, Q2 slow ramp.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall about 10% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the Q4 base included an annual actuarial valuation booked in the audited year-end; Q1 has none. Management expects employee cost to stay at current levels post-commissioning.

Logistics and US tariff uncertainty (10% duty, reported re-implementation) for export markets.

527001|2026-03.headline: Ashapura Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 105% QoQ to INR1,969 crores, but management expects Q1 FY27 EBITDA similar to or below Q4 on falling bauxite prices and freight.
527001|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was INR1,969 crores versus INR960 crores in Q3, with EBITDA of INR211 crores (vs INR143 crores) and PBT before exceptional items of INR147 crores (vs INR89 crores). For FY26, revenue rose 91% to INR5,237 crores, EBITDA rose to INR674 crores from INR445 crores, and PBT before exceptional items rose to INR450 crores from INR305 crores. Management said Q4 EBITDA per tonne fell to $5.9 on ocean freight, fuel costs and lower bauxite prices, and guided Q1 FY27 to be similar to or weaker than Q4. The Board recommended a 100% dividend for FY26.

financial_highlights.change: Decline attributed to ocean freight, fuel and bauxite prices

segments.name: Guinea (bauxite)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR4,200 crores with EBITDA of INR561 crores; bauxite exports about 8 million tons vs 3.5 million tons in FY25. Iron ore is still in commissioning and slower than planned.

segments.name: India (Bentonite & Allied Minerals, White Performance Minerals)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR998 crores with EBITDA of INR112 crores. Margins hit by fuel, transport, input costs and a lower-margin product mix.

segments.commentary: Impacted by a sharp rise in sulfuric acid prices, a key raw material. No segment figures given.

segments.commentary: Delivered encouraging growth vs prior year. No segment figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bauxite volume guided at 10-12 million tons, with 15 million tons targeted for FY28, contingent on freight, geopolitics and the quota system.
Q1 FY27 EBITDA expected to be similar to or a little worse than Q4 FY26; management expects the full FY27 EBITDA to be better than Q4 FY26 run-rate.

GSM port expansion to add 50-60% capacity, expected by end FY27-28.

demand_pricing: Management said bauxite CIF China rose from about $60 to $68-69/t, mainly due to freight increases on that route.
Aluminium metal trading near $3,600/t, expected to rise toward $4,000/t, supportive for bauxite demand.

Long-term freight contracts with shipping lines held up during the quarter; talks under way with large shippers for longer-term freight arrangements.
India: value-added products in oil and gas and foundry; claimed about 35% India bentonite market share and over 40% of India's bentonite exports (to be verified).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 FOB realisation and was there a further bauxite price drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the press release figure of $5.9 EBITDA per tonne in Q4; said bauxite prices fell in Q4 and Q1 may still be difficult.

qa_highlights.question: Will Guinea's quota system stall new mining releases, and is it positive for Ashapura?
qa_highlights.answer: Details are not public; management believes the quota is aimed at large players (70-80 million tons) and should be positive for Ashapura.

qa_highlights.question: Is Ashapura required to build local refining or smelting capacity in Guinea?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ashapura's concessions carry no such terms, and no refinery or value-addition obligation exists today.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ashapura balance volume ramp-up against prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a price taker, sees no near-term constraint from prices, and would change strategy only if freight became very volatile or vessels were unavailable.

qa_highlights.question: Is there capex on iron ore and bauxite beneficiation?
qa_highlights.answer: Models under evaluation with partners, including BOT; management aims to limit balance-sheet capex, nothing finalised.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 revenue and EBITDA ballparks?
qa_highlights.answer: Guinea turnover of at least about $700 million at about $70/t; India flat to slightly better; EBITDA to be clearer after the quota system but hoped to be better than FY26.

527001|2026-06.headline: Ashapura Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19.2% to INR1,616 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR188.9 crore and margin fell to 11.7%.
527001|2026-06.overview: Consolidated income from operations rose about 19% YoY to INR1,616 crore, while reported EBITDA was broadly flat at INR188.9 crore as higher fuel, marine freight and input costs absorbed the gain. PBT declined about 1.4% YoY to INR130.03 crore and EPS rose to INR12.07 from INR11.5. Guinea bauxite volumes fell to 2.34 million tons from 3.16 million tons in Q4, with bauxite EBITDA per ton rising to USD6.3 from USD5.9. India businesses were hit by fuel, freight and sulphuric acid costs, with the bleaching clay JV under the most pressure.

financial_highlights.change: vs 3.16 mt in Q4 and 2.05 mt in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Guinea bauxite and iron ore
segments.commentary: Turnover about INR1,360 crore (84% of group) and EBITDA INR163 crore; volumes 2.34 mt, EBITDA USD6.3/t. Iron ore is in trial production with revenue not disclosed and EBITDA reported is bauxite-only.

segments.name: India bentonite and allied minerals / white performance minerals
segments.commentary: Wholly owned; bentonite broadly stable with domestic growth offsetting weaker exports, while white performance minerals profitability was hit by higher sales and distribution costs. No segment figures given.

segments.name: Bleaching clay (Ashapura Perfoclay, 50% JV)
segments.commentary: Sulphuric acid, a key raw material, rose about five-fold over the past year to above INR30/kg, adversely affecting the business. No figures given.

segments.name: Advanced ceramics (Orient Ceratech, 32%)
segments.commentary: Management said segment EBITDA more than doubled on premium product mix, oil and gas demand and steel-industry materials. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bauxite volume target of 10-12 million tons retained with a potential variance of ±10% (about 9-11 mt); Q2 is seasonally weakest, with most sales in late Q3 and Q4.
Bauxite EBITDA per ton expected near USD6 (USD5.5-6 range) for the next one or two quarters; return toward ~USD10 is a medium to long-term expectation, timing not predicted.
Iron ore: 15 million ton target by FY28 reaffirmed ("achieve or even cross"), but long-term iron ore guidance needs a couple more quarters.
Guinea export quota system expected before end of CY2026, seen as supportive of realisations and freight.
Management expects bauxite revenue near USD1 billion (about INR10,000 crore) at 15 mt once conditions normalise.
India capex of close to INR200 crore planned across projects and verticals.
capex_capacity: Boffa port fully operational with capacity raised from 5 mtpa to 8 mtpa; no further expansion to 10-12 mt planned near-term, to be decided as volumes ramp.
GSM second port new jetty under construction, expected operational by Q4 FY27, raising capacity from 6 mtpa to 10 mtpa; combined port capacity about 23 mt.
Total bauxite export capacity stated at 18 million tons.
Bauxite washing plant set up with ~20,000 tons/day capacity, on an operate-and-transfer model; a comparable plant would cost about USD15 million and take about one year to build if expanded.
Ashapura has over 1 million tons of bentonite grinding capacity, which management described as the world's largest.
demand_pricing: Freight remains highly volatile and elevated; management expects volatility through 2027 and freight is the main margin overhang.
Chinese index bauxite price around USD72/t, up from ~USD61, mostly due to ocean freight rather than FOB Guinea price.
Alumina prices under pressure; management is positive on medium-term demand, citing four new Chinese refineries adding 20-30 mt of bauxite demand.
Middle East and Europe customer demand impacted by geopolitics and freight; company focusing on India, Asia and Africa.
Customer demand volatile; customers may take time to absorb market and cost changes.

qa_highlights.question: Status and timing of Guinea bauxite export quota system and expected realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the quota system before end of 2026 and sees realisations flat until then; margins also flat with freight overhang. FY28 15 mt target described as on track.

qa_highlights.question: Response to new entrants such as Nimba selling bauxite via monthly tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a new development with slow materialisation and will not significantly disrupt the market, with volumes likely going to other traders; Ashapura may participate in tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Impact and expansion of the washing plant on EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant is roughly EBITDA neutral and mainly a sustainability and throughput tool; no EBITDA quantification given; expansion would take about one year.

qa_highlights.question: Boffa port expansion beyond 8 mt to 10 mt by Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: No near-term plan; 8 mt is seen as reasonable for now, with expansion to 10-12 mt to follow volume ramp-up without a fixed timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Fako deposit and China Railway arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Only an MOU; details under study and little progress to report, with possible update next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why no iron ore revenue disclosure, and is the 10 mt guidance achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Iron ore is in trial production with low revenue, so it is not split out; EBITDA disclosed is bauxite only. Guidance is 10-12 mt with ±10% variance, and management said it is broadly on track.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA per ton outlook for Q2, FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Near-term USD5.5-6/t; a return toward USD10/t is expected over the medium to longer term, timing uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of Orient Ceratech's EBITDA doubling and India growth levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are oil and gas product demand with debottlenecking and steel-industry materials replacing imports; India growth from cat litter, foundry, oil and gas, and kaolin for paper and paint.

risks_watch: Timing of the Guinea bauxite export quota system (management expects it before end-CY2026); realisations and freight are expected to stay flat until then.
Ocean freight volatility through 2027 and limited vessel availability; freight is the main margin overhang and the FY27 EBITDA per ton outlook (USD5.5-6) depends on it.
FY27 bauxite volume delivery: Q1 at 2.34 mt versus the 10-12 mt target with ±10% variance; Q2 is seasonally weakest and most sales land in late Q3 and Q4.
Competitive entry such as Nimba's monthly tenders, and whether Ashapura participates in tenders on viability.
India margin pressure from fuel, sulphuric acid (above INR30/kg, about five-fold YoY) and weak Middle East and Europe demand; the bleaching clay JV is most exposed.
Iron ore commercialisation remains undisclosed in revenue; long-term iron ore guidance deferred by a couple of quarters; Fako/China Railway deal is only an MOU with little progress.
key_quotes: Let us acknowledge that there is some pressure on EBITDA margin in the short-term. However, we remain optimistic about the future outlook.
So the objective of this plant is more on a sustainability perspective as we have put up the 20,000 tons kind of capacity in a short period of time.
So, I would take that also with a little bit pinch of salt.
So we are consciously taking a call to focus on profitability while this disrupted situation remains.
527001|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on the long-term Guinea bauxite and India value-added outlook but cautious on the near term, repeatedly flagging freight, fuel and vessel availability as the constraints on margins and volumes. It was evasive on quantification: it declined to give the washing plant's EBITDA impact, iron ore revenue or a firm EBITDA per ton path beyond the next one or two quarters.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Bauxite EBITDA/t guided at USD5.5-6 near term versus USD6.3 in Q1, and consolidated EBITDA margin fell to ~11.7% from 13.8% YoY on fuel, marine freight and sulphuric acid (above INR30/kg, about five-fold YoY); management expects realisations and margins flat until the Guinea export quota system arrives before end-CY2026.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Boffa port is already fully operational at 8 mtpa (from 5 mtpa), and the GSM second-port jetty raising capacity from 6 to 10 mtpa is under construction and expected operational by Q4 FY27, taking combined port capacity to about 23 mt.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Bauxite volumes rose to 2.34 mt from 2.05 mt in Q1 FY26 (about +14% YoY) and Boffa is now at 8 mtpa, but Q1 fell from 3.16 mt in Q4 and Q2 is seasonally weak, so growth depends on the late Q3-Q4 sales concentration.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: India capex of close to INR200 crore is already planned across projects, and the Boffa expansion to 10-12 mt has no fixed timeline and will follow volume ramp-up; utilisation is not disclosed, so a new large capex is conditional rather than firm.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 bauxite target of 10-12 mt (±10%) was only held, not raised; Q1 volume was 2.34 mt, Q2 is seasonally weakest, and the near-term EBITDA/t range is USD5.5-6 against USD6.3 achieved in Q1.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 volume of 2.34 mt is well below the 10-12 mt FY27 run-rate needed (about 2.5-3 mt per quarter on average), with Q2 seasonally weakest and most sales in late Q3 and Q4; freight volatility through 2027 is the main overhang, so the ±10% band is the safety valve.

rows.label: Guinea bauxite export quota system
rows.why: Management expects the quota system before end-2026 and says it is supportive of realisations and freight, while realisations stay flat until then.

rows.label: Orient Ceratech advanced ceramics growth
rows.why: Segment EBITDA more than doubled on premium mix, oil and gas demand and steel-industry materials replacing imports, though no figures were given.

rows.label: Fako deposit / China Railway arrangement
rows.why: Only an MOU with little progress to report; management flagged a possible update next year.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term Guinea bauxite (15 mt FY28, USD10/t medium term) and India value-added outlook but cautious near term on freight, fuel and vessel availability; analysts pushed on the washing plant EBITDA impact, iron ore revenue and the EBITDA/t path, which management large

530005|2026-03.headline: UltraTech Q4 FY26: consolidated volume about 44 Mt, EBITDA of INR1,253/t, and a INR240/share FY26 dividend, with India Cements brand migration completed.
530005|2026-03.overview: The call was the UltraTech Q4 FY26 earnings call, transcript filed by India Cements Ltd as a subsidiary disclosure. UltraTech crossed 200 Mt India capacity and committed to 242.5 Mt by FY28. Q4 realisations rose about 2.5% on grey cement pricing, with consolidated EBITDA per tonne at INR1,253 (INR1,296 excluding acquired assets). Management flagged West Asia-linked cost pressure, mainly bags (about INR90 crore hit in March) and a mark-to-market forex loss (about INR120-130 crore), and said price hikes taken in April offset it. The Board recommended a INR240/share dividend for FY26, and India Cements' 100% brand migration to UltraTech was completed at end-March 2026.

financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY25 excl. acquired assets was INR1,225/t; excl. acquired assets Q4 FY26 INR1,296/t
UltraTech brand volume up 19% YoY as stated
first profit after a long time, as stated
as stated by CFO in closing remarks
up from INR333/t in Q2 and INR305/t in Q3
dividend payout 37% of profit last year as stated

segments.name: India (UltraTech India, ~196 Mt capacity)
segments.commentary: Average utilisation above 80% and about 90% per the CFO; trade mix around 66-67%. Ex-West Asia aberrations, India EBITDA was about INR1,240/t per management.

segments.name: UAE / overseas (~5 Mt)
segments.commentary: Utilisation fell from 100% pre-conflict to about 80%, now recovering. Bulk-only, so no bag cost. Q4 EBITDA INR278 crore.

segments.name: India Cements (acquired)
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA INR497/t, with INR200/t of underlying margin sitting in UltraTech's books under the tolling arrangement, giving about INR670/t on a combined basis. Target above INR1,000/t by FY28. Q4 volume 3.12 Mt, of which 0.39 Mt non-UltraTech brand.

segments.name: Kesoram (acquired)
segments.commentary: Already operating at more than INR1,000/t EBITDA in Q4 per management. Brand migration fully complete.

segments.name: Cable and wire
segments.commentary: About INR800 crore of an INR1,800 crore capex spent; management expects launch around Q3 FY27 (first month of Q3).

guidance_outlook: Sustainable volume growth of 7-8% per annum; double-digit volume growth targeted for FY27 (industry 6.5% for FY26 as cited by management).
Capacity to reach 242.5 Mt in phases by FY28 with 37 Mt of further additions committed; growth beyond 240 Mt being planned.
Annual capex of INR8,000-10,000 crore from internal accruals for the foreseeable future; leverage to stay below 1x.
Cost efficiency programme: about INR185/t delivered; target above INR300/t, now expected to be exceeded by FY28.
Clinker factor (clinker-to-cement ratio) target 1.54x by FY28, from 1.48x currently; the company will remain fully clinker-backed.
Green power: about 43% of power from green sources; target about 85% by end FY30.

Price hikes taken in April 2026 management views as sufficient to offset bag cost increase (about INR6/bag) and sustain profitability; diesel and June-quarter fuel (about INR1.77-1.8/kcal) not fully factored in.
capex_capacity: Capacity at 200 Mt in India; 37 Mt more committed in a phased manner, taking capacity above 242.5 Mt by FY28.
India Cements: INR1,592 crore committed for efficiency improvement, plus INR400 crore for capacity expansion; Kesoram cost-improvement capex of INR400-500 crore.
Acquired ICL and Kesoram assets together are about 13% of consolidated capacity.
No thermal capacity to be added; the mix shifts to WHRS and renewables. Lead distance 367 km; new Lucknow bulk terminal.
demand_pricing: Grey cement prices rose about 2.5% in most geographies in Q4, helped by trade mix and premiumisation; April 2026 cement price increases were taken.
Industry volume growth in the March quarter estimated at 6-7%; FY26 industry growth estimated at 6.5%.
Trade/non-trade mix about 65-68%; rural demand described as steady.
Bag prices rose from about INR9 to INR15 a bag during March, and about INR13-14 by late April. Bag supply was described as expensive but not a constraint.
Management said price hikes were 'here to stay' given cost inflation across the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Is a high payout ratio sustainable given the balance sheet and capex funded from internal accruals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it depends on performance and the Board; FY26 dividend of INR240/share is described as the highest level, with a possible repeat next year but no commitment.

qa_highlights.question: How much West Asia cost impact is in Q4 and how should June quarter look?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental bag cost in Q4 was about INR90 crore, which cannot be annualised. Power and fuel are not expected to be a large issue in June; a mark-to-market forex hit of about INR120-130 crore is in EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How much of India Cements' INR1,000/t target comes from cost versus realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost programmes and price increases are both contributors. INR200/t of EBITDA sits in UltraTech's books; combined EBITDA is about INR670/t already, with the target including both books.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the India Cements merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy legal cases inherited with India Cements have to be closed first; management wants no risk to UltraTech before the next phase of integration.

qa_highlights.question: Is the UltraTech balance sheet ring-fenced from the group's RCB exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not a penny has moved from the UltraTech balance sheet for other purposes, and it is committed to keeping it ring-fenced.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cement lagging other building materials on price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the lag mainly to industry fragmentation, and said price increases typically come in Q1 of the financial year.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: sustained high pet coke (about $160/t cited by an analyst), oil near $100/bbl and diesel pass-through, which management says is not yet factored in.
Bag cost volatility and whether the April price hikes hold through monsoon (July-September).
Forex: $950 million of hedged foreign currency borrowings marked at INR94.85/$ at 31 March; the rupee moved to about INR94.2 by late April, so a mark-to-market effect can reverse.
Whether India Cements' remaining legal cases close, allowing the next integration phase.
Whether the INR200/t of India Cements EBITDA in UltraTech's books comes through and the INR300/t efficiency programme is delivered.
Sustainability of the dividend payout beyond the special FY26 payout, and the RMC (ready-mix concrete) growth plan (no monetisation planned).
530005|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on capacity, integration and dividend, but guarded and deflecting on West Asia cost trajectory, diesel, forward pricing and the India Cements merger timeline. Several answers were framed as 'we will wait and watch'.
key_quotes: UltraTech crossed 200 million tons of cement production capacity in India, a first for any company in a single country outside of China.
We said we would do these things, we have done them and we enter fiscal '27 in a stronger strategic position than at any point in our history.
Not a penny has moved from UltraTech balance sheet for any other purposes.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: India Cements EBITDA rose from INR305/t (Q3) to INR497/t (Q4) and the efficiency programme is at INR185/t against a INR300/t target by FY28, but West Asia cost inflation (about INR90 crore bag hit in March, FX loss of INR120-130 crore) and unfactored diesel and fuel pressure cap near-term upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: phased, 37 Mt by FY28 (Q4 FY28 end-point)
rows.why: 37 Mt of further phased additions are committed, taking UltraTech India from about 200 Mt to 242.5 Mt by FY28, with utilisation at 90%; cable and wire INR1,800 crore (INR800 crore spent) launches around Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets double-digit FY27 volume growth against 6.5% industry growth in FY26, backed by 90% utilisation and 37 Mt of phased capacity additions.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at about 90% across the network with 37 Mt already committed, and management plans INR8,000-10,000 crore of annual capex from internal accruals, so further expansion beyond 240 Mt is being planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management targets double-digit FY27 volume growth and 7-8% sustainable growth, and the April price hikes are described as sufficient to offset bag costs, but no revenue or margin guidance was raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: West Asia pressure is not yet fully in the numbers: diesel and June-quarter fuel (about INR1.77-1.8/kcal) are not factored in, bag costs rose from about INR9 to INR15 a bag in March, and the INR120-130 crore forex MTM hit is in EBITDA, though April price hikes are said to offset it.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The INR1,800 crore cable and wire business has INR800 crore spent, with launch guided around the first month of Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Efficiency programme to INR300/t+ by FY28
rows.why: About INR185/t already delivered against a target above INR300/t, now expected to be exceeded by FY28.

rows.label: Leverage below 1x while funding capex
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA is 0.94x consolidated and capex of INR8,000-10,000 crore a year is funded from internal accruals, with leverage guided to stay below 1x.

rows.label: April 2026 price hikes hold
rows.why: Price hikes taken in April are seen as offsetting bag costs of about INR6/bag, but grey cement prices rose only about 2.5% in Q4 and the monsoon is a test.

tone.note: Management was confident on capacity, volume growth and the dividend, but guarded on West Asia cost trajectory, diesel, forward pricing and the India Cements merger timeline; analysts pushed on those cost and integration points.

530005|2026-06.headline: UltraTech Q1 FY27: domestic grey volume up 13.1% to 81% utilisation, EBITDA INR5,146 crore and PAT INR2,604 crore (+17.2%).
530005|2026-06.overview: The document is headed India Cements Ltd but the enclosed transcript is UltraTech Cement's Q1 FY27 earnings call (held 20 July 2026), with CFO Atul Daga presenting. Domestic grey cement volume grew 13.1% YoY, with capacity utilisation at 81% versus 76%, and revenue rose 16%. Management flagged a fuel and packing cost shock during the quarter and guided to a further INR130-140 per ton cost increase in Q2 FY27. India Cements turnaround continued, with EBITDA per ton at INR603 versus roughly INR386 in Q2 FY26, and Cables and Wires remains on track for Q3 FY27 launch.

financial_highlights.value: About INR12 per bag average from INR9
financial_highlights.change: up about INR3/bag average in quarter

financial_highlights.metric: India Cements revenue (ex-factory, net of freight)

financial_highlights.change: from about INR386 in Q2 FY26, INR400 and INR509 in intervening quarters

segments.name: Grey cement (UltraTech incl. India Cements and Kesoram)
segments.commentary: Domestic volume up 13.1% with 81% utilisation on a 200 mtpa base; brand growth of 21.3%. East was the slowest region in the quarter, South and North were just below 15%, West and Central above 15%.

segments.name: India Cements (turnaround)
segments.commentary: Brand migration to UltraTech is 100% complete; revenue up 21% and volume up 19% like-for-like; conversion ratio 1.5x. Management targets INR1,000 per ton EBITDA with the full capex benefit from Q4 FY28.

segments.name: Cables and Wires
segments.commentary: INR1,800 crore programme with INR888 crore spent or committed to date; commissioning and product launch reaffirmed for Oct-Dec 2026 quarter (Q3 FY27).

guidance_outlook: Management is targeting double-digit grey cement volume growth for FY27.
Industry volume growth in Q1 FY27 estimated at 7-8% (management's marketing intelligence), though 'too early'.
Q2 FY27 cost increase guided at INR130-140 per ton (fuel, maintenance, operating deleverage, monsoon), with measures planned to absorb part of it.
Industry expects cement prices to hold broadly steady through the monsoon quarter; management said it will attempt higher prices.
Capacity to reach 212.7 mtpa grey by end FY27 and about 235 mtpa by March 2028; consolidated capacity beyond 242 mtpa.
Management expects a better H2 FY27 cost position if the West Asia conflict eases; India Cements EBITDA of INR1,000 per ton remains the target, with full benefit from Q4 FY28.
Company does not give formal Cables and Wires guidance; net debt to EBITDA expected to remain below 1x for FY27.
capex_capacity: Domestic capacity at 200.1 mtpa and total capacity 205.5 mtpa after commissioning of 8.7 mt of UltraTech capacity (Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam, Patratu) in the quarter.
Projects under execution backed by about INR17,000 crore capex over the next 2-2.5 years; all growth capex funded from internal accruals.
Green power at 1,897 MW (about 47% of power requirement at quarter end); 71 MW renewables and 19 MW WHRS commissioned in the quarter; target 2.5-3 GW shortly.
India Cements cost-improvement capex of about INR2,000 crore (WHR, preheater and cooler upgrades); green power share to rise from about 3% to about 86% by end FY28.
Lead distance down to 360 km from 367 km; AFR substitution ramping up.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as strong and broadening, citing infrastructure, housing, urban real estate, ports, data centres and metro projects.
All-India exit prices improved through June; East and South led increases, Central and West steady, North consistent.
Premiumisation and blended cement mix support blended realisations; RMC is about 3.5% of UltraTech sales and retail about 65-66%.
Blended coal cost was USD134/ton in the quarter (INR1.9/kcal cited); currently about INR2/kcal and inventory-loaded.
Diesel (industrial) rose from about INR78-80/litre pre-war to about INR150-157, lifting limestone raising costs by about 13-14% QoQ per the raw material index.
Pet coke now costlier than coal on an energy basis, so coal is preferred.

qa_highlights.question: How will growing operating cash flow be deployed across dividends and cement capex, and will cables and wires capex scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash flows are fully booked for growth capex and dividends; no further cables and wires investment is foreseen for now, with the business first maturing.

qa_highlights.question: What remains before India Cements is merged into a standalone entity?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex programme completion and disposal of non-core land are pending; the journey is expected to complete in Q4 FY28 or a quarter earlier, with some operating parameters still to bring in line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 FY27 cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost increase of INR130-140 per ton expected in Jul-Sep quarter, covering fuel, maintenance, deleverage; Q1 one-off impact was about INR40 on fuel and about INR20 on bags.

qa_highlights.question: Regional demand trends?
qa_highlights.answer: East was slowest in April-June (elections, labour availability); South and North below 15%; West and Central above 15%. East expected to see a multi-year upcycle.

qa_highlights.question: Industry volume growth for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Estimated at 7-8% based on marketing intelligence; management noted it is early.

qa_highlights.question: Growth beyond 240 mtpa and inorganic options?
qa_highlights.answer: Inorganic opportunities will be examined; the team is working on plans beyond 240 mtpa and details will follow.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict and fuel cost volatility: crude above USD100 at the start of the quarter, with ocean freight insurance up to 4-5% from under 1%.
Q2 FY27 margin pressure of INR130-140/ton from fuel, maintenance and monsoon deleverage; watch whether management absorbs part of it.
Monsoon and dry spells (Rajasthan, some other states) could affect rural demand and next-year water-linked construction.
Cables and Wires: Q3 FY27 launch timeline, working capital build-up over the next 6 months, and ramp-up.
Industry capacity plans may be revised, per management comments on the 2027-28 industry capacity number.
India Cements per-ton EBITDA trajectory towards INR1,000/t and the India Cements merger timeline (Q4 FY28).
530005|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional, with strong emphasis on demand, brand and track record. Management was candid on near-term cost pressure but gave few hard numbers on the longer term; it deflected several questions (e.g., cables and wires guidance, challenges over 5 years, capacity additions by the industry).
key_quotes: We intend to grow like a challenger and not an incumbent.
We absorbed the shock better than any peer, and we will harvest the relief faster than any peer.
We said we will cross 200 million tons; we did a year early.
Yes, we are targeting double-digit volume growth this year.

rows.when: Q3 FY27 to Q4 FY27; ~235 mtpa by Mar 2028
rows.why: 8.7 mt commissioned in Q1 FY27 and about INR17,000 crore of projects under execution take capacity to 212.7 mtpa by end FY27 and about 235 mtpa by March 2028, with utilisation already at 81%.

rows.why: Cables and Wires commissioning and product launch reaffirmed for Oct-Dec 2026 on an INR1,800 crore programme with INR888 crore spent or committed.

rows.label: India Cements EBITDA INR1,000/t target
rows.why: India Cements EBITDA is at INR603/t (from about INR386 in Q2 FY26) with brand migration 100% complete, and the full capex benefit (about INR2,000 crore cost-improvement programme) is expected from Q4 FY28.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA below 1x
rows.why: Net debt to EBITDA is 0.87x, down from 0.94x at start of year, and management expects it to stay below 1x for FY27 with growth capex funded from internal accruals.

rows.label: Cement price increases
rows.why: All-India exit prices improved through June, but the industry expects prices to hold broadly steady through the monsoon quarter, and management says it will attempt higher prices.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, brand and capacity additions, and candid on the INR130-140/t Q2 cost pressure. Analysts pushed on the cost outlook and the cables and wires plan; management gave few longer-term numbers and deflected some questions.

530005|2026-09.headline: UltraTech Q2 FY27: volumes up 13.8% with 71% utilisation; spot trade prices ~5% above Q2 average entering Q3.
530005|2026-09.overview: UltraTech reported a strong Q2 FY27 on volume growth of 13.8% and a 21% rise in net profit, despite fuel costs rising sharply on the West Asia conflict. Q2 average trade prices were flat to Q1 (down 1-1.5%), but prices rose 7-10 per bag month-on-month in late September and kept rising in October, with management putting spot about 5% above the Q2 average. Fuel cost rose from INR 45 to INR 51.5 per bag, and management expects the cost pressure to largely persist through Q3-Q4 at roughly INR 2.2 per kcal. Capacity reached 204.7 Mt domestic after 4.6 Mt commissioning in September, and the Ultravolt wires and cables business launched on 3 September. Net debt rose to 1.26x net debt/EBITDA from 0.94x at March-end.

segments.name: Cement - North
segments.commentary: Volumes grew more than 20% YoY; utilisation upwards of 70%; new prices absorbed.

segments.name: Cement - South
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 15-20% YoY on about 50 Mt capacity; utilisation above 70%; capacities fully sold out; prices improving. A greenfield plant was commissioned this quarter.

segments.name: Cement - West
segments.commentary: Volumes grew about 10%; utilisation close to 70%; Mumbai prices up 3-4% per bag in September.

segments.name: Cement - East
segments.commentary: Volumes grew about 5%; utilisation about 60% due to heavy monsoon; prices fell in August and are now catching up since early October.

segments.name: Cement - Central
segments.commentary: Volumes grew about 10%; utilisation about 60%; pricing described as muted.

segments.name: Ultravolt (wires and cables)
segments.commentary: Launched 3 September 2026; about 25-27 days of operation in Q2. INR 1,100 crore of INR 1,800 crore capex spent or committed; 80,000+ retail points and 1,500+ UBS channel partners signed up; management says it will not talk about revenue or margin yet and expects a meaningful quarter in April-June 2027. Expense attributable to the business is not material per management.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 capex guidance held at about INR 10,000 crore (plus or minus); fuller view promised after Q3 results.
Full benefit of recent price increases expected to reflect in Q3 earnings rather than immediately; management intends to sustain YoY higher EBITDA per ton over the next two quarters.
Pet coke and fuel cost: management sees the INR 2.2/kcal level persisting through Q3-Q4 if $180/t pet coke holds; marginal impact expected in Q4 from inventory pipeline.
Targets 240 Mt capacity as planned; next organic growth phase to be announced before FY27 end, with detailed plans to come.
Net debt/EBITDA expected below 1x by March 2027.
Business-as-usual delivery of INR 1,400/t EBITDA exit-March 2028 target; cost pressures expected to be covered by price increases.
Ultravolt maturity expected by FY28; Board has not sanctioned capex beyond INR 1,800 crore; target revenue reference of INR 10,000 crore now seen at INR 16,000-18,000 crore on copper prices.
Industry demand expected to grow close to 8% in H1 FY27 and to remain strong through March 2029.
capex_capacity: Commissioned 4.6 Mt in September 2026, including the 3.6 Mt greenfield at Petnikota (Andhra Pradesh) and 1 Mt debottlenecking at three units; domestic capacity now 204.7 Mt.
On track for 240 Mt capacity as planned.
Added 116 MW renewable power and 10 MW waste heat recovery; 47% of power from non-fossil sources; 2 GW green power for captive use.
AFR systems commissioned at 2 plants; thermal substitution rate about 7.2%.

Ultravolt: INR 1,800 crore plan with about INR 1,100 crore spent or committed; balance expected over about two quarters; mother plant at Jhagadia, Gujarat; 78,000 tpa copper consumption capacity annualised.
demand_pricing: Q2 average trade prices flat vs Q1 (down about 1-1.5%) due to soft August; trade prices rose 7-10 per bag MoM in late September, and exit-September trade was at least about 3% above Q1 average.
Spot realisations in October about 5% above Q2 average, per management.
Trade ratio stable at 65-67% (65.7% in Q2 per management); premium cement 37% of sales; blended cement 67.3%.
Over 25% of trade sales come through the UBS network (about 6,500 stores, target 10,000 by FY28-29).
Industry demand close to 10% YoY in Q2; management says the Q1 industry rate was 6.5%.
Fuel costs: pet coke about $180/t; pet coke share cut to about 25% of mix; domestic coal supply constrained as Coal India prioritises power sector.
Public infrastructure awards picking up; central capex strong through July; road construction weak.

qa_highlights.question: Variable cost inflation in H2 at current spot levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify but noted inventory in the pipeline means Q3 impact is limited and marginal impact in Q4; expects not much additional inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Tamil Nadu levy of INR 160/t: accounted in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is already accounted for in Q2 with no reversal, and the company incurs no additional cost from the effective date.

qa_highlights.question: Capex guidance and H1 capex of INR 5,882 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management held full-year capex at about INR 10,000 crore plus or minus, to be refined after Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost rise about 22% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 5,000 crore NCDs at 7.25% were raised and held for about two months; management said the borrowing was a good decision given current rates.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt increase in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex and dividend payment; net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x from 0.94x at March-end, with expected to fall below 1x by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Is trade volume demand housing-led or industrial-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade ratio stable at 65-67%, indicating retail housing demand holds share; industrial volumes growing faster; industry sold 463 Mt in FY26 vs UltraTech 145 Mt.

qa_highlights.question: Ultravolt capacity and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 10,000 crore revenue target from early 2025 could reach INR 16,000-18,000 crore at current copper prices; no further capex beyond INR 1,800 crore sanctioned; production to double from current levels.

risks_watch: Fuel and energy costs: pet coke about $180/t, domestic coal constraint, and industrial diesel at record highs; West Asia conflict outcome uncertain.
Weak monsoon (fourth lowest since 2001) and drought pockets could soften rural demand.
Ultravolt ramp-up: stock-outs possible, unproven margins, and no revenue disclosure yet; separately reported from next quarter as a division of the standalone financials.
Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x; capex and dividend are funding needs.
Festive-season slowdown may delay full realisation of price increases until Q3 results.
530005|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and volume momentum, with specific numbers for most questions, but evasive on Ultravolt margins and utilisation and on H2 cost inflation. Management repeatedly deflected to "give us some time" for the new business and declined to quantify cost trajectory beyond INR 2.2/kcal.

financial_highlights.change: Ahead of industry growth of close to 10%
Absolute fixed costs up 4% vs volume up 13.8%

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 204.7 Mt domestic capacity after 4.6 Mt commissioned in September, with 240 Mt target stated as on track but no dated timeline; utilisation at 71% gives room before new capacity is needed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume grew 13.8% YoY versus industry near 10%, with North volumes up 20%+ and South volumes up 15-20% with capacities fully sold out; industry demand expected near 8% in H1 FY27 and strong through March 2029.
