rows.why: Management said the next organic growth phase will be announced before FY27 end, and 240 Mt target is still short of 204.7 Mt current capacity; utilisation at 71% is below the 80% threshold, so the trigger is the stated plan rather than utilisation pressure.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects the full benefit of recent price increases to show in Q3 earnings and sustain higher YoY EBITDA per ton over next two quarters, but has not raised formal guidance and capex is held at about INR 10,000 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fuel cost at INR 51.5/bag vs INR 45 and pet coke around $180/t with domestic coal constrained; weak monsoon (fourth lowest since 2001) could soften rural demand and delay price realisation until Q3 results.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: already launched 3 Sept 2026; meaningful quarter Apr-Jun 202
rows.why: Ultravolt wires and cables launched 3 September 2026 with INR 1,100 crore of INR 1,800 crore spent or committed and 80,000+ retail points signed up, though revenue and margins are not yet disclosed.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA below 1x by March 2027
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x at end-Sep 2026 from 0.94x at March 2026, and management guides below 1x by March 2027 as EBITDA rises with price increases.

rows.label: UBS retail network expansion to 10,000 stores
rows.why: Over 25% of trade sales come through about 6,500 UBS stores, with the target at 10,000 by FY28-29; Ultravolt has 1,500+ UBS channel partners signed up.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing and volume momentum with specific numbers, but evasive on Ultravolt margins and utilisation and on H2 cost inflation, deflecting to 'give us some time'; analysts pushed on H2 variable cost inflation, the interest cost jump, and the net debt rise.

530007|2026-03.headline: JK Tyre Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 42% YoY to Rs.546 crore on 12.9% margin, with a further Rs.4,980 crore brownfield expansion approved.
530007|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs.4,233 crore and PAT rose 83% to Rs.188 crore, with FY26 revenue at a record Rs.16,384 crore. Management said volume growth was broad-based, led by domestic OE and TBR, and margin expansion came from volumes, mix and cost control. Raw material costs are expected to rise 18-20% in Q1 FY27, which management is offsetting with staggered price hikes of 4-5% (replacement) and 5-7% (export), with a further 5-6% under way. The Board approved Rs.4,980 crore of additional PCR and TBR brownfield capacity to 2029, on top of the Rs.1,130 crore already under implementation.

segments.name: Consolidated mix Q4 FY26 (by revenue)
segments.commentary: Truck & bus ~56%, PLR ~27%, non-truck bias ~13%, 2/3W ~4%. Market split: replacement 63%, OE 27%, exports ~10%.

segments.name: Standalone mix Q4 FY26
segments.commentary: Truck & bus 59%, PLR 25%, non-truck bias 12%, 2/3W 5%. Standalone replacement 61%, OE 30%.

segments.name: JK Tornel (Mexico)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs.2,138 crore (FY25: Rs.2,147 crore); FY26 EBITDA Rs.141 crore, PBT Rs.61 crore (+63%), PAT Rs.42 crore (+91%). Q4 revenue Rs.378 crore, EBITDA Rs.24 crore (+36% YoY); management described Q4 as sluggish on US tariff uncertainty.

segments.name: Domestic India volumes
segments.commentary: Q4 domestic volumes +21% YoY; OE +42%. TBR replacement +19%, TBR OE +53%. Passenger line +16% (replacement +10%, OE +26%). Farm volumes +58% (replacement +30%, OE nearly doubled, exports +44%). 2/3W OE +72%, 2/3W exports +31%.

segments.name: Exports (India)
segments.commentary: Q4 export volumes steady; FY26 export volumes +5%. Passenger exports +20% for FY26. Premium 16-inch+ domestic sales +13% in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Raw material prices expected to rise 18-20% in Q1 FY27 vs Q4 FY26 (CFO-level figure stated as 18-19% later in Q&A); management sees some softening in crude and possible raw material relief from Q3 FY27 if conditions hold.
Further price hike of 5-6% under way on top of 4-5% already taken in replacement (5-7% in exports); OEM price increases lag. Mainly taken in Q1 FY27.
Management expects demand to remain buoyant in FY27, with mid-single-digit growth in some categories; no OEM order cuts seen.
Cash outlay of about Rs.1,200 crore per year; total expansion of Rs.6,110 crore (Rs.1,130 crore + Rs.4,980 crore) to complete by FY29, with debt-to-equity of about 2:1 on the projects.
Rs.1,130 crore expansion to complete by Q3 FY28; capacity for TBR and PCR to rise 24%.
capex_capacity: Installed capacities fully utilised across segments; India utilisation above 90% for FY26.
Rs.1,130 crore expansion under implementation (mainly TBR, some PCR), completion by Q3 FY28.
Board approved further brownfield PCR and TBR expansion of Rs.4,980 crore in phases until 2029, increasing TBR and PCR capacity by 24%.
Management stated the Rs.4,980 crore plan is in addition to the Rs.1,130 crore; the total of Rs.6,110 crore is to be spent over three to four years.
2/3W: growth via productivity improvements and expanded outsourcing of 2/3W tyres.
demand_pricing: Q4 price hikes of 4-5% in replacement and 5-7% in export; OEM pricing lags. Competitors have taken hikes in the same range, per management.
Management reports no OEM order book cuts across CV, passenger or other lines, though supply chains were disrupted by the West Asia crisis.
New OEM approvals in FY26 from Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland, Mahindra, Switch Mobility, VECV and Euler Motors; 50+ new brand shops added.
Management cited the Levitas Ultra premium passenger offering, puncture guard and smart tyres, and the 'selling miles' fleet mobility programme as barriers to entry against new entrants.
Management noted a peer's warning on possible demand moderation from price hikes, but did not give a view on Q2/H2 demand impact.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q4 market and category mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated: replacement 63%, OE 27%, exports ~10%. Truck & bus ~56%, PLR ~27%, non-truck bias ~13%, 2/3W ~4%. Standalone: truck & bus 59%, PLR 25%, replacement 61%, OE 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Mexico (JK Tornel) decline QoQ, and was there an impairment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Mexico was sluggish in Q4 due to geopolitical volatility and US tariff uncertainty. FY26 revenue was steady at Rs.2,138 crore vs Rs.2,147 crore. No impairment was mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the price hike came in Q4 vs Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly in Q1 FY27. OEM price increases lag, and a further 5-6% hike is planned.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded, and what is the FY27 outlay?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash outlay of ~Rs.1,200 crore per year. Debt will be taken, supported by higher EBITDA; project funding is about 2:1 debt-to-equity. Leverage expected to stay comfortable at 2-3 year levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus funds from the Dec-2023 QIP, held in fixed deposits, have been gradually withdrawn and deployed into expansion projects, reducing interest income.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook and order book position?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand expected to stay buoyant in FY27, with strong or mid-single-digit growth in some categories. No OEM order cuts seen.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.5,000 crore capex in addition to the Rs.1,130 crore, and when does the Rs.1,130 crore finish?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the new plan is in addition. The Rs.1,130 crore is under implementation and will complete by Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material outlook for Q1 and Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material costs are rising ~18-19% in Q1 FY27. Some softening in crude is expected, which could ease raw material costs beyond Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How has competition responded to price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Competitors have taken price hikes in the same range (about 4-5%).

qa_highlights.question: How will JK Tyre defend its position against new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an entrenched OEM and fleet position, premium products, the selling miles fleet programme, and OEM technical norms in passenger cars.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for 2/3W and off-highway?
qa_highlights.answer: 2/3W growth via productivity gains and outsourcing, with more outsourcing planned. No specific off-highway plan was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Rs.6,000 crore outlay over 3-4 years be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. FY26 cash generation exceeded Rs.1,600 crore; the outlay includes planned borrowings and internal accruals. Spending can rise if needed.

risks_watch: Raw material costs guided up 18-20% (CFO 18-19%) in Q1 FY27; margin sustainability depends on speed and size of price hikes (4-5% taken, further 5-6% under way) and OEM lag effects

Execution and funding of Rs.6,110 crore expansion (Rs.1,130 crore to Q3 FY28; Rs.4,980 crore in phases to FY29) at ~Rs.1,200 crore annual cash outlay, with debt-to-equity about 2:1 on projects; net debt/EBITDA is 2.13x at 31-Mar-26
Mexico (JK Tornel) Q4 slowdown tied to US tariff uncertainty; Q4 revenue Rs.378 crore; USMCA review due July 2026
Competitive entry: management mentioned a large off-highway player's plans in TBR, PCR and 2/3W; peer warned of possible demand moderation from price hikes, with no management view on Q2/H2 impact
West Asia crisis supply disruptions and rupee weakness; management hopes for US-Iran peace talks to normalise energy markets by H2 FY27
key_quotes: Keeping in view the ongoing situation, raw material prices are expected to go up by 18 -20% in Q1FY27 from Q4.
We have not seen any order books getting cut from any of the OEM, be CV s, passenger or any other line.
So, these total expansions of Rs.6,110 crores will be completed by FY29.
Yes, the Rs.5,000 crore worth of capex is in addition to Rs.1,130 crore expansion plan.

Cautious on input costs and geopolitics: management said the West Asia crisis is pressuring margins and gave no view on Q2/H2 demand impact from price hikes. Evasive on the Mexico Q4 decline, attributing it to tariff uncertainty without quantifying it.

rows.why: Raw material costs guided up 18-20% in Q1 FY27 vs a 12.9% Q4 EBITDA margin; price hikes of 4-5% taken plus 5-6% more under way, with softening in crude possibly giving relief from Q3 FY27, so margin direction depends on pass-through speed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY28 for Rs.1,130 cr; phases to FY29 for Rs.4,980 cr
rows.why: Rs.1,130 cr TBR/PCR expansion is under implementation with completion by Q3 FY28 (TBR and PCR capacity +24%), and the Rs.4,980 cr brownfield plan is approved; however, neither adds capacity within the next 2-4 quarters beyond the Q3 FY28 date.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 domestic volumes +21% YoY (OE +42%), management expects demand buoyant in FY27 with mid-single-digit growth in some categories and no OEM order cuts, with utilisation above 90%.

rows.why: Board approved Rs.4,980 cr further brownfield expansion on top of Rs.1,130 cr under implementation; utilisation above 90% for FY26 means further capex is already in motion, with ~Rs.1,200 cr annual cash outlay.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance upgrade was given; management flagged rising raw material costs of 18-20% in Q1 FY27 and West Asia pressure on margins, and gave no view on Q2/H2 demand impact from price hikes.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw material cost up 18-20% in Q1 FY27 against price hikes of 4-5% taken plus 5-6% under way, with OEM pricing lagging, so margin squeeze risk exists; a peer warned of demand moderation from price hikes.

rows.label: Further 5-6% price hike under way
rows.why: Following 4-5% replacement and 5-7% export hikes already taken, a further 5-6% is under way to offset 18-20% raw material inflation, with competitors taking hikes in the same range (4-5%).

rows.label: Mexico (JK Tornel) US tariff exposure
rows.why: Mexico Q4 revenue Rs.378 cr and EBITDA Rs.24 cr; management called Q4 sluggish on US tariff uncertainty, with FY26 revenue flat at Rs.2,138 cr vs Rs.2,147 cr.

rows.label: Leverage rising with capex
rows.why: Consolidated debt rose to Rs.4,445 cr from Rs.4,081 cr and net debt/EBITDA is 2.13x, while the ~Rs.1,200 cr annual cash outlay is funded partly by debt at about 2:1 debt-to-equity on the projects.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery, demand and the Rs.4,980 cr expansion, but cautious on input costs (raw materials +18-20% in Q1 FY27) and geopolitics, and evasive on the Mexico Q4 decline; analysts probed price-hike pass-through and funding of the Rs.6,110 cr plan.

530007|2026-06.headline: JK Tyre Q1FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell to Rs.268 crore (6.8% margin) from Rs.424 crore, as raw material costs rose ~20% QoQ.
530007|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 2% YoY to Rs.3,956 crore, while EBITDA dropped about 37% YoY to Rs.268 crore and PAT was Rs.43 crore. India domestic volumes grew 25% YoY, led by 42% OEM growth, but India revenue growth was about 14%, implying weaker realisations. Mexico (JK Tornel) was hit by input shortages and a productivity-related slowdown, and net debt rose Rs.500 crore QoQ to Rs.4,945 crore. Management guided to margin recovery from the second half, with 10-11% FY27 operating margins as the working assumption.

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity / Net debt to EBITDA

segments.name: India domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes grew 25% YoY across replacement and OE; OEM volumes grew 42%, TBR OE +18% and TBR replacement +15%. Net sales realisation rose about 5% QoQ and about 4% YoY on a standalone basis.

segments.name: Passenger lines (PCR)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 10% YoY, led by OEM. Sixteen-inch and above rim sizes make up 35% of PCR sales volume.

segments.name: Farm
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 31% YoY, with OEM +35% and replacement +25%.

segments.name: 2/3-wheeler
segments.commentary: OE volumes grew 17% and replacement volumes grew 48% YoY.

segments.name: JK Tornel (Mexico)
segments.commentary: Output was constrained by input shortages (bead wire largely from China, shipping disruption) and a productivity-negotiation slowdown, since resolved. An analyst cited a decline of about 82%, which management did not dispute.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth expected at good double digits (about 10-11%), driven by price hikes and volume, with new capacity running fully by Q3 FY27.
FY27 operating margin guided at about 10-11%, which management said may be below FY26; margins expected to improve progressively from H2 FY27, returning to 11-13%.
Further price increases of 8-9% planned; cumulative increase of about 11% taken in the replacement market to date.
Raw material costs expected to rise a further 8-10% in Q2 from higher-cost inventory, then stabilise; natural rubber expected to stay range-bound after some softening.
Total debt expected to rise by Rs.500-700 crore in FY27 to fund capex and working capital.
Mexico expected to deliver better results than Q1 in the remaining three quarters.
capex_capacity: Expansion plan worth Rs.4,980 crore for PCR and TBR at the Chennai tyre plant (about 24% capacity addition over roughly four years, per management).
Capacity additions in the next financial year to be mainly TBR and passenger car, plus balancing at Banmore; expected to add about 7% to current installed capacity.
Indian capacity utilisation about 95%; consolidated utilisation about 80%. TBR and 2/3W near full; PCR about 95%; LCV and farm above 95%.
Upgradation and modernisation project under way at JK Tornel, Mexico.
demand_pricing: Indian auto retail sales grew more than 15% (FADA source); PV +23%, CV +14%, 2/3W +14%, farm +22%.
Price hike of about 5% taken in Q1, applied in monthly staggered steps; 8-9% more planned, with OEM price increases flowing with a lag.
Natural rubber (RSS4) prices softening in India; management hopes for a fall by next quarter.
Export volumes from India rose 2% QoQ.
Product mix at consolidated level: truck and bus 56%, passenger line radial 27%, 2/3W 5%, others 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Vijay Kumar (Axis Capital): India volume growth of 25% versus India revenue growth of about 14%; does this imply lower pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic volumes grew 25% YoY; net effective price increase was about 4% YoY on a standalone basis and NSR rose about 5% QoQ. OEM prices lag, so the full effect will show in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Vijay Kumar: What drove the Mexico weakness, and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Bajoria cited constrained inputs (bead wire from China, shipping disruption, container shortages, NR up about 18%) and productivity negotiations with workers; these are resolved and management expects better results in the remaining three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Bhagnani (Living Root Analytics): What margin and revenue trajectory for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins to improve progressively from H2 FY27 once raw material costs stabilise; price hikes should cover the RM increase except 1-2%. FY27 revenue growth guided at about 10-11%; operating margin about 10-11%.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Bhagnani: Will debt rise this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, net debt is expected to rise by Rs.500-700 crore in FY27 due to capex disbursements and working capital, partly offset by repayments and internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Krish Jain (NAFA): What capacity utilisation and additions are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: India utilisation about 95%, consolidated about 80%. Capacity additions of about 7% by next financial year, mainly TBR and PCR, with the full run-rate expected by Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Digant Shah (DAM Capital): Will Mexico production normalise to Q3/Q4 revenue levels? What is the USMCA status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected the record: it was a slowdown, not a strike. Production has resumed and is near normal, with similar topline expected. USMCA has been renewed for 10 years.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on RM cost stabilisation after a further 8-10% increase expected in Q2 FY27 from high-cost inventory.
Mexico output recovery and the sustainability of the bead wire supply from China amid US-China tensions.
Net debt rising to about Rs.5,400-5,600 crore by year-end (Rs.500-700 crore increase) with net debt/EBITDA at 2.56x in Q1, against a margin recovery that is not yet visible.
Price hike realisation (8-9% planned) versus volume response, with OEM price lags.
EV tyre replacement life: management cited about 5-10% shorter life due to higher torque, with the degree depending on usage.
key_quotes: And I can only assure you that this year, in the remaining 3 quarters, we will be definitely showing you better results than in Q1.
But yes, in the range of about 10% to 11%, if I have to make a guess.

Mr. Vijay, as I said that during this quarter, the operations at Tornel, Mexico were impacted due to the ongoing geopolitical disruptions resulting in constrained availability of key inputs, which also affected the output.
Thank you. First of all, I want to make a small correction that it was not a strike, it was a slowdown.
530007|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on demand and the medium-term outlook, citing record industry growth and 25% domestic volume growth. It was cautious on near-term margins, guiding only to a 10-11% FY27 operating margin "if I have to make a guess" and avoiding a firm Mexico recovery figure. Answers on Mexico were defensive, with the CEO-level speaker correcting the "strike" framing and asserting normalisation without quantifying it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides margins back to 11-13% in H2 FY27 from 6.8% in Q1 as 8-9% further price hikes flow through, but Q2 raw material costs rise another 8-10% from high-cost inventory, so the recovery is conditional on RM stabilising.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 for next-FY additions; Q4 FY27 for Chennai Rs.4,980
rows.why: Approved Rs.4,980 crore Chennai PCR/TBR expansion adds about 24% capacity over roughly four years, and about 7% of installed capacity (TBR, PCR, Banmore balancing) comes next FY with full run-rate by Q3 FY27; India utilisation is about 95%.

rows.label: Volume growth

530007|2026-09.headline: JK Tyre Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue hit a record Rs.4,850 crore (+20% YoY), with EBITDA margin up to 7.1% from 6.8% despite raw material inflation.

Consolidated EBITDA rose 28% QoQ to Rs.343 crore and PAT to Rs.60 crore, as NSR increases of about 7% QoQ offset a further ~9% QoQ rise in raw material costs. Net debt rose Rs.751 crore QoQ to Rs.5,696 crore on working capital for higher RM prices and capex. Management guided to a further 4-5% RM basket increase and 4-5% NSR increase in Q3.

segments.commentary: OE volumes up 76% YoY and replacement up 9% YoY; management cites category growth of high single digits in the medium term.

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs.479 crore and EBITDA Rs.23 crore in Q2 as operations resumed; OEM volumes to the US expected to return to last-year levels in Q3-Q4, and Mexico-to-US exports grew triple-digit QoQ in volume.

530019|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs 2,290 Cr, but EBITDA margin fell 272 bps to 15.7% on SPECT supply shortfall and Montreal under-absorption.
530019|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 19% YoY to Rs 2,290 Cr on radiopharma, allergy immunotherapy, CDMO sterile injectables and generics, while EBITDA rose only 2% to Rs 363 Cr. Normalized PAT was Rs 129 Cr, down YoY on higher depreciation and interest. For FY26, revenue grew 14% to Rs 8,280 Cr, EBITDA rose 8% to Rs 1,326 Cr and margin fell 99 bps to 15.9%, mainly from lower CMO Montreal output in H2. Management frames FY27 margins as a two-half story, with H1 hit by SPECT shortages and H2 expected at 17-18%.

530067|2026-03.headline: CSL Finance Q4 FY26 PAT rose 2% YoY to Rs 19.4 crore while SME retail stalled; wholesale carried growth and FY26 PAT rose 19% to Rs 86 crore.
530067|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed a split performance: wholesale kept growing on AUM, asset quality and profitability, while SME retail lagged amid industry consolidation and new competition in the sub-Rs 10 lakh secured segment. AUM reached Rs 1,448 crore (up 21% YoY) with the mix now 69% wholesale and 31% SME retail. Q4 PAT of Rs 19.4 crore was up 2% YoY but down 7% QoQ on higher ECL provisions and write-offs, and Gross NPA rose to 1.1%. Management guided to 15-25% AUM growth for FY27 and expects SME retail to normalise gradually.

vs 0.46% Q4 FY25 and 1% Q3 FY26

segments.commentary: Now 69% of AUM and described as the key growth driver; management cites strong collections over the last two quarters and no current stress on newly boarded accounts. Off-book co-lending deals were closed in Q4 to build fee income.

segments.name: SME retail
segments.commentary: Now 31% of AUM, down from a peak of 48% in FY23-24; growth has been weak for 12-15 months. Ticket focus is Rs 7-50 lakh after exiting the Rs 10 lakh segment, and the company is consolidating low-productivity branches.

Co-lending and joint lending to grow fee income in FY27 and beyond.

Net branch additions were nil during the year as branches were reshuffled and relocated.
Management plans to focus on productivity of existing branches for the next 3 months before resuming openings from Q3 FY27.
No geographic expansion beyond current region planned for the next 12-15 months due to limited funds.
demand_pricing: SME retail hit by over-leveraged borrowers in the lowest income strata, stagnant MSME incomes, and new aggressive lenders (formerly MFI-heavy) in sub-Rs 10 lakh secured SME lending.
Management attributes SME slowdown to senior team changes, higher branch attrition, tighter policies and geopolitical caution.
Wholesale co-lending: sole lending for tickets up to roughly Rs 30-40 crore; co-lenders brought in for larger tickets, with the company retaining 10%-15% to 40% stake.
Wholesale focus is the daily NCR market, a niche where management says ample opportunity exists.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 disbursements fall 16% QoQ and what is the FY27 disbursement outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wholesale is lumpy and should be judged annually; Q4 was lower after an elevated Q3, and prepayments and collections affected the number. No absolute disbursement guidance was given beyond AUM growth of 15-25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new ECL framework?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board approved a new ECL policy this quarter, more objective and based on 4-5 years of SME portfolio performance, per RBI direction. Management said it would have produced a lower provision than the current conservative approach, so no adverse impact is expected from FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the higher tax rate in Q4 and what is FY27 tax expected to be?
qa_highlights.answer: Ind AS fee amortisation creates a gap versus income-tax computation; the weighted average effective tax rate is expected around 27% versus the 25.17% normal rate.

qa_highlights.question: How does the co-lending / off-book strategy work and what is the ticket split?
qa_highlights.answer: Co-lending earns processing and other fees, with no risk sharing as in DA. Sole lending up to about Rs 30-40 crore; co-lenders are onboarded for larger tickets to manage risk and cash flows.

qa_highlights.question: Why has SME share fallen and what is the strategy to rebuild it?
qa_highlights.answer: SME share fell from a 48% peak in FY23-24 to 31%. Causes cited: senior team changes, branch attrition, tighter policies, and a cautious stance over the last 3-4 months. Strategy is to source only better-CIBIL customers, consolidate branches, and re-observe policies for 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost and NPA outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost around 0.5% is expected to stabilise. Management said the recent NPAs came from large SME tickets of Rs 50 lakh to Rs 1.5 crore that were stopped; SARFAESI resolutions should offset fresh slippages.

risks_watch: SME retail recovery depends on macro improvement; management has not provided SME growth numbers and is in a cautious phase for 2-3 months.
Gross NPA rose to 1.1% from 1% in Q3 FY26; watch whether resolutions via SARFAESI bring it down as guided.
Wholesale asset quality is untested in a stressed cycle; RBI standard provisioning on project finance rose to an average of 0.98% from 0.8%.
Co-lending fee income is a new revenue stream whose scale is not quantified.
Q4 disbursement and AUM trajectory is lumpy, and Q4 FY27 AUM growth could be flat if the 15-25% guidance is not met.

rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at Rs 1,400-1,500 cr (~20% growth at midpoint), backed by a Rs 1,250 cr executable group order book and a KSA 0-12 month pipeline of ~$22 mn, with crane utilisation at ~86%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation ~86% on crane rental with the Rs 652 cr pool already board-approved and a planned KSA/Qatar depot whose location and timing are undisclosed, so further capex disclosure is probable.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue (Rs 1,400-1,500 cr) and EBITDA (Rs 525-575 cr) guidance were merely reiterated, and management guides a lower blended margin as Sangreen grows toward one-third of revenue.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: ECL charge of ~Rs 6.2 cr, FX MTM of Rs 1.4 cr and a one-time incentive pushed core crane margin to 47% from 53%, and GCC DSO of 201 days plus ~15% of the Rs 686 cr renewable order book possibly slipping into FY28 threaten the Rs 525-575 cr EBITDA guide, though guidance was held.

rows.label: GCC/KSA DSO normalisation (201 days)
rows.why: GCC DSO at 201 days with management citing significant July collections and improvement visible in Q2 results, but not yet verified.

rows.label: Gross D/E within 0.72x ceiling; net 0.3-0.7x
rows.why: Gross D/E at 0.54x versus 0.72x ceiling and a treasury surplus of over Rs 300 cr, with management comfortable on the ceiling.

rows.label: Renewable E&C order book ~Rs 686 cr execution
rows.why: Order book is already above FY26 renewable revenue, but ~15% (about Rs 100 cr) may slip into FY28 on client delays and POCM recognition.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, KSA and the Rs 1,250 cr order book, but defensive on the 6-point core crane margin drop and evasive on lifting capacity, blended borrowing cost and E&C margin sustainability, while analysts pushed on margins, ECL and GCC working capital.

530073|2026-09.headline: Sanghvi Movers Q2 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR277 crore; FY27 guidance reaffirmed at INR1,400-1,500 crore total income and INR525-575 crore EBITDA.
530073|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR277 crore (+32% YoY) with EBITDA of INR106 crore (+20%) and a 36% margin, while PAT was INR40 crore versus INR36 crore a year earlier. Revenue fell sequentially from Q1, which management attributed to renewable project phasing, monsoon slowdown in India and crane deployment timing in the Middle East. Order book rose to INR1,582 crore as of 23 October 2026 (+26% from INR1,253 crore in July), and the CFO said the book is executable within FY27 with about 8-10% expected to slip. Capex ceiling was revised to INR583 crore, with part of the KSA capex deferred to FY28 due to shipping and port constraints.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR36 crore in Q2 FY26
equal to 82% of FY26 full-year, per management

financial_highlights.metric: Net worth / gross debt / net debt (30 Sep 2026)
financial_highlights.value: INR1,398 crore / INR805 crore / INR391 crore (after INR414 crore treasury)

segments.name: Crane rental - India and Botswana
segments.commentary: H1 total income INR406 crore, fleet utilisation 78%, yield 2.24%, EBITDA margin 46%. Q2 India utilisation 71% vs 86% in Q1; yield 2.20% vs 2.04% a year ago. Segment DSO about 89 days.

segments.name: Crane rental - GCC (Saudi Arabia, Qatar)
segments.commentary: H1 total income INR39 crore, utilisation 86%, yield 3.80% vs 3.5% target, EBITDA margin 24% attributed by management to start-up costs. DSO fell to 165 days from 201 days in Q1.

segments.name: Renewables engineering and construction (E&C)
segments.commentary: H1 total income INR365 crore with EBITDA margin about 14%; TTM ROCE 63%. About 36% of H1 group revenue; FY27 mix now expected around 60:40 crane rental to E&C vs earlier 2/3:1/3. DSO below 60 days.

segments.name: Project EPC
segments.commentary: About 2% of H1 group revenue. Being wound down; management expects revenue recognition to complete in Q2-Q3 FY27 and to reverse the negative EBITDA shown on page 31.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reaffirmed: total income INR1,400-1,500 crore and EBITDA INR525-575 crore; management said the H1 result supports these numbers.
Management expects 8-10% of the INR1,582 crore order book (about INR140-160 crore) to spill into FY28, which it says keeps FY27 within the INR1,400-1,500 crore range.
FY27 gross debt to equity projected at about 0.70-0.75x, versus 0.72x ceiling cited earlier.
FY27 capex ceiling INR583 crore: INR182 crore capitalised in H1 (INR90 crore in Q2), about INR401 crore pending in H2, with capex typically back-ended to Q3-Q4 after monsoon.
Saudi capex of INR80-90 crore postponed to FY28; management expects GCC EBITDA margin to improve in the next full year.
Around INR120 crore of term-loan repayments due in H2 FY27.
Management expects Q3-Q4 yield and utilisation to improve, which it says will absorb fixed costs and average out margins.
Blended ROCE guidance for FY27 and FY28 given on page 18 of the investor presentation; management cites about 16% ROCE and about 16% ROE as targets.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex ceiling revised to INR583 crore including FY26 carry-forward; INR182 crore capitalised in H1 FY27 and about INR401 crore pending in H2. Management says about 96% of the planned pool is revenue-generating assets.
KSA capex of INR80-90 crore deferred to FY28 because of shipping, port congestion and delayed crane delivery; procurement is being aligned with contracted demand.
Management said it is waiting for shipping costs to normalise before mobilising some larger cranes planned for the Middle East.
Target yields: India about 2%, KSA 3.8-4%. Management said crane-level IRR is an internal metric and is not disclosed.
demand_pricing: Group order book INR1,582 crore as of 23 October 2026: India and Botswana crane rental INR683 crore, GCC crane rental INR45 crore, renewables E&C INR854 crore. Group enquiry pipeline about INR6,700 crore.
India H1 crane utilisation 78% within a historical 73-84% range; management expects H2 seasonal pickup after monsoon.
GCC yield fell to 3.80% in H1 from about 4% in Q1 because overtime work dropped in Q2 due to supply-chain disruption. Management said yields should recover next quarter.
Management said it does not pass cost escalation to customers in E&C; contracts are fixed price.
Management said it has framework discussions and MoUs with OEMs that establish it as an exclusive EMC partner (slide 24).

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR1,582 crore order book be executed this year, and could FY27 revenue exceed guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the book is executable in FY27 but E&C carries about a 10% deferral risk. Chairman Rishi Sanghvi reaffirmed guidance, citing grid, PPA, WTG supply, site availability and monsoon delays into Q3, and said 8-10% of the order book (INR140-160 crore) may spill into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East margin outlook given breakeven, and whether delayed capex could be brought forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the planned INR80-90 crore capex is postponed to FY28, the KSA business is EBITDA positive and generated cash profit in Q2, and margin should improve in next year's guidance. Shipping normalisation, which may take a long time, decides when larger cranes can be mobilised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the India crane margin fall from 53% to 46% when other income rose?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the one-time employee incentive was about 1% of margin and PF law changes plus insurance costs are the other operating cost drag. Management said contract labour costs will keep pressure on margin, offset by higher Q3-Q4 yield and utilisation. Other income includes an insurance claim on an impaired asset.

qa_highlights.question: Could Middle East strategy shift to India if the conflict persists, given GCC is only about 3-4% of order book and gross block?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the cranes are mobile and one 600-tonne crane was moved from India to KSA during the conflict. Management said GCC has about SAR216 million of live enquiries that it cannot service yet for lack of cranes on site. Gross block data is on page 29.

qa_highlights.question: How has E&C grown revenue over 40% while industry installations were flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman cited more than 20 GW of wind erection by the parent, full-scope services to independent power producers, and larger composite jobs. He said Sangreen Future Renewables has a strong order book, with the customer base reflecting the delivery record.

qa_highlights.question: Why did GCC yield fall to 3.8% from about 4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said lower overtime in Q2 due to supply-chain disruption in manpower and materials at site reduced yield. CFO said yield should rise in the next quarter, though he added 'ideally'.

qa_highlights.question: Are equity raises or a subsidiary IPO planned to fund expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said no equity raise is being considered at this point.

risks_watch: GCC execution and yield: shipping, port congestion and manpower shortages delay deployment; GCC EBITDA margin was 24% in H1 and yield fell to 3.80%.
Order book conversion: 8-10% of the INR1,582 crore book may slip, and the company flagged internal execution challenges in E&C.
Margin pressure from contract labour, PF law changes and insurance costs in the India crane business; India crane EBITDA margin fell to 46%.
Rising rates: RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps in October 2026, and weighted average borrowing cost is 8.28%.
Project EPC wind-down: management expects the negative EBITDA to reverse in Q2-Q3 FY27, which needs to be verified.
Heavy H2 capex of about INR401 crore, mostly in Q3-Q4, and about INR120 crore of term-loan repayments in H2 FY27; gross debt to equity is set to rise to 0.70-0.75x.
530073|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on demand and visibility, but cautious on near-term execution: management reaffirmed guidance and called the Middle East deferral a timing issue. It was evasive on the India margin bridge, and on the INR9 crore PPE impairment, which it ties to an insurance claim booked in other income.
key_quotes: So as a management who believes in abundant and prudent cautious guidance, we believe that we still reaffirm what we have guided for between INR1,400 crores to INR1,500 crores.
So shipping and port disruption in West Asia have delayed new crane deployment in Saudi Arabia, and we have moved part of the capex to FY28. So this is a timing issue, not a demand issue.
No at this point of time we are not looking to raise any equity.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects Q3-Q4 yield and utilisation to recover from India utilisation of 71% (vs 86% in Q1) and GCC yield of 3.80% (vs about 4% in Q1), but India crane EBITDA margin fell to 46% from 53% on labour, PF and insurance costs, and group EBITDA margin is 36%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About INR401 crore of the INR583 crore FY27 capex pool is pending in H2, mostly in Q3-Q4, with INR182 crore already capitalised in H1 and about 96% of the pool revenue-generating, though KSA capex of INR80-90 crore slips to FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book of INR1,582 crore (+26% since July) is executable in FY27 with 8-10% (INR140-160 crore) expected to slip, and H1 revenue grew 36% YoY to INR657 crore, though India utilisation fell to 71% in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 78% for H1 (India 71% in Q2) and KSA capex of INR80-90 crore is deferred to FY28 with no new capacity announced; management is still waiting on shipping costs before mobilising larger Middle East cranes, so a new capex plan is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 total income guidance of INR1,400-1,500 crore was reaffirmed, not raised, and management says 8-10% of the order book may spill into FY28, which caps upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 total income of INR689 crore needs H2 to deliver the rest of the INR1,400-1,500 crore range, while the INR140-160 crore order-book slip, GCC yield at 3.80%, and India margin pressure from labour and PF costs all carry risk.

rows.label: INR1,582 crore order book executable in FY27
rows.why: Book is up 26% since July to INR1,582 crore with INR854 crore in renewables E&C, and management says 8-10% (INR140-160 crore) will spill into FY28.

rows.label: Gross debt to equity rising to 0.70-0.75x
rows.why: Gross debt to equity was 0.58x at 30 Sep 2026, but H2 capex of about INR401 crore and about INR120 crore of term-loan repayments push FY27 gross debt to equity to 0.70-0.75x, against a 0.72x ceiling.

rows.label: Project EPC wind-down reverses negative EBITDA
rows.why: Project EPC is about 2% of H1 revenue and management expects revenue recognition to finish in Q2-Q3 FY27, reversing the negative EBITDA, though this is not yet verified.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, order visibility and reaffirmed FY27 guidance, and cautious on GCC shipping, E&C execution and India margins; analysts pushed on the India margin bridge, GCC yield, E&C growth and order book conversion.

530075|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 EBITDA rose to Rs.90 crore (about 71% margin, Rs.83 crore or 69% ex one-off) on flat volumes; exit guidance 2,500 BOEPD, 5,000 BOPD by FY29.
530075|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs.121.7 crore and net profit of Rs.57.3 crore, with volumes flat QoQ and realised oil down to $88.2/bbl from $95.3/bbl. Management reiterated a 2,500 BOEPD exit for FY27 and 3,500 BOEPD next year, with 5,000 BOPD targeted by FY29 on onshore assets only. The company signed two KG Onshore and Cambay Basin revenue sharing contracts (DSF IV) on 22 October 2026. Bakrol's 10-well campaign is complete, Karjisan's seven-well campaign is under way, and October production was about 2,000 BOEPD. Balance sheet is debt-free with about Rs.100 crore cash and liquid investments and Rs.780 crore equity.

segments.name: Cambay Basin (Bakrol, Karjisan, Lohar, Cambay)
segments.commentary: Bakrol average about 950 BOE/d in October after the 10-well drilling and fracking campaign; Karjisan (PSC, royalty and cess under 5% of top line) has seven wells planned this fiscal, two drilled but not yet on production. Cambay field (50% JV with Synergia) has one to two optionality wells planned for late Feb/early Mar 2027.

segments.name: KG Onshore
segments.commentary: Seven new discoveries added, about nine fields in total, of which only Mukkamala is producing; management says resource base may be larger than the offshore portfolio. Single-rig, multi-well appraisal planned; a resource estimate to follow after third-party reserve work. Wells expected to cost about $10 million more than Cambay's roughly $1.5 million.

segments.name: Duarmara (Assam, JV)
segments.commentary: Duarmara-4Z found oil in the TIPAM-1 zone rather than the expected gas; oil recirculated to surface twice. Well cost about Rs.60-70 crore, and a plan covering wells 1, 2 and 4 is due over the next five to six months. Gas monetisation is constrained by Assam's lack of National Grid connection.

segments.name: Offshore
segments.commentary: Treated as optionality; excluded from the 5,000 BOPD guidance, with management focus shifting to it in FY28-29.

guidance_outlook: Exit FY27 at about 2,500 BOEPD, with Karjisan's seven wells and the Cambay optionality wells as the main drivers; October production was about 2,000 BOEPD (one answer cited about 1,950).
Exit FY28 at about 3,500 BOEPD and FY29 at about 5,000 BOEPD, onshore only; minimal contribution assumed from KG and Duarmara.
EBITDA margin expected to stay above 65% for the year; management says its endeavour is to keep margins in line.
Capex guided at Rs.250 crore for FY27 (against Rs.220 crore in FY26), with funding via internal accruals for now; no commitment on debt or equity raises.
KG Onshore development plan and capex guidance to come after field development plans are filed with regulators; Duarmara oil plan in five to six months.
capex_capacity: Bakrol 10-well campaign complete (drilling and fracking); production response showing Bakrol as a multi-year growth field.
Karjisan: seven wells planned for FY27; two drilled, first perforation expected within about a week, rig back on site.
Cambay field: one to two optionality wells planned for late Feb/early Mar 2027; field area about 160 sq km.
Duarmara: well cost Rs.60-70 crore; TIPAM-1 oil zone; partner alignment needed.
Historical capex: Rs.51 crore (FY23), Rs.160 crore (FY24), Rs.87 crore (FY25), Rs.220 crore (FY26), Rs.250 crore (FY27 target).
demand_pricing: Pricing is linked to international crude benchmarks; Cambay crude sells at about a 10% discount to dated Brent on average, with most volumes to Indian Oil and about 20% to private buyers at a slightly higher discount.
Realised oil ran about $76 in July, $84 in August and above $100 in September.
Royalty and cess are about 30% of top line in Bakrol and Cambay versus under 5% in Karjisan, averaging about 15-16% of revenue.
Variable handling cost is about $1-1.5 per barrel on ONGC tolling; fixed costs are about 70-75% of the cost base.
Management's investment hurdle: double-digit returns at $65-70/bbl, cash back within one to one-and-a-half years, and no loss at $50/bbl.
Assam gas is sold at a discount to APM prices because Assam is not connected to the National Grid; oil is easier to truck out.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins above 65% be sustained for the full year as costs stay flat while volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed costs are 70-75% of the cost base and incremental barrels are cheaper in Cambay; KG will add establishment costs, but margins should hold. Management's stated aim is to keep margins in line, not a firm guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: How much incremental revenue will Karjisan and Bakrol add, and does the 2,500 exit depend on Cambay?
qa_highlights.answer: Bakrol is at about 950 BOE/d. Karjisan's seven wells are already in the 2,500 exit figure, which management said has no ambiguity; Cambay optionality wells sit outside it and could take production beyond 5,000.

qa_highlights.question: How will KG Onshore be funded and ramped up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to decide between internal accruals, debt or equity; it will start with one rig, drill a couple of wells and then decide on a bigger campaign. Wells cost about $10 million more than Cambay wells.

qa_highlights.question: What pricing formula and price range should be used for sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is set by a crude-yield-based discount to dated Brent (about 10%), and investments are screened at $50-70/bbl. Management gave no explicit bear-to-bull range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Duarmara oil potential, capex per well and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Well cost Rs.60-70 crore with 3.5 km wells. Oil is light, and flow and frac options are being studied. A concrete estimate is expected next fiscal, not this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CWIP high and why are deferred tax liabilities rising?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs.100 crore of the Rs.190 crore CWIP is Duarmara, to be capitalised on production. Deferred tax is rising because drilling capex is fully expensed for tax; it may partly reverse if drilling slows.

risks_watch: Duarmara gas evacuation and oil development path are unresolved, with the TIPAM-1 oil zone yet to be tested and the JV partner to be aligned.
KG Onshore high-pressure, high-temperature wells cost about $10 million more each; no resource or reserve estimate yet.
Karjisan's seven wells and the Cambay optionality wells (with Synergia) need to deliver to reach 2,500 BOEPD exit and 5,000 BOPD by FY29.
Realisations are sensitive to crude; September's above-$100 prices lifted the average, and private buyers' purchasing has been limited at higher prices.
Growing deferred tax liability and the chance of a funding decision (debt or equity) once KG ramps up.
Management's first investor call; one-off Rs.6.5 crore refund included in other income.
530075|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning on the Cambay ramp-up, with a clear 2,500 BOEPD exit and 5,000 BOPD FY29 target. Cautious and deliberately vague on KG Onshore, Duarmara and offshore, explicitly declining to give capex, reserve or funding numbers beyond the onshore guidance.
key_quotes: So, at $65-$70, if a project gives me double-digit return and gets me back my cash within year to year and a half, that is a go project for me.
Karjisan has the best fiscals in our portfolio as of today, because it has concessional Cess and royalty rates to it, because it is still in its primary term as a production-sharing contract.
So, the 5000 barrel plant that you have has a very subdued KG or the Cambay optionality in it.
Oil does not need pipeline infrastructure. Oil I can just put into a truck to haul across 300 kilometers and sell to refiner somewhere, right?

financial_highlights.change: flat volumes QoQ; Q1 not stated

financial_highlights.value: Rs.90 crore (71% margin); Rs.83 crore (about 69%) excluding Rs.6.5 crore one-off refund

financial_highlights.change: down from Rs.7.5 crore in Q1
rose as new Bakrol wells came into production
nearly 5x vs Rs.11.8 crore in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.value: about 1,700 BOEPD production, revenue about Rs.254.8 crore, EBITDA about Rs.180 crore, net profit about Rs.112 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Cash, bank balances and liquid investments

financial_highlights.value: about Rs.190 crore, of which about Rs.100 crore is Duarmara

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin above 65% for FY27 (Q2 at 71%, or 69% ex Rs.6.5 crore one-off), with fixed costs at 70-75% of the cost base and incremental Cambay barrels cheaper, though it is an aim, not a firm guarantee and KG will add establishment costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Exit FY27 at about 2,500 BOEPD from October run-rate of about 2,000 BOEPD, driven by Karjisan's seven wells (two drilled, first perforation within about a week) and Cambay optionality wells planned for late Feb/early Mar 2027; the 2,500 exit already includes Karjisan but not Cambay optionality.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volumes rose from about 1,700 BOEPD H1 average toward the 2,000 BOEPD October run-rate and a 2,500 BOEPD FY27 exit, but Q2 volumes were flat QoQ and the ramp depends on wells not yet producing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is already guided at Rs.250 crore (up from Rs.220 crore), and KG Onshore development capex and a Duarmara oil plan (Rs.60-70 crore per well) will follow in five to six months or after field development plans are filed, but no figures are committed yet.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was held (2,500 BOEPD FY27 exit, 5,000 BOPD FY29), and October production of about 2,000 BOEPD plus Bakrol's 950 BOE/d and Karjisan's wells leave room, but realisations fell to $88.2/bbl from $95.3/bbl and September's above-$100 price lifted the average.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Exit and FY29 targets depend on Karjisan wells and Cambay optionality wells being delivered, and realisations are crude-sensitive (July about $76, August $84, September above $100), with private buyers limiting purchases at higher prices.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: KG Onshore (seven new discoveries, about nine fields, only Mukkamala producing) and Duarmara oil (TIPAM-1 zone) could add new production, but KG resource estimates and Duarmara plans are not due for several months and minimal KG/Duarmara contribution is assumed for FY28-29.

rows.label: Two KG Onshore and Cambay DSF IV revenue sharing contracts signed
rows.why: Two revenue sharing contracts (KG Onshore and Cambay Basin, DSF IV) were signed on 22 October 2026, adding acreage that supports the onshore growth story.

rows.label: Debt-free balance sheet with cash buffer for capex
rows.why: No borrowings and about Rs.100 crore cash and liquid investments against Rs.250 crore FY27 capex funded from internal accruals for now, though a debt or equity decision is possible once KG ramps up.

rows.label: Assam gas monetisation constrained by no National Grid link
rows.why: Assam gas sells at a discount to APM prices because Assam is not connected to the National Grid, so Duarmara's gas contribution is unlikely to add near-term revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Cambay and Karjisan ramp to a 2,500 BOEPD exit and held FY29 5,000 BOPD, but was cautious and vague on KG Onshore, Duarmara and offshore funding and capex; analysts pressed on margin sustainability, KG funding, and the crude sensitivity of realisations.

530117|2026-03.headline: Privi FY26 revenue rose 21.7% to INR2,582.9 crore and PAT 75% to INR327.5 crore, with a 25.76% EBITDA margin.
530117|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR725.70 crore (up 15.29% YoY), EBITDA INR184.41 crore (up 25.09%) at a 25.41% margin, and PAT INR95.66 crore versus INR63.57 crore a year earlier. For FY26, income grew 21.73% to INR2,582.92 crore, driven by about 6.5% volume growth, roughly 8% price increases and product mix. Management reiterated a 20%+ growth target and 20%+ EBITDA margins, with the first capex phase due by 30 June 2026 taking installed capacity to 54,000 MTPA. The PRIGIV JV turned profitable for the first time in Q4, and the merger with PFSPL and PBPL awaits NCLT approval.

segments.name: Standalone aroma chemicals (core)
segments.commentary: Management said demand for core aroma chemicals is steady, with about 70% of revenue from exports, mostly under contracts. Realisations rose from about INR450/kg to about INR600/kg over five years, per management.

segments.name: PRIGIV JV (with Givaudan, 51:49)
segments.commentary: Turned profitable in Q4 FY26 for the first time. Revenue is expected at about INR130 crore in FY27 versus INR55 crore last year, with an additional INR50 crore capex. It manufactures high-end specialty chemicals exclusively for Givaudan.

segments.name: Downstream / new specialty molecules
segments.commentary: Silver Amber, Amber Silk, Privilege and Privitolide are in commissioning, with one already commissioned. Ethyl maltol, maltol and cyclopentanone projects target mechanical completion by June 2027, with revenue expected over the next 18 months. Furfural backward integration is about 2 years away, and the vertical is said to reach about INR1,000 crore revenue.

guidance_outlook: Targets 20%+ revenue growth for the coming year on a standalone basis; the 20% excludes merged entities until the scheme is effective.
Expects to sustain 20%+ EBITDA margins going forward; one answer referenced a 24% margin and another 25%.
Long-term target of about INR5,000 crore revenue and INR1,000 crore+ EBITDA in 3 to 4 years, roughly 2x.
Post all three capex phases, standalone capacity is expected at about 72,000 MT, around mid-to-late 2028.
Expects the NCLT approval for the merger of PFSPL and PBPL into the parent during FY27, internally targeted for Q3 FY27.
Expects state incentives of about INR13 crore a year, based on 50% of the GST on in-state sales in Gujarat and Maharashtra.
capex_capacity: First capex phase to complete by 30 June 2026, taking installed capacity to 54,000 MTPA, with a calibrated ramp-up over the coming quarters.
Phase 2 of the multi-specialty aroma chemicals project is progressing as planned.

The three new-molecule projects (ethyl maltol, maltol, cyclopentanone) are in detailed engineering with procurement started; the 12 to 15 month build targets mechanical completion by June 2027, followed by about one month of trials.
A biomass-to-value-added-products demonstration plant with capex of about INR70-75 crore is in basic and detailed engineering, expected in about 12 months.
Furfural backward integration is expected around FY28-29, after first establishing the finished goods and sourcing furfural from outside in the meantime.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall sequentially in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil attributed it to the timing overlap of annual raw-material and finished-goods contracts, which fall into Q4 and Q1, and said the business should be judged on an annual basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth guidance inclusive of the proposed merged entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said the 20% is standalone as it stands today; the merged entities will be consolidated once the scheme takes effect.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital days rise amid the current situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Babani said any increase would be no more than 3-5%, because price rises tend to lengthen customer payment times.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the FY26 forex gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said forex gains of about INR14 crore were recorded in other income, as the company is a net exporter.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net-capacity and commissioning timelines after all three phases?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said about 72,000 MT standalone after the first three phases, with completion around June to September 2028.

Demand for the new molecules at lower price points (for example about $45/kg); management is still testing market elasticity.
Biotech demonstration plant economics and capex, which management called complex and still at engineering stage.

530117|2026-06.headline: Privi Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.22% YoY to Rs 666 crore; consolidated EBITDA Rs 167.47 crore at 24.58% margin, PAT Rs 83.2 crore.
530117|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 consolidated total income of Rs 681.42 crore (+20.01% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 167.47 crore (+18.73% YoY) at about 24.58% margin, and PAT of about Rs 83.2 crore versus Rs 61.46 crore a year earlier. Growth was attributed to volume, price and product mix. Phase-1 capacity expansion (48,000 to 54,000 MT) is slated to commercialise within about 15 days, while the Phase-2 completion timeline has slipped to September 2027 for the final 12,000 MT. Gross margin compression (about 650 bps YoY per an analyst) was explained as a base effect from low-cost raw materials in CY25 and a normalising RM/sales ratio of 52-55%.

segments.commentary: Management says camphor is about 4-6% of revenue (figures given as 5-6% and 4-5%), made via CST route; not treated as a strategic product.

Chairman: targeting ~20% CAGR with similar EBITDA margins, benchmarked off prior-year numbers.

Phase-2: additional 12,000 MT (54,000 to 66,000 MT) to be completed by September 2027; Phase-2 has commenced.
Phase-3 (multi-specialty aroma) expected to start around end-2026 or early 2027; funding mainly internal accruals with bank borrowing as needed.
Capex outlook for FY27 and next two years: Rs 850-900 crore, covering Phase-2 and Phase-3.
Post-merger, about 6,000 MT of Privi Fine Sciences capacity to be added to Privi portfolio. Utilisation at around 90% of installed capacity.
Demonstration plant in Navi Mumbai for 2 TPD biomass processing; 12-15 months to build, then about a year of operation before a large-scale plant (outside the 5K/1K plan).
demand_pricing: Demand described as healthy across fragrance and flavour value chain despite global headwinds; customers diversifying supply chains.
Growth attributed to volume, price increases and product mix; no quarterly volume/realisation split given (to be disclosed annually).
Crude-based raw materials ~15-18% of purchases; alpha-pinene from GTO at historic highs, but CST purchases are back-to-back with customers.
Management claims Iran war and Hormuz freight impact limited; Red Sea freight impact seen as ongoing for years with no margin concern.
Maltol and Ethyl Maltol >95% manufactured in China; Privi targets about one-quarter of global opportunity, with Ethyl Maltol demand from Indian pharma importers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall ~650 bps YoY to ~44.2% and what recovers in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited low-cost RM and high CY25 selling prices in the prior-year base; RM/sales guided at 52-55% on average. Management expects EBITDA margin near 24.6-25% via scale benefits and lower depreciation and interest.

qa_highlights.question: Phase-2 capacity date: June or September 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Clarified: the 6,000 MT Phase-1 tranche moved from June 2026 to September 2026; the 12,000 MT Phase-2 balance completes by September 2027. Guidance unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue from PRIGIV and its EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: PRIGIV revenue about Rs 18 crore in Q1 with EBITDA margin of about 14-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Alpha-pinene price rise impact?
qa_highlights.answer: CST purchases are back-to-back with customers; balance GTO-based alpha-pinene is at historic highs and costs are being passed on. Future direction not predicted.

qa_highlights.question: Phase-2/3 funding and debt levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily internal accruals, with bank borrowing as needed; debt/EBITDA and debt/equity to stay well below typical thresholds.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for this year and next two years, and new 5K/1K plan products?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex Rs 850-900 crore over this year and the next two. Furfural-based chemistry (about Rs 1,000 crore+ revenue), Musk T and about 10-11 specialty molecules; plants mechanically complete by mid-FY28.

530117|2026-09.headline: Privi Q2 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% to INR773.16 crore and EBITDA 16.7% to INR212.49 crore, with a 27.48% EBITDA margin and first-ever interim dividend of INR5 per share.
530117|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly total income of INR773.16 crore (up 13.9% YoY), EBITDA of INR212.49 crore (up 16.66%) and PAT of INR117.03 crore (up 24.61%). H1 PAT was INR201 crore, up about 29%. Phase 1 capacity expansion (48,000 to 54,000 MTPA) was completed as of 30 September 2026, with Phase 2 and Phase 3 capex still in progress. Management reiterated 20% annual growth and a path to INR5,000 crore revenue by 2030, but H1 volume growth was only about 7-7.5% and Q2 volume growth about 4%.

segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR68 crore with loss of about INR34 crore. Capacity of about 6,000 MTPA is in place but utilisation is held back by pending regulatory and pollution board approvals; management sees potential revenue of INR300-350 crore at full utilisation.

guidance_outlook: Management maintains 20% growth guidance for FY27 on an annual basis, despite H1 growth of about 15%; it expects H2 to be stronger than H1.
FY27-28 revenue expected close to INR3,750-4,000 crore with 20% growth maintained or exceeded; EBITDA margin to be held at current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Has the debottlenecking capacity commissioned by September 2026 started ramping, and what is utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil said expansion is complete, with part of volumes in Q3 and most in Q4 when annual contracts start; utilisation on expanded capacity is expected at 85-90%.

qa_highlights.question: Does management still hold 20% growth guidance when H1 grew about 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer confirmed 20% annual growth guidance, saying H1 is normally lower than H2 and investors should look at yearly numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin look flat ex-other income, and when were incentives received?
qa_highlights.answer: Iyer said incentives were INR1.62 crore in H1 FY27 vs INR9 crore last year, with INR12-15 crore expected in the next two quarters; margin held because fixed costs were spread over a larger base and RMC was about 52%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income high in Q1 and Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Iyer said it is mainly forex gains, as Privi is a net exporter and the dollar has favoured it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital trending down, and what is the long-term level?
qa_highlights.answer: Iyer said customers pay on time or early; cycle is below 100 days now and the long-term annual range is 105-110 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Privi Fine Sciences merger and its utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil said regulatory approvals are nearing completion; management expects the merger before FY-end. Utilisation is about 85%, but the expansion awaits pollution board permissions, and management expects revenue to rise from about INR100 crore toward INR250-300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue will the Phase 1-3 capex generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Iyer said Phase 2 could deliver about INR1,000 crore at full 12,000 MTPA capacity, Phase 3 (INR400-425 crore capex) about INR450-500 crore, with total about INR1,900 crore by 2030.

Phase 2 and 3 timelines (June-September 2027 completion, about INR1,000 crore spend) depend on execution; capex is still largely ahead.
Privi Fine Sciences / Privi Biotechnology (merger, 6,000 MTPA plant) remains loss-making at about INR34 crore loss in FY26 and depends on pending pollution board and regulatory permissions.
PRIGIV deleveraging (debt conversion to advance with multinational partners) is in process but has no timeline.
Q2 margin benefited from the prior-year INR9 crore incentive base and forex gains in other income; underlying margin gains are harder to isolate.
Two strategic JV agreements remain unsigned; management gave no timeline.
Freight and geopolitical exposure; management says limited impact, but freight is passed through on a quarterly basis with a lag.

530305|2026-03.headline: Piccadily Agro FY26 standalone revenue rose 28% to INR1,143 crore and PAT 33% to INR140 crore; management guides 60-70% Alco-Bev growth in FY27.
530305|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first year Piccadily crossed INR1,000 crore revenue, with standalone PBT up 33% to INR190 crore and PAT up 33% to INR140 crore. Q4 standalone revenue rose 33% YoY to INR364 crore, with PBT of INR63 crore and PAT of INR46 crore, while Q4 standalone EBITDA margin fell about 300 bps on a weaker sugar quarter and a higher distillery mix. Management announced a scheme of demerger of the sugar business into a separate listed entity, targeted for completion in FY27, and a change of statutory auditor (partner-level continuity). FY27 is guided as an exceptional year, with Alco-Bev growth of 60-70% in value terms, driven by capacity additions at Indri and the new Mahasamund (Chhattisgarh) plant.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of IMFL volume growth by brand (Indri, Cashmir, Camikara, Whistler) and channel split between CSD, HORECA, export and domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Why Indri grew only about 16% in FY26 against expectations of 25-30%, and whether there is brand fatigue.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said increased competition is not the main reason; supply was constrained during the expansion. Supply constraints are expected to ease from this year, allowing stronger growth.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 EBITDA margin decline: was it mix-driven, and what margin range is expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sugar margin fell to about 2% in Q4 FY26 from 11% a year earlier, with a higher distillery sale mix also contributing. Management guided FY27 Alco-Bev absolute EBITDA growth of 60-70% with margin flat to about 50 bps higher.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the INR300-350 crore incremental IMFL revenue in FY27 on a base of about INR500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to use of new Indri and Chhattisgarh capacity, previously constrained by supply, plus a new product pipeline expected to start from around Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for FY27 and the Scotland facility.
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex not more than INR25-30 crore, mainly barrels (85,000 to 1,00,000) with some warehouse and bottling expansion. Scotland distillery construction is starting, with completion over the next couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: what drove the 132% jump in short-term borrowings and the normalisation path?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowings funded higher receivables from IMFL sales and about INR100 crore of added malt inventory. Management expects to bring borrowings back to FY26 levels as sales grow 60-70% and malt inventory is monetised.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 47.3% branded growth and what is the Chhattisgarh contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Indri grew high double digits, Whistler more than 60%, and Camikara began contributing via CSD. Chhattisgarh contributed about Rs 5 crore from roughly 15 days of production.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin rise only 30 bps and how are costs trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to mix, with Indri the highest-margin product. Cost pressure from grain and fuel hit the distillery segment. Employee, distribution and brand investment costs rose ahead of H2 revenue, and management expects margins to recover as revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is there enough aged malt to support Indri growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. The company holds 87,000 filled barrels, which management called the largest in India, and sees no supply constraint for 18-20% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Indri scale ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to reach top-five single malt volumes of about 0.5 million cases in 4-5 years, implying about Rs 1,200 crore Indri revenue at current prices. Current capacity supports about 8-8.5 lakh cases if all malt went to Indri.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Chhattisgarh ethanol exposure a guidance risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 300-400 crore guidance is intact and that ethanol is a stopgap; the company plans branded products from Chhattisgarh. It declined to split ethanol and alco-bev revenue until Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt fall and what is the working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 10 crore of debt was repaid in Q1. Management plans no net debt increase this year, with larger reductions from FY28 after investment in liquid and barrels. Receivable days fell to about 100.

530307|2026-03.headline: Management flagged a 9% QoQ fall in Q4 export volume (44,500 MT vs 48,900 MT) from war-stranded shipments, and declined to quantify the Q1 spillover.
530307|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a profitable year and declared a dividend of INR 3 per share, but the transcript contains no reported P&L figures beyond the Q4 export volume. Management attributed FY26 gains to buying paddy/rice inventory when prices were low, and said prices have since risen about 30% from Nov-Dec to March. The West Asia conflict slowed shipments to Iran, Afghanistan (via Bandar Abbas) and some Iraqi ports, while Red Sea, Jordan (Aqaba), Egypt, Oman, Dubai and Saudi (Jeddah) routes continued. Freight and insurance increases are said to be passed through to buyers, with ECGC claims filed for extra war charges. Management declined to quantify Q1 spillover or EBITDA margin for Q1 and repeatedly said it was too early to comment on El Nino impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected EBITDA margin for Q1 FY27 given higher freight?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is premature to comment on margins, with business continuing and demand for essentials holding up.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 the next inflection point for revenue, after about 3-4 years at INR 1,400-1,500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Setia said cargo is still moving and that history shows growth after roughly three years of flat revenue; a large buyer is due to visit the factory the following week.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin profile structural or cyclical, and what happens if realisations fall 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin to buying inventory at low prices early in the season, with godowns full. It did not give a sensitivity to a 10% realisation fall.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle target?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Setia said the target is a maximum of 40-45 days. The moderator cited the current cycle at about 190 days (60 debtor days, 140 inventory days), and management said it would maintain it.

qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Mahy attributed the drop to shipments stuck en route due to the Iran conflict. The moderator said containers would be executed in Q1, and Gaurav confirmed the issue is resolved.

Digital initiatives: 50,000 new designs added monthly by dealers via AI room visualisation; online lead generation contributing sales for 350-plus dealers monthly.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins sustain around Q4 levels given gas price pressure, and have price hikes been taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the margin trajectory to continue; Q4 margin was 7.7% versus about 6% in Q3 (per management's description). Price hikes of about 20% were taken in March-April and further gradual increases are expected depending on gas and diesel prices.

qa_highlights.question: What are gas prices and the Q4 blended INR per SCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas pricing is formula-linked and changes every few days, with the mix moving from 80% formula to 55% normal and 45% spot. Overall gas prices are up about 30%, and Q4 blended cost averaged about INR45 per SCM.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company undertake capex now that debt is repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: No capacity capex is needed in FY27 given existing capacity; capex will be for maintenance, around INR10 crores plus or minus INR4-5 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue goes to marketing?
qa_highlights.answer: Marketing was 3.6% of revenue in FY26 and is expected to creep up toward about 4%, with no final decision taken.

qa_highlights.question: Will capacity utilisation rise above 80% and will the company gain share from unorganised players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide on FY27 utilisation, citing gas uncertainty. It said it is better placed to gain share from Morbi disruption due to its balance sheet and sell-out model, and that OBTX share could rise, though it has not quantified the split.

qa_highlights.question: How are price hikes expected to play out, and is there demand slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects realisations to readjust over about 3-4 months as gas costs normalise; tile is 1-2% of project cost, so customers are not expected to defer purchases. Management said it has seen no demand slowdown, with the Q4 volume growth figure cited.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR1.28 crore exceptional item and the fall in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: The exceptional item is the one-time labour code provision for retirement benefits at 50% of salary. Other expenses fell to INR31.8 crores from INR33.6 crores in Q4, mainly from lower travel and design costs; FY26 other expenses were at a similar level to FY25.

risks_watch: Gas price volatility and allocation cuts; formula-linked pricing changes every few days, and June Gujarat gas pricing is expected to rise about INR5 per cubic metre.
Demand after price hikes of about 20%: dealer destocking, working-capital squeeze and project wait-and-watch behaviour.
Q1 FY27 margin impact from the remaining energy cost increase, as cost increases began 9-10 March.
Morbi reopening pace and labour constraints, which could change competitive pricing; some pricing may reverse as gas costs ease within about 3-4 months.
Adhesives and anti-static product contribution remains small; the adhesive business is still at pilot stage.
530365|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on profitability, the balance sheet and market share opportunity, but cautious and evasive on forward guidance, citing gas-supply uncertainty; management repeatedly declined to give FY27 volume, margin or utilisation numbers.
key_quotes: Our strong balance sheet and success in cost management enables us to manage any volatility which might be seen in the short-term.
As utilization levels continue to improve, the benefit of operating leverages are becoming increasingly visible in the business.
So as of now, we have passed on all the cost increase to the consumer.

rows.why: Q4 margin 7.7% vs ~6% in Q3 on ~20% price hikes, but Q1 FY27 still absorbs remaining gas cost rise (June Gujarat gas up ~INR5/SCM) and realisations may readjust down over 3-4 months as gas normalises.

rows.why: Utilisation at 60-65% with ample spare capacity; capex limited to maintenance of ~INR10 crore (+/-4-5) in FY27 versus INR6-7 crore in FY26.

rows.why: Management gave no numerical guidance and declined to forecast volumes, margins or utilisation citing gas uncertainty; said FY26 margins beat FY25.

rows.why: Adhesives in pilot-stage expansion in select North and East geographies with epoxy, grout and spatula added in last 2-3 months; management expects decent FY27 volumes but gave no figures, and anti-static/antimicrobial contribution is very small.

rows.why: Management expects realisations to readjust over about 3-4 months as gas costs normalise, after ~20% cumulative hikes in March-April 2026 (15-16% March, 5-6% April).

rows.why: Dealers are cutting stock to avoid high-priced inventory and large projects are in wait-and-watch mode after the ~20% price increase, which could slow near-term sell-in.
